As stated before in an earlier review, the plug does not sit right, it is too lose and falls right out. you need this!!! it saves on batteries and its so useful, just plug it into an extention cord and check otu the stars! This is a very nice and useful product if you own a celestron telescope it keep  you from using the batteries up I was using up batteries like it was my job when just using the telescope in my backyard. Now I just have to run an extension cord to it and not worry about a thing.

name: Home Audio Power Amplifier System - 2X40W Mini Dual Channel Mixer Sound Stereo Receiver Box w/ AUX, Mic Input - For Amplif...
reviewText: Using this as a remote amp and it works as advertised. No problems at all! Have it hooked to 6 speakers with reasonable sound. I ordered this to power up my old sony speakers that were lying around. This amplifier along with the sony speaker sounds awesonme. I also have a Bose soundwave. I like this better than bose. Bose has excellent bass, however it sounds a bit artificial with so much bass. This amplifier and speaker produces natural sound with a perfect balance of bass, treble and midrange. The amp was not as loud as I hoped it would be.  Connected to the audio out of my TV it needs to be cranked to 3/4 volume to be heard over the TV's internal speakers. I have it connected to a pair of Bose 161 speakers. And about half volume there is a noticeable hum during quiet moments. The unit itself also has a hum you can feel when touching it (vibration). I wanted a inexpensive Amp to power some outdoor speakers on our deck.  I am able to hook up our TV and stream Pandora through this device to drive the outdoor speakers.Not high quality sound, but neither are the speakers.  Does the job.  A remote might have been a nice option? Purchased this amplifier to drive a multi platform PC and gaming system, and it has worked flawlessly in that role for several years.  This is not the most powerful or feature filled amplifier on the market, but it will fill the void between computer speakers and a full blown 200 watt home entertainment system.  The controls are all manual so don't expect a lot of gadgetry.  This is a small footprint solution which can cross out the lower wattage PC and TV speakers and provide you with the power to push a system with enough punch to match any very powerful car stereo.  I use it with a Bose base cabinet and two satellite speakers, it provides me with three device selections (more if you use a TV selector box)  and its small enough to fit in a tight space on the desk or on a shelf.You can even use this amplifier as a small PA, fitting it under a podium and plugging it into a 1/4 in microphone cord and a one or a pair of speakers.

name: Celestron AstroMaster 130 EQ Motor Drive Telescope (Grey)
reviewText: Great telescope.  My previous telescope was the astromaster 114eq and this telescope, the 130eq is waaay better. the stars are so much clearer and planets look great. Definitely worth the extra 100 dollars for the inch larger aperture. First let me say that if you are looking at the 127EQ Powerseeker or the 130EQ Astromaster. BUY THE 130EQ!  The mount is 1000 fold better on this scope and the fact that it is a TRUE newtonian and not a bird-jones style scope like the 127EQ that "cheats" the optics capabilities by magnifying them makes it hands down better for clear viewing.I had the 127EQ and found out the hard way what a frustration it was trying to understand why I couldnt see things at all really with it.  It was defective and I switched it out for this one.Quality is at least 2X better on this than the 127EQ.  My son and I spied Jupiter the night it came in and were thrilled.Don't expect HUGE planets in the viewfinder (other than the moon) or super fine details.  That comes with a bigger monetary investment. Pros:* Once it's set up, it produces some nice imagery.  The views are relatively clear.* If you set up the red dot finder correctly (YouTube it), you can find pretty much any major star you could see easily with the naked eye.  Don't expect anything more, though.* Price -- If you're using this review to determine whether to purchase one, understand:  You get what you pay for.  The value you get with the imagery for this price range is hard to beat.  Period.  Please understand that before you read the cons.Cons:* The tripod is shaky.  I rate it a 3/10.  It's not stable at all, and even with shock absorbers on the feet, you basically have to use this scope hands-off or it's unusable.* EQ mount.  To be fair, it's a true EQ mount.  However, the engineering quality on the mount is poor.  If you want to aim it, you have to manually point it in the right direction.  To fine tune it, you can use the RA fine-adjustment knob, but the other knob only works with limited travel.  I haven't had a chance to study it and figure out where the bind is, but there's simply too much play to make it useful.  I rate it 2/10.*  The motor.  The motor's mounting location severely restricts how you can turn the scope.  Plus, when you have the motor on, you can't use the fine adjustment knob, rendering the ability to fine tune the sighting so the motor can do it's thing useless.Final thoughts:*  If you're not imaging, don't get this model.  Get the regular AstroMaster 130EQ.  It's a great scope, but the motor is not good on this mount / tripod setup.* If you ARE imaging, don't do like I did and get the camera adapter and think you can just go and take great pictures.  It's impossible for this stand/mount to balance a SLR.  The mount is too unstable / low quality to hand-hold.  Go with a lightweight camera -- either amscope or celstron, or get a webcam adapter.* You'll have to fine-tune the red-dot to use it.  It took me several sessions before I figured out how to set it properly, and even then, it was more luck than skill.*  To really get the most out of this scope, you'll need to buy some better optics.  I bought a Barlow 3x and love it.  Celestron has some accessory kits, so do some research.  If you're really worried about the $$ of upgrading the optics, I think you'd have a hard time buying a reflector scope out of the box that's any better without spending $500.  For this price range, it's a decent starter scope.  My wife and I like it. this is great for amatuer star gazers and anyone that has previous knowledge from other scopes. great view and even better price. i like it alot Finderscope is so terrible and unusable that the entire telescope can be used only by randomly looking around.  At least it was (relatively) cheap.  I suppose buying more eye pieces would make finding objects easier, but I didn't expect to have to do that right away in order for the product to be usable.

name: 2 PACK 2000mAh Battery for Canon BP-511A BP-511 BP511 [Camera]
reviewText: This is a great buy & they are working well for me.  Saved some money! I haven't had one give me any trouble! I bought these two replacement batteries for my wife's Canon 50D's battery grip (which I also reviewed on Amazon).  So far, it's been working great and holds a charge for a very long time.  I charged it once so far and it's been about a month with some shooting and it's still showing full.  Interesting, it's either lying or just a great battery.  I think it's the latter.  Anyway, for something like $6 per battery, it's a bargain.I would recommend this battery to anyone looking for some spares to keep handy. I have a old first generation DSLR canon 300D which is still working very well except the battery was dying.  Guess what, I purchased eforcity battery for this camera before from somewhere else. That was a huge disappointment. It just didn't charge at all. At the risk of being fooled twice, I order these batteries. They turned out to be a big surprise. I've been using the first one for a year. It holds the charge for a long time if I don't use the camera for a while. The volume allows me to shoot as many pictures I want to without warning of low battery. I haven't even tried to use the second one. It's a battery.  It works.  No space science there.I bought these to replace the original about 5-year old 1100mAh Canon BP-511 battery that started to show signs of age.  Old Canon's battery capacity decreased to the point where fully charged and with EF 100-400L IS lens fitted on camera, it wouldn't last till the end of my son's 30-minute soccer class.These new batteries seem to be able to power my camera and a battery thirsty lens for a very long time.  So, I'm happy.Mine were shipped by bargaincell.com.  As some reviewers already noticed, capacity is not printed on the batteries.  Which is strange and unusual.  I actually got batteries in two separate boxes (not one box with two batteries).  Each box had SKU CAMCAN001 printed on it.  Google search finds the page on the sellers web site that lists battery capacity as "only" 1600mAh.Whatever the true capacity of these batteries are, they are still a great deal, and I'm definitely going to keep mine (I read reviews that challenged if these are truly 2000mAh before buying, so I knew what I going into).  Unless you absolutely must have 2000mAh battery (currently selling for around $25), buy these and don't think twice.  $7.34 for two is an incredible price.  On the seller's own website, they sell single of these for $8.49!  So grab two-pack on Amazon for the price of single battery while they still offer this deal.The only complaint I have is that they do not come with plastic lid that protects contacts when battery is not in the camera.  Luckily, my camera bag has handy compartments for batteries, so I don't really need those plastic lids (and I have one plastic lid that came with Canon's battery too).The only reason for taking off two star is uncertainty what the true capacity of these batteries is.  It's a really bad move on the manufacturer's and seller's part (taking one star off for each).  Other than that, they work perfectly fine. What else is there to say?  I somehow received a pair of 2200mAh batteries rather than 2000mAh batteries.  They work fine, the voltage was good when I got them, and they seem to hold a charge just fine.EDIT 12/29/2012:  Both batteries died quick deaths.  One lasted about 3 months, the other made it around a year.  I'd forgotten to update this entry until I stumbled across it just now.

name: Lowepro Nova 180 AW Camera Bag (Black)
reviewText: good but not perfect. Great product! I Already had a Lowepro (top loader zoom), but with vertical grip my camera didn't fit anymore, at first the bag seems a little too compact, but actually works great.I have a Canon 60D with 18-135 lens attached, facing lens down in the bag. Vertical grip attached too. The charger in there, a sun cap and a bunch of small accessories. There is still room for the flash and two lenses that will come at some point.The two things I think are missing are a hard plastic bottom (it is probably fine, but doesn't make me entirely comfortable with my lens facing down), and even though there are plenty of inside dividers, I thing there are two sideway shapes missing, as well as Velcro on the side of a couple of the big ones. It took me a great deal of research to determine which camera bag would fulfill my needs.  I am a neophyte in the DSLR with a new camera for Christmas.  Prior to this I have been a point-and-shoot guy Nikon Coolpix 7900.  Got on the Lowepro website and used their bag suggestion search option.  Then back to Amazon armed with the information I needed.  The bag appears to be well made and I look forward to adding a few accessories to fill it up properly.  The padding seems sufficient and flexibility within the main compartment.  The water resistant cover and band across the back to fit on drag around suitcase are great extras. Bag doesn't look too big but you can fit a lot of gear in there. Holds crop sensor body, flash, two lenses and accessories like chargers for flash and body batteries, memory cards etc.Rain cover is nice but I never really used it so far.not sure if it will protect if it rains. I guess you need to carry plastic bag with you to be safe. I looked and researched so many camera bags for my Nikon D5100 before finally choosing this one.  I'm a newbie to SLR photography, so I haven't had a ton of experience with camera bags.  I am female though, so I've had a ton of experience shopping for handbags.  That sort of counts, right?A BAG TO GROW INTO: At any rate, I wanted my first bag to be fairly "comprehensive."  I wanted it to be big enough to fit my current gear (Nikon D5100 with the kit lens and Nikon 55-300mm f/4.5-5.6G ED VR AF-S DX) AND future gear (Nikon SB-700 AF Speedlight Flash and Nikon 35mm f/1.8G AF-S DX Lens.)  So I wanted a bag that would carry the camera, 3 lenses and a flash plus all the other accessories like spare batteries, etc.POUCHES!!: There are two memory card pouches on the interior of the lid as well as a larger zippered compartment where you could store flat things like lens caps.  There's also a front zippered pouch (bottom half) to stuff with other things like cleaning accessories, cables, etc.  The front of this pouch will feel "poofy," because that's where the All Weather Cover is stored - access that from another zipper along the bottom edge of the pouch. There is another front zippered compartment (top half on the flap) that would be suitable for less bulky items.  The pouches on each side are also made of a somewhat stretchier mesh material with some elastic banding along the top to keep things from falling out.  The zippered compartment on the back is really more suitable for papers or anything thin.  Overall most of these pouches don't really expand a whole lot, so don't really expect to be stuffing anything super bulky in them.  The side pouches will hold bottles of water though.ZIPPERS & TOP COVER: I also wanted a bag that was secured with zippers (YKK), so that nothing falls out.  I especially like how the top is designed with the flaps that hang over the top edge as well - kind of like how the top of a shoe box fits over the bottom half.  The design (along with the All Weather Cover) reduces the chances of water or debris entering the bag.  There is also a plastic buckle that secures each half of the bag.  Of course this does make it more time-consuming to get into the bag, but that was not a concern for me with this bag.  ***I do wish the top cover opened the opposite way - away from the body instead of toward.  That would make it slightly easier to access the interior while wearing the bag, although you can just wear it with the front facing towards you.QUALITY: The bag is sturdy nylon with strong stitching.  Its not double-stitched all around but at the key points of weakness (top handle, side clips for the shoulder strap, etc.)  The padding seems adequate.  The interior divider padding is about 1/4" thick and the exterior padding is about 1/2" thick.  The interior is also lined in a light grey that makes it easier to find things within the bag.  The Velcro has a strong "stick" and there's enough of it for greater flexibility in configuring it.  I wanted a quality bag, and I'm not disappointed.  ***I do wish that the bottom of the bag had the water-proof EVA base like the Case Logic SLR bags have for extra protection.COMFORT & CONVENIENCE: The bag is fairly boxy and bulky.  This is definitely not a small bag, and I thought it might be a bit uncomfortable to wear, but its actually pretty comfortable even when loaded due to the nice wide strap (1.5") and shoulder pad with the non-slip backing.  The shoulder strap extends up to 55" which gives about a 27.5" shoulder drop which is pretty substantial.  If you prefer the top handle, its thick and cushy with a comfortably soft fabric on the underside.  There's also a flap on the backside of the bag for sliding onto extended luggage handles for easier transport.  Sweet!OVERALL: I really love this bag.  Its got a few features that might not make it super-easily accessible, but I wanted more of a "tanky and secure" nylon bag which could carry most of my gear comfortably.  I didn't really buy this bag for "out-on-the-town-and-shooting" - I bought theLowepro Passport Sling Camera Bag-Micafor that.  This bag though is great for when you want to bring more of your arsenal with you and keep said arsenal protected.  I do really wish it had the EVA-clad base and the top flap opening away from the wearer, but we can always hope for the future.  Sorry for the mini-novel, but I hope this helps some prospective buyer out there.

name: Manfrotto 035RL Super Clamp with 2908 Standard Stud - Replaces 2900 - Black
reviewText: Manfrotto knows how to make a clamp.  A huge over-kill but you can trust whatever you mount on this won't go crashing to the floor.  I do wish they had made a double end 3/8 and 1/4 stud instead of just the 3/8.  Now I have to get an adapter.I'm using it to hold my iPad to a 12' light stand that I converted to a 12' high tripod for taking aerial shots over people's heads and to eliminate bushes and other obstacles that may get in my way.  It offers a unique perspective. This thing is the gold standard for super-stable photography clamps.  It will clamp down with enough force to crush walnuts without causing you to worry you're going to break it by applying too much force.  The v-shaped insert is an especially nice touch for clamping to boards/tables and the like.  I never go on a location shoot without one.The downsides:  It's rather heavy, it doesn't provide any articulation once clamped, and it's a bit on the pricy side (though totally worth it). Love it. name: Polk Audio OWM3 100 Watt 2.0 Channel On-Wall Speaker (Black)
reviewText: Nice set of rear speakers for surround sound system. Just as advertised. The sound quality, size and ability to mount on wall without any brackets is great. I bought a pair of these OWM3s to use as rear speakers for my 5.1 system.  They were recommended by a local supplier to go with my Polk OWM5 front speakers, and they work great together.  Aesthetically I would have preferred rear in-wall ceiling speakers but in white and the relatively smallish size, these OWN3s don't look bad. Amazon gave the best price for these speakers among the suppliers that I reviewed. I have a 7.1 sound system so I am using these speakers for the back channel. For that purpose they are excellent. I can't vouch for how they would sound as front speakers. They appear to be well made and have a nice heft to them. They are inexpensive but not cheaply made. I bought the white speakers and that color is actually ever-so-slightly off-white which I find attractive. It is not a brilliant white like a sheet of copy paper.I mounted these in the corner of the back and side wall. The mounting template is frustrating as it does not accurately give the distance from the corner to fastener location. Once you get the first hole in the right place you can place the second hole using the template. At least it does give the correct distance between the fasteners. I have never seen a speaker with so many options for mounting. If you have shelves at the right height, you can just attach the little weighted stands to the speakers an they stand up nicely.Note that one of the mounting positions shown in the Amazon photos requires a swivel stand that is not included.The instruction manual is nicely printed but all the different languages it supports are interspersed with the English making it very difficult and annoying to read through. The first half of the manual is taken up with warnings and cautions. I guess there is  always somebody who will find a way to cause damage with a tiny speaker like this but I'm pretty sure the world has gone crazy. I would prefer each language had its own section as I just feel like throwing this thing at the wall every time I try to learn about the product I bought. Read one sentence in English and the adjoining sentence is in French or Norwegian and so forth. I won't downgrade the score for this, since at least they did provide instructions. I bought (2) pair of these to act as surrounds and back surrounds for a 7.1 system in a room with very limmited options for proper mounting.  I found using Omnimount10 brackets did the trick.  Overall system is Polk Monitor70s up front, JBL sub, JBL front high Studio Series, a Polk Center, etc.  These OWM3s are inexpensive and sound as good as some costing twice as much.  For the price, these look and sound well above average. Great sound, great size. I use them for rear surround sound on the home theater system and they do the job well

name: Bushnell 10 x 42 Powerview Roof Prism Binocular
reviewText: Nice for the price but there is a little bit of haze on the edges. Nothing major though and they're great lens quality for a budget conscious purchase. I bought these for a trip to Cape Cod and Canada and have also used them for horse races at Churchill and they worked perfectly. Great purchase! Great price, good quality binoculars, plus warranty.I think that pretty much sums these up.  They don't fog up too much and don't have the best quality lenses in low light conditions (break of dawn hunting and twilight hunting).  But for the average user these are just fine, because you're not spending $200+ on some binoculars you're barely going to use anyway! These were purchased as a gift.  I have a set of 10 X 42 Bushnells that are a step up from these and they are far superior in image quality and clarity.  This Powerviews are average at best.  Recommend spending the extra $ on something a little nicer. i am surrounded by friends who are lusting after $2500 10 X 42 swaro binos.  these are $60 10 X 42.  i will admit, they are a bit heavy, but for a $2440 savings, i can live with a bit heavy.  i have plenty of experience with bushnell products and i have never been let down by their product.  granted, the pricier models have caught my eye, and given the opportunity and financial freedom, i would probably choose the more expensive, waterproof model.  but at my present situation and need, these will do the job for and probably last long enough for my kids to slog through the rain, snow and dirty campsites with them.update:  i noticed when i got to the wide-open pine tree forests while elk hunting that these have the distorted halo around the edges, denoting inferior lens grinding quality.  my $120 bushnell binos smoked these ones in a side by side comparison.  but if you only have $60 to spend, they will do what you need them too.  you can also thread the top lens caps onto the strap.  since the bottoms are permanently attached, these make a good pair to hang around your neck while you are slinging mud on the wheeler or walking through a nasty snow/rainstorm. I bought these for my 10 year old son.  I spent way too long researching binoculars, but after a while these seemed the best value for the price (as I did not want to spend too much, in that he might break them early on).  When I received them I was a little surprised at how heavy and large they were.  For some reason I had the misconception that they were going to be compact, but they should be fine with the strap and case.

name: Nikon Af-S Dx 18-105Mm G Vr Zoom Lens for DSLR Camera - Black
reviewText: Bought it as part of d7000 kit. I don't know if I got a defective unit, but images were blurry, outdoors, inside, nature, portrait..basically under all conditions.  I used a prime lens with the d7000 which worked GREAT. However I had to return the whole kit. All I would like to say is....- The plastic mount broke off after a year of use.- And this is normal use with good care.- Optically - pretty OK - for this price. Pls refer the other reviews for the tech details - I found them useful.-Bottom Line is - If the plastic mount decides to detach itself from the lens after a year of normal use...whatever the other specs...... NOT recommended... I tend to side with Ken Rockwell over Thom Hogan in this lens review. My personal opinion is Thom is being a little lenient on this lens.In one line, I'd say it's a very convenient lens as far as the focal length goes, but the lens quality is quite poor - both in image quality and build quality.I know build quality isn't important to many people, but this lens is actually quite bad - I was always afraid this lens would snap off one day - the plastic mount seems really flimsy. I've been very careful over 18 months and haven't damaged it.I shoot with a D5100, I purchased a light body for travel, and own 3 other lenses - one 35mm f/1.8 prime, one 55-200 zoom and an ultra-wide. This is the second-most expensive lens in my kit, yet the weakest. After 18 months, I realized that I was avoiding the lens whenever I didn't need the convenience. It is disappointingly weak at 18mm f/3.5 and the output looks comparable to a high-end P&S; camera. It is pretty soft at all focal lengths, and has significant distortion. I also have a feeling that colors look a little washed out on this lens.Taking a gamble, I put in an extra 200$ and tried the Sigma 17-50 f/2.8. I was surprised at how good the Sigma is. I've dropped the lens out of the kit and am looking to sell it now. Eventually, I am noticing that the prime lens is having reduced usage because the Sigma is doing some of it's work. I don't think I would be too unfair in saying one could replace the prime + the 18-105 with the Sigma 17-50. I recently traded the 18-55mm VR lens from my D60 kit for this lens. I wanted something with more range than the 18-55 offered, and with VR, so it was a choice between the 18-200mm VR and this lens. Between the price of the latter, and the reports of worse distortion, zoom creep, and poor feel of the zoom & focus rings of the 18-200, I decided this was the best choice. The fact that this lens is a tad shorter and a good bit lighter (420g vs. 560g) make it an even better choice for a walkaround (or even only) lens for normal use.The fit & finish is much better than that of the kit lens, and while it is a bit heavier than the 18-55, it's not appreciably longer, if any. I'm not a good enough photographer to tell you how it compares on distortion to either the 18-55 or the 18-200, so I won't even try. But it produced a number of wonderful images for me today, under low light and handheld, without noticeable distortion, and they were very clear except if I was shaking badly (this is with shutter speeds of 1/40-1/10). I purchased it for $300 new, about half of the price of the 18-200mm VR. In all, I am quite satisfied with this lens as an all-around, do-everything lens.Update: Well, this lens lasted me about a year. No, it didn't break, I just upgraded to the 16-85mm VR and passed it on to a family member just getting into digital SLRs.So for an extra ~$450, the 16-85mm VR adds:-VRII instead of original VR, and the Active-Normal switch that comes with this. Nikon claims 4 stops for VRII, instead of 3 stops. I didn't test them side by side, but I do notice both the new lens and my 70-300mm VR (which also has VRII) are less prone to shake than the 18-105mm was. Not sure if I'd claim a full stop better, but there is some improvement.-An extra 2mm on the wide end, and better image quality, at the cost of 20mm on the telephoto end. I honestly don't miss the 30mm on the long end, and I can switch to the telephoto lens easily enough. Honestly though, I don't find myself racked out at 85mm and wanting just a little more focal length much at all. The 2mm on the wide end is kind of a toss-up. It's nice to have, and actually noticeable compared to 18mm. But it won't replace a dedicated wide-angle if you like wide-angle shots, just add 2mm more overlap than you already get. Kind of makes you feel goofy buying a $1k wide-angle for only 4-6mm less focal length.-A metal mount, a distance scale, and overall better construction. The metal lens mount and distance scale are no-brainers, even though I hardly NEED the distance scale. But both that and the metal mount could've easily been added to the 18-105mm for negligible cost, especially considering the $400+ MSRP. It's kind of disappointing that Nikon skimped on a little plastic window and a little chunk of metal, even for a kit lens, to save maybe $10. The zoom and focus ring action of the 16-85mm VR is much more fluid-feeling than the plasticy feel of the 18-105mm VR, but it also weighs a good bit more. Not heavy in a bad way however, it just feels more solid.Honestly, while I don't regret buying the 16-85mm VR, I'm not sure if it's really worth the extra cost (compared to the normal ~$300 cost of an 18-105mm VR, not retail, which would be silly for a common kit lens). I upgraded for the image quality, and because it felt weird to have the most-used lens in my kit be the lowest quality (image and construction). If you can live with the plastic mount, slight distortion and softness, and cheaper feel, the 18-105mm is still a great value for the money. This lens and the 70-300mm VR still match or best the 18-200mm VR lens, at about the same overall cost, with more versatility. I have a :Nikon D40X Whooo! " D40X" I love it. I get great picturesout of it. I have a Nikon D90 and a Nikon D7000...I wish I loved my 7000 as much as I do my old out dated "D40X". I know it must be user error. Most people who have the D7000 love it. My wife loves hers.I have the Nikon 18-105 DX VR and I don't care what anyone else says about this lens, I love it. For me it  is one of my best Nikon lens. I have never had any trouble with the mount and I do change my lens many times during a photo shoot between "landscape" and "wildlife" ( I live in Alaska !), ...BUT I do take real good care of my stuff.I have compared the 18-105mm DX VR  with the Nikon 18-55mm DX VR. They both will take good pictures. I get a little sharper picture in certain lighting with the 18-105mm  . I also have the Nikon 35mm DX It is a good, sharp, cheep, prime lens.Everyone should have one...or the 50mm.Everything depends on so many variables in photography. The user...the lighting...the subject.All of my  shooting is outdoors..."wildlife" with a Nikon 70-300mm DV VR I get better pictures using the 70-300mm on my Nikon D40X ...crazy I know.

name: AKG 2458X00190 Headphones (Black)
reviewText: MADE IN AUSTRIA. Granted this pair of headphones is not suited to all music genres coming across as thin and neutral for heavy metal or most loud bass heavy music, however it comes to a class of its own  when most of one's repertoire is Jazz Vocals and Accoustic instrumentals (Guitar, Flute, Cello).  And yes, it does not tolerate or flatter poor recording, rather focussing itself on the most accurate and neutral reproduction of good quality audiophile recordings.  Much have been said about its neutrality but with these there is no hearing fatigue and allows one to remain sublimely teleported into audio heaven for hours.I find myself gravitating back to this pair for almost all of my repertoire.  The soundstage is outstanding. And distortion - nil. Extremely comfortable to wear. Lightweight . Wire frames allow easy hanging-up after use.  Comes with both sizes of quality gold-plated jacks.I have recently readded the use of the fiiO E7 DAC (an experiment) to it and found that it does subtly smoothen out the edges (which I didn't realise existed) and round off the higher registers which was just discernible.  As for the bass, I've found setting EQ to +1 helps deepen the bass and give it a rather pleasing signature for more bass involved music like Black Eye Peas, U2, BonJovi etc.Highly recommended with (above) caveats but not everyone will like it. The Ultimate Gentleman of Headphones esq. Not pushy. Quietly dignified and delivers big within its domain.Also ownAKG 271MKII (studio recording pair)Senheisser 598 (all rounder with some bloat) Just love AKG. K702 is sooooo good with classical. It is a lot better than my old Bose NC15. But they function differently in my life. I need time to warm it up to its perfection. I will write more reviews when I use over 3 month. Then the comments will be reasonable. Comfort was the main reason why I bought this set of cans. A long time ago (2001) I got  a pair of Sony MDR-605 (discontinued) and were very comfortable for wearing them for hrs without feeling the usual pressure pain given by the pads of a smaller headphones like the (Fanny Wang FW-HEADPH-1001) which sound great using an android smart phone or perhaps an iPod; but, after a 3 or four hrs had to take a half hr break to let my ear's blood circulate to get rid of the discomfort from the pressure between my ears and the pads. The K-702s have big round foam pads covered with some velour cloth and fit fine around my ears (big) and put the contact of the pads on my skull but they are not pressured by the spring action of the arc over your head like the Fanny Wang's, this headphones rest their weight on top of your head by a padded (bumpy) arch which is not super soft but not uncomfortable either. Unfortunately because of this comfort feature if you nod/shake you head left and right you will feel the headphone's pads move along so they are not stable if you plan on doing sports where your head will do a lot of shaking and those pads will definitely get soaked with sweat. I use them only indoors and mostly sitting down at a computer and they are very comfortable for hrs. They do require good juice to appreciate the power of the drivers and something with a tiny amp such as a portable device (droid phone) will not suffice to do this.  As stated in other reviews they require a long break-in period and needless to say they sound great. I gave the K702 model an "average" rating based strictly on concern about their not being manufactured in Austria any longer, and my strong distrust (through sad experience) of the long-term reliability of anything made in the Peoples Republic of China (P.R.C.). (Here's a 2012 example of P.R.C. assembly quality of an AKG K242hd headphone: youtube.com/watch?v=Z_fGEK9rokw. Who knows what the interior may look like). The country of manufacture/long-term reliability is my only concern with the K702.If that's not a concern for you, then ignore my opening paragraph and read on. My "Made in Austria" K701s are outstanding (5 stars all the way), and the K702 has virtually identical technical specifications as the K701s.I am generally comforted to know that a product was produced in a factory with a history and tradition of producing that product well. Preferring to trust AKG's traditional reputation for excellent engineering *and* manufacturing, I purchased the more costly "Made in Austria" K701s, and the K701s I received in January 2014 (sold by Audio Plaza/fulfilled by Amazon) were still made in Austria (printed on the box and on the side of the headphones). However, In March 2014 AKG informed me that *all* AKG headphones are now being designed in Austria and assembled in the P.R.C. The AKG "Professional Headphones" web page identifies only the K712 and K812 as still "Made in Austria". So while Amazon is still selling them, it appears the AKG K701s "Made in Austria" will gradually disappear as the remaining stock gets depleted.Being a retired sound engineer/recording studio owner, I've been accustomed to high quality professional mixing/mastering headphones that have a flat frequency response across the audio spectrum and reproduce music accurately and without coloring any portion of the audio spectrum. This lead me to the AKG K701 and AKG K702 headphones.The K701/K702 is aimed not at the iPod generation but at AKG's studio market (found on AKG's "Professional Audio Solutions" web site, "The K702's are reference, open, over-ear studio headphones for precision listening, mixing and mastering."). The K701/K702, being flat and neutral analytical reference headphones (i.e. 30Hz-10kHz +/- 3dB), only reproduce the content of the source, for better or worse. If you have the K701/702 cans powered adequately and the music source you are listening to using AKG K701/K702 cans sounds to you to be strident or muddy, or has a thin bass, or whatever, it's the musical source, not AKG K701/K702 headphones; being neutral and flat, they can only reproduce the true content of the source music. That is the purpose of studio analytic/reference grade headphones. Non-linear headphones are useless for the accurate monitoring/mixing/mastering necessary to create the highest quality artistic decisions about the musical performance. If in doubt as to the intended purpose and audio quality of the AKG K701/K702 headphones, independent reviews at audiophile sites such as KenRockwell, innerfidelity, headphone, and audiophile magazine will affirm the numerous 4 and 5 star ratings for the audio performance of the K701/702 found on Amazon.Here's the only other caveat: If your only exposure to music has been the hypercompressed,loud, bass-heavy thumping of FM radio and such, and you like that, then you probably won't be happy at all with these exquisite headphones. So if analytical/uncolored listening is not your goal, then these headphones aren't for you. Seek out a non-linear product that will give you a rewarding listening experience.Here's some general audio related background information others have found informative/useful."Break-in" PeriodThe jury is out on this. The only formal study of which I'm aware was inconclusive and can be found on the innerfidelity web site by searching on "On the Measurement and Audibility of Headphone Break-in".I don't know of any professional audio people who give "burn-in" any credence. The subjective perception of "burn-in" is, in my opinion, the user's hearing being re-trained and adjusted to the frequency response curve of the headphone. Thus a listener coming from a headphone whose response curve boosts the lows and dips the mids (as most consumer cans do) will hear a headphone with a flat and neutral response curve (like the AKG 701/702) as having a shallow bass and a strident upper mid range. As the listener's hearing adapts over time to the uncolored accuracy of the neutral/flat headphones, the headphones miraculously "improve" after having been "burned-in", when in fact it's the listener's hearing being "burned-in" by the headphones.Headphone Impedance:Headphones with lower impedance ratings offer higher volumes at the same level of input, but they need heavier drivers to compensate for the low impedance or risk sounding muddy and distorted. The lower mass of the drivers of a higher-impedance headphone can deliver unparalleled clarity and response, but it takes more power to achieve the same loudness.How We Hear - Consumer Headphones v. Analytical/Reference Headphones:At low listening levels the human ear is most sensitive to the mid range (200Hz -2kHz), gradually losing sensitivity below and above those points. If you picture the ear's frequency reception at low levels it would look roughly like a frown. At higher listening levels, the lows and highs become more pronounced and less out of balance with the mid-range.The frequency response of consumer grade headphones typically looks like a smile. At higher listening levels the result is unnatural sound (lows and highs artificially boosted by the headphone's particular design). This makes most consumer grade headphones unsuitable for critical/analytical listening because the amount of boost incorporated by the individual manufacturers can be difficult to assess. Most, if not all, boost the low end significantly (+5dB or more), dip the upper mids by -5dB or more, and sometimes also boost the high frequencies. A few start rolling off the upper mids and just keep going downhill. In very broad terms, consumer grade headphones intentionally alter the audio spectrum in the low, mid, and high frequencies. Also, if headphones are underpowered, you won't hear the low and high ends accurately because of the human ear/low volume factor. Underpowered headphones don't get enough power from the source to allow the ear to hear the lows and highs at a level comparable to the midrange.From a performer/producer/sound engineer's perspective (AKG's target market for the K701/K702), it is the non-linear consumer grade headphones that are lacking. Non-linear headphones are only used by the pros to listen to (not create) the rough mix so they can judge what the typical consumer might hear v. the artistic goal for which the musicians and producer are striving, so that they can tweak the mix without seriously compromising the artistic goal.A sound engineer's job is to faithfully capture the sound of the music produced by the musicians. The ONLY way to do that is to monitor using amplification, speakers and/or headphones that are neutral (i.e. have a flat frequency response) over the entire audio spectrum (we'll ignore physical sound treatment of the control room for the moment). I have never met a professional who wanted to produce a mix geared to the lowest common denominator, nor geared to sound good only on the highest end audio equipment. Recording studios spend hundreds of thousands of dollars to achieve the highest degree of audio accuracy so musicians, producers, and sound engineers can make informed decisions about the mix. If the goal is a bass-heavy musical product, the flat, neutral, uncolored monitor speakers/headphones will tell the producer when the mix achieves that goal.The working mix is also played over typical consumer equipment, in car stereo systems, MP3 devices, etc. to see if it flys on what the average consumer will be using. Those with high-end and esoteric stereo systems will derive the full benefit of the musicians', producer's and sound engineer's artistic efforts. Those without will still get an enjoyable product. Studio grade analytic/reference headphones provide that flat frequency response required for artistic accuracy. I was looking for a little more bass in these phones but the clean accuracy is what counts here. My Sennheisers gave up after decades of use. Bought these because I had AKGs way back in the 60s.

The bass is really thumping even when at lower registers. Treble I don't mess with too much so it either doesn't do much or I just don't notice. I use these with headphones a lot and although the sound is nice with them sometimes I wish it could be cranked just a little louder.Great but falls a little short of exceptional. For the price of $70 bucks though I think they are convenient and worth it. Toodles!4.3 stars. I wanted 2.0 speakers for travel. I am dissappointed with the sound quality and volume. I do not know if it is possible to make a speaker with better sound in a compact case. Perhaps they would sound better with a larger speaker in a square case with less depth.I would not buy these for home use. I have heard the "Logitech Z-2300 THX-Certified 200-Watt 2.1 Speaker System" which would be excellent for home use. I was looking for replacement computer speakers after my Harman-Kardon speakers died. I was pleasantly surprised by these new speakers that output decent audio quality for their size. I use this with an USB to analog stereo converter (that is kept plugged on a USB hub). They work really great! I bought this as a gift for my wife, we were really surprised at the great sound these speakers produced for their size...for the money they are hard to beat. These speakers seem to be really well made and have very high quality knobs, but creative has put too much effort into making low and high quantity far greater than quality. The treble quality is quite poor, it's screechy and doesn't seem to be smooth throughout the 8khz to 12khz range, there are peaks at different parts of the spectrum. The bass, similarly, is too boomy and quite uncontrolled. The midrange, contrary to what others have said, I find to be quite adequate and cannot find any real fault with it. However, these are overall pretty disappointing speakers for the price, but I don't know why I was expecting stereophillic quality with Creative. Going to try the JBL duet III now.

name: Nikon Af-S Dx Nikkor 35 Mm F/1.8G Prime Lens for Digital SLR Camera (Black)

name: AmazonBasics HAMA299068 RJ45 Cat-5e Ethernet Patch/LAN Cable for Router (14 Feet/4.26 Meters, White)
reviewText: Works as expected and the shipping speed was right on time. A bit over priced in my opinion, but what cables aren't nowadays.My reviews are kept up to date if/when the product malfunctions, breaks, or functions less than reasonable expectations hold overtime. This cable does what it's supposed to do but it feels like a very low-quality cable and is very rigid. The first one arrived and did not work Amazon replaced it for free and without running me ragged to return it. This is basic, simple, and well made.I trust buying it from Amazon because I know it won't be cheaply made. There are cheaper cords out there being sold by different marketplace sellers. I've ordered some that are very cheap in price but then they have malfunctions soon after installation, they send the wrong item, they send a generic brand with fake stamps on them of better brands, or it takes 2 weeks to receive it from overseas.I bought this to connect directly to my modem for installing a new router. Easy to put in or out of modem/router but also secure fit that stays in. Plus, it's always nice to have an extra Ethernet cord because you never know when the need for one will arise. Storing in the box it came in.My internet is so important and vital in my business. You don't have to buy the most expensive product to get the best quality. I don't think you can go wrong with this cable so I recommend it. I bought this cable to put together a quick network connection between my router and a computer in another room. I ended up running it beneath the floor and through the walls on both ends. I find this cable to be of exceptional quality and the connector ends feature a neat snagless design. A few years back, I paid around $10 for a 7ft Staples brand CAT5e cable. Amazon's cable both exceeds the quality and value of this older cable I have. The only possible problem I could find with it is that the plastic protector for the clip end bumps up against both my router and computer's connection too much. I have no need to plug and unplug it all of the time so this does not matter to me that much. I would hazard a guess that this cable is still better than cheaper generic brands out there. I have a gigabit NIC (onboard Asus P7P55D) connected to a Gigabit router (Netgear WNR3500L running tomato) and this cable only allows for a 100Mbit connection. I'll be RMAing it with Amazon to see if a new one resolves this issue. Otherwise...good price if you have Prime.Edit: Amazon sent a new cable and it now connects at 1000Mbit.

name: ASA HS-1 Aviation Headset
reviewText: I have a Bose A20 headset with bluetooth and I absolutely love it. However, when shopping for a headset for my passengers, I wasn't exactly thrilled with the thought of buying another $1k headset.This fits the bill perfectly. This headset is very durable, looks nice, and sounds excellent. Although I really enjoy the noise canceling capability of my Bose A20, I would have no problem using this headset instead.The headset has the a mono/stereo switch on the junction box. If you're only getting sound in one side, try moving the switch; that should fix you up.The headset that was shipped to me does have the flexible mic boom. That is a very nice feature. The boom is a bit larger than the one on my Bose A20; I'm not sure if that is a feature or a detriment at this point, though.This headset doesn't include a case but, for this price, who could complain? I bought the ASA Single Headset Bag from Amazon for very little money and it works perfectly.If you're looking for an extra headset or even just a beginner headset, you can't go wrong. But, once you start flying, check out the Bose A20 or another higher end headset....you'll thank yourself for the investment. Purchased 3 of these as passenger headsets. The build quality is better than expected. Not the same as my DCs or Lightspeed, but also 1/3 the price! I like that the headband protector is leather- should help prevent window scratches when pax fall asleep :) For the price, this is a great item. Sure, it doesn't have all the noise-cancelling features of the really expensive models, but the chatter is clean and there actually isn't much bleed-through of outside noise (can't escape the engine noise entirely since in a one-seven-two you're pretty much sitting on the thing), but it does a fair job. Everyone wants David Clark headsets...  I had one pair when I first started flying 14 years ago.  Dad gave them to me as a present when I first became a student pilot.  I loved them and they worked forever.  The finally died so I pick up these cause I was not going to pay that price, LOL.....  For this price, super great headsets.  Great sound and volume control, mic works well, and very comfortable.  Only thing is keep checking the knobs on each side to make sure the stay tight.  Besides that, they are awesome.... I currently own the HS-1A headset with the flexible boom MIC (as pictured). The product pictured here is the HS-1A not the HS-1. both have excellent reviews and are great products however until amazon makes it clear which one you'll be buying i would advise caution.

name: Celestron Speciality Series Travel Scope 70 Telescope
reviewText: Great product, I have had many wonderful hours with it it works great This is a fine scope, I had an issue with looking through the scope without the direct angel, but overall this is a good scope.  I own an 8in Reflector and a 6in Reflector, this is not a great scope for looking at the planets and Deep Sky Objects, but looking at the Moon and Star Clusters this scope is great.  I live in a city and Ive had issues looking at Saturn, but with my larger scopes I can see it fine.  Other reviews say they can see the planets fine, so I think I just havent gotten it aligned just right.  To anyone telling you not to buy this scope and to save your money, DO NOT LISTEN TO THEM!  If you know you like looking at the stars, go ahead and grab a better scope, but if your not sold on the idea start here and work your way up.  Besides this scope is so light.  My 8in weights over 60lbs when setup and its really large and hard to carry around.  I love that scope, but for quick observing or for camping trips when I want to pack light this scope is great and easy to use. This is a great scope and I use it for target practice, star gazing, and general snooping from balconies while on vacation. The tripod is flimsy as others report. The case is nice but I would have liked a little more magnification. Its hard to make out target shots at 300 yards. Less than that works fine. The tracking scope, or what ever its called, that goes on the side is pretty much useless. A star program comes with it and I really enjoy using it to see what stars are in the sky at my location on a given night. Over all , a pretty good scope, not great, but price is right. The telescope itself is ok, though at higher magnifications focusing becomes something of a chore, and there is a hue when looking at stars. The biggest problem is the tripod, as it's way too unstable. This is the perfect gift for a seven year old budding star gazer.  If the child is happy, I'm happy.

name: Celestron Speciality Series FirstScope Telescope
reviewText: First of all I've just started amature astronomy this year so I've never owned a telescope, I've been using a 15x70 celestron binocular on a tripod. I've had the Celestron Firstscope for a couple of weeks now and I've been please with it..considering how much I paid for it (big bang for the buck). Anyway, I know a lot of people suggest not to buy the accessory but one thing I learn when I attended a star party prior to buying this telescope is Finder Scope is very useful/important when trying to align your scope with a certain object. So I did buy the accessory, and I'm glad I did. Although it's true that using the finder scope is hard to use if you have the telescope on top of a table or the ground, so what I did is I look around my house that is tall enough that I can put it on top and I found an old cd rack in the garage that is about 5 feet tall. It was very sturdy and made using the telescope so easy with the finder scope.With the eyepiece that came with the telescope and accessory everyone who said that they are useless...they are correct, those type of eyepiece are really hard to look into and may disappoint you. So what I did is I baught a 2x Barlow and a 25mm plossl eyepeice from Orion and the diffrence are night and day, with the eyepiece I purchase it made field of view much clear, crisp and I saw more stars. So far I've been out observing and star gazing as much as I could and as much as the weather permits. The moon through this telescope with the 25mm and 2x barlow eypiece looks awesome the craters are very clear, mars look like a tiny orange dot and saturn...so far same as mars look like a dot maybe with a medium or higher power eyepiece I might be able to see saturns ring. Overall great buy specially for a starter like me, I will probably use this until I'm ready to move to the next level at least now I can save up to a much powerful and expensive telescope. This is called a first scope and it was my first scope. It was very easy for a newbie to use. The swivel is surprisingly stable. The scope is well built and has a hard plastic coating to it. I was looking at the moon in no time and admiring the details. I think this is the best scope in its price range. Be warned though....this scope can ignite an interest in a very expensive hobby and you'll be wanting a much larger and pricey scope in no time after seeing what this can do! :) - price was very affordable, got it for the kids- appears to be well made and is working just fine, it should last some time- yes i would reccomend this for for a starter telescope I have many high end telescopes. I also bought a Orion 100mm Sky Scanner for my son and won this Celestron scope at an astronomy event. Both are OK but the Orion is a much better product and worth the extra money....bigger aperture, better eyepieces, red dot finder on the Orion is worth as much as this entire scope. I am a big Celestron fan having 5 different models but this is really the very bottom level. It is easy to use, but its lower quality and limitations will soon tell you that you should have paid a bit more money. this unit is simple to set up, on top of table or deck rail if wide enough, small kids can look at some starts, great for first time telescope, not for advance fans.Worth the money before buying a bigger telescope, incase my kids lost interest.He can also use it to see birds or other items across the back yard but needs to position on a low table or floor.

name: BIC AMERICA Wired 500 Watts Acoustech PL-28II Center Speaker - Black
reviewText: Received mine today. First off let be say I have the Klipsch Reference Series RP - 5 Towers each with a built in 12 inch side firing sub, RS 3 Surrounds,  two BIC bookshelf speakers for rear and a BIC 475 Watt 12 inch Sub. I replaced a Klipsch Icon Center with this beaut. I also own  pair of  Klipsch RF- 5 Towers that I use now with my IMac and a Yamaha sub.Later for that. This center lives up to all the great reviews it has gotten. Yes, horns require some break in and yes this one sounds a little harsh out the box, but it makes for it in volume. I put in We Were Soldiers and my son, my best friend and gave it a critical listen. I have a 120 Watt Harmon Kardon AVR that sweetens most speakers.Let me tell you this babe held its own with the towers and sub. While the bombs and bullets were flying and when things went boom, the dialogue was crystal clear and loud enough not to be drowned out. That's quite a feat being that with the Icon the voices always sounded a little muddled.This is a $500 sounding CC for under $200. Why wait? Klipsch better be careful. I got this speaker in two days after I ordered, it was packaged just right, double boxed. The PL-28II center speaker, I'm using the FH-65B for front left and right because I don't have room for tower speakers and PL-66 for surround.My set up is powered by my TX-NR 818 and I have plenty of power to drive everything.I just ran audyssey x32 speaker configuration,Audyssey set the fronts FH-65B speakers at 40Hz my center PL-28II is set at 90Hz , surrounds PL-66 are at 120Hz and wides DV62si at 70Hz highs are Micca in wall speakers that are high above front left and right are almost to the ceiling. They are at 40Hz and the back speakers in the ceiling behind me set at 120Hz and of cource the subs are 120Hz .Going to leave it like this for a week or so and then run audessy x32 again and see what it settles to after a so called break in.The speaker sounds great.I have my TX-NR 818 in listening Mode DTS Neo:X I go back and forth between that and Audyssey DSX. I've been reading about reference level they say to listen at 0db but it much too loud -15 seems to be more or should I say loud enough.UpdateTX-NRI just moved the speakers around I moved the FH-65s to the wides the PL-66s to front mains and using the DV62si as surrounds and of course the PL-28II AS THE CENTER.  The PL-66s match beautifully with the PL-28II and the from three speakers are very amazing, and the sound is incredibly great. My Speaker configuration came in after running audyssey front 100Hz center 90Hz surround 70Hz wide 40Hz high 40Hz surround back 120Hz. So there you have it I'm going to give this a try for a week and run audyssey once again and see what I come up with after a good break in..... waiting for it to break in, still has a little of that tin can sound but ive only had it about 2 weeks,  i'll update my review if it doesn't get better I have never owned a center channel this massive before.  This thing is huge, it's like a boombox!!!  It kinda works that way too.  I like how the horn tweeter is extremely clear.All the dialogue in movies that I would have to strain to hear or rewind, is now front and center.  I listen to a lot of R&B; and Rap music and with those genres, the treble and high-mids can sometimes get lost with all the low-mids and bass.  This speaker lets the lyrics come to life in drum heavy music!I love this speaker and prob would have paid $100 more for it.  At $199, I'm not sure it can be beat.System:Receiver -Onkyo TX-NR5009 9.2-Channel Network A/V Receiver (Black)Center - PL-28Front -Polk Audio Monitor 70 AM7025-B 3-Way Floorstanding Speaker (Single, Black)x2Rear & Side -BIC Acoustech PL-66 Surround Speakers (Pair)x2Subwoofers - MBM-12 MK2 Mid-Bass Module,BIC PL-200 Acoustech Platinum Series Subwoofer, &BIC America F12 12-Inch 475-Watt Front Firing Powered SubwooferPROS:1 - Price2 - Clarity3 - AppearanceCONS:1 - Size (not really a con, but definitely make sure you pay attention to the dimensions.  It is HUGE.) I am running FH6-LCR's as L and Right, and Bic venturi as wide's (the bookshelf ones), and the smaller 3" driver Venturi as rears......back to this center...When I first unplugged the FH6 center and plugged this in I wasnt inpressed, it wasnt better, then I re-ran Auddsey calibration on my Onkyno 809 and BAM!!It is "throaty" and full of volume and thickness.  The mid-bass is great and it is so efficient my receiver had to set it at -9.5db (versus +1) on the FH6.  I adjusted it to -3.0 and its just what I want to hear.When someone said "sounds like the people are in the room with you" that is true, you can hear people breathing, clicking, everything.  It sounds like this speaker has its own amplifier but do not confuse that with loudness or sound pressure.What it really sounds like is when you take a good microphone and plug it into a PA amp and talk, that's what it sounds like right in your face.Will update once I watch planet of the Apes this weekend and Lord of the rings 2.  Only watched 1h of Underworld last night.  Very impressive.  Very.  Makes you "want" to even listen to the dialog "down time" scenes of movies when there are not explosions or gun fire.  The big difference between this and other Bic but non-Acoustech speakers is this sounds great with music also.I have installed 6 of the BIC 8" inwall speakers (Acoustech, L,R, surrround and 2 in his bar for 2 chan audio) in my uncle's basement and love the bass and sound.  Terminator salvation blew the grill off the front, which prompt me to finally pull the trigger on this center.My theater area is about 40' wide by 20' from projection screen to sofa. Also this would sound great mounted on the wall behind a screen about 3' off the ground.  My screen is 106" but not the kind that lets audio pass thru'***Note  Its impossible to screw these terminals with your fingers so I used 2 banana plugs to connect the speaker wire**Because this speaker has the highest sensitivity in my set up at about 96-98db its best if you are going to manually do any adjusting to do it just under refrence level (ref. level is when the volume reads "0" on absolute recievers or 82 on onkyno recievers when its set to count from 1-100).  For instance it is nice and full at 63 but at 72 it overpowers my entire system, wont even think about 82 (ref level) with this beast.  I dont want to but I know I'm going to end up getting a pair of PL-89's to go with this and probably moving my bed into the basement and living in my theater room.  haha.

name: BIC AMERICA PL-89II Wired Acoustech Platinum Series Tower Speaker (Pair, Black)
reviewText: These things kick butt and the price is very right. They blew my mind from day one and I love them more and more every time I want to be blown away.BIC has got a fan in me. I own 2-F-12 subs and together with the pair of PL-89 II,s made me truly enjoy my system! Thanks BIC AMERICA!!  UPDATE!! OCT 27th... Yeah the reviews are accurate as I read and experienced for myself they have broken in and they are truly excellent speakers! I had to lower my subs because the bass became too much as they got even better!! SOO.. I,m very happy and I recommend them to all who want fabulous sound and some cash to spare! I have had the same PSB tower speakers for 19 years and I thought it was time for a upgrade. I had surched the net for top rated speakers and fond the PL-89's came in 2nd from 2013 behind the WAY overpriced B&W; , so I checked into these and decided tp give them a shot.WOW am I glad i did, My Denon HT system has NEVER sounded this good for blu ray and CD's. The audio from Blu Rays are amazing. Now I consider my 90's PSB Century 1000i  to be great speakers but the Bic PL-89II blow them out of the water in terms of sound qty.I paid $528.00 for the pair and they easily could charge and be worth $500 EACHIf you are looking for new Speakers defiantly give the PL-89II a shot. I love these speakers...they are easily worth more than the selling price, especially compared to other brands like Klipsch.  Great sound, nice build, and looks great. Not being a audifile myself, but needed a speaker set up I was going to go the route as most none audifiles and buy a Bose system not knowing any better. Thank goodness I didn't waste my money. Several months ago my old roommate had bought a Bose system and thought they were great. Great volume but after going to my buddies house with his set up i discovered there was more to just volume but depth and feel of audio. Now this set up that i made isnt the top of the line or anything but works very well for my set up and size of room i am dealing with.Soon as I unboxed them they look great. Way larger than I had thought they would be but still dont over power the space.Took about a week for them to break in and start to produce some great sounds. Had a house party the week after and had the whole house shaking with the rest of my BIC set up.Bottom line, I love them and am happy shelling out the close to $600 I payed for them. :) These towers are WONDERFUL for movies, sports, and any other TV watching experience.  For music, however, I feel they leave a lot out in the mid-range frequency department.  Now, with the right receiver and EQ settings, this deficiency is almost non-existent...but it still exists to the trained ear.  I would also like to see a bi-amp option for these towers.  Overall a great buy for the typical home theater setup.

name: Nikon En-EL9a Rechargeable Li-ion Battery - Retail Packaging

name: Lowepro Toploader Pro 65 AW (Black)
reviewText: This small version of a large camera case is perfect.  I have a Nikon D70 and a few lenses, but periodically, I wish to carry the camera alone, rather than the larger bag I keep it in.  This works great, never worry about the camera banging loose on my side while I am ready to take photos.  It is easy to carry, easy to reach into, and comfortable without feeling bulky.The padding is thick, providing great protection for the camera.  The larger pocket is just enough for small items especially the Nikkor lenses I have.  I like the color, the strap is long enough and the case feels good at my side.  I like the weatherproof rugged material.  Since I don't do a ton with the camera, this is just my size for carrying around the camera.  .....Rizzo The Topeloader Zoom 45 should be good for a DSLR with an attached zoom lens of up to 55mm. I had no problem getting my Sony Alpha and a few small accessories in it. While this is an adequate camera case, I decided that the Alpha will stay inside my slightly more expensiveSony LCS-AMA/B Digital SLR Carrying Case, specifically designed for it.Since there are many reviews already discussing this case, I thought I'd offer a brief comparison between the Lowepro offer and the largely similar Sony case I've been using for the past few years. I would like to make it very clear that the Sony product costs about 35% more so it being the better choice (if price was not an issue) should not be a surprise.LOOKS AND DESIGNBoth cases are black but, if placed next to each other, the Sony is larger (more room inside) and the fabric looks cheaper on the Lowepro. In addition, Sony's displays a leather-like (probably plastic) accent on the front.The Lowepro has one unprotected outside pocket which for some reason appears to be made of an even cheaper-looking nylon. A second internal pocket is protected by padding and it should probably be used to store more fragile accessories such as memory cards. Sony's 2 pockets are both external and some level of protection is achieved by the sturdier material that's lined with some thick velvety fabric on the inside. Sony's case does not have interior pockets.The Lowepro's insides are a thin grey nylon holding some protection pads in between them and the exterior wall. Sony's interior is an elegant velvety and its protection pads are not as obvious as the Lowepro's, making the Sony's the more elegant case, inside and out.Unique to the Lowepro is the rain protection cover that hides inside a secret, Velcro-locked compartment. It sounds like a good idea - when it rains, you pull out the cover and... cover your case with the camera inside. In practice, I've had my Alpha case for several years now and it's been to quite a few places and I don't remember a time when I wished I had a cover that I could use to cover my camera case. But it's good it's there.UTILITYBoth cases had no problem accepting my Alpha and I was able to find room (pockets) for the few accessories I carry: a USB cable, a memory card, a quick cleaning kit.Both cases come with an adjustable and removable shoulder strap, a grab handle (Lowepro's is padded) and a belt loop. Sony's case, while larger or rather because it is larger makes it somewhat easier to quickly get the camera in and out of it and its side pockets are easy to access. Lowepro's internal pocket may offer more protection.EVALUATIONThe Lowepro is not a bad case and I would use it if I had no alternative option. However, knowing what I know, I am going to keep Sony's as my primary camera case. If I had to make a purchase decision, I would pay more and get the Sony case. These being said, the Lowepro earns its 3 stars which, on Amazon's star scale means "it's Okay"._____________________________________________Note:I just noticed that reviews from more than one model seem to be bundled together: 55 AW, 60 AW, 65 AW, 75 AW. THIS review is for the ZOOM 45 AW case only. The cases are quite different, it seems so I would be mindful of this. For example, one review states that you can rearrange the removable foam pads, which is nice but this is not a feature found in the 45 AW. Naturally, any comments regarding the bag's roominess should be related to the specific model. I love this bag!  I use this bag mainly for hiking and in the future, biking.  I use it with both the shoulder straps and chest straps, both are excellent ways to carry the bag.  I use it to carry my 1D Canon with a 70-200IS zoom attached, a strobe in the exterior pocket, and cards and spare batteries.  I don't regret buying this bag and would recommend it to anyone.  Great bag!Update (08/23/2011): I've been using this bag very frequently for almost two years now and for the most part, I love it.  It's still just as functional as when I first bought it.  There is a problem though. On one side of the bag where the shoulder strap attaches to the bag, it's beginning to tear alittle.  It may be due to frequent use, but isn't that what the bag is for?  The bag is still serviceable, but I'm not sure for how much longer. This is very well thought out. Plenty of room for my full frame camera with medium zoom attached. I like the built-in rain cover. I use this camera bag for backpacking.  I attach it to my backpacks hit belt and it works great.  It's not in the way while I walk and keeps my camera easily accessible.  The bag has plenty of padding and the built in all-weather cover is a bonus while in the wilderness.  It's designed to fit a DSL with a vertical grip but will fit a camera without one with some extra room.  I can fit my Nikon D200 in this bag along with a 28-80mm lens without the lens hood or the lens hood inverted.  The extra pockets are nice along with the buckle to close the bag.  While hiking I never zipper up the bag unless it's raining.

name: Noctua NT-H1 3.5g, Pro-Grade Thermal Compound Paste.
reviewText: First time switching away from Arctic Silver. I definitely don't regret it! This stuff is inexpensive (this tube is huge, and will last for at least 10 builds), easier to apply, and the cooling performance is equal or better in every case I've seen. You get quite a bit in this syringe and it works well. I game quite a bit on my L502x and I used this thermal paste to refresh the older  thermal paste on my laptop. No problems after a month. Its a good paste easy to spread and it Dropped my temps about 5 degrees c from Arctic silver 5 I am not one to run bench marks so i am not going to rattle off temperatures that probably don't have anything to do with what particular hard ware you would be using this thermal paste on. I am just going to say that this is one of the best thermal pastes out there in terms of performance. Once you get to a certain level of quality, there really is a negligible difference between them in terms of temperatures.However Noctua Thermal Compound has a couple of features that make it rise above the competition. Firstly it requires no curing. Compared to other thermal compounds that may take weeks, if not longer, of high temperature, as well as temperature cycling (going from hot to room temperature) to reach their peak performance, this compound is at peak performance from the moment you install it.Second feature is its low viscosity. That is, its not as thick as some competing thermal compounds, meaning that no matter what CPU you are installing this Noctua Thermal Compound on, it does not require spreading nor tinting of the thermal compound on the CPU/Cooler. All installation requires is a small pea sized dot of Noctua Thermal Paste in the center of the CPU and then place the heatsink. Because of the low viscosity of the thermal paste, the pressure between the heasink/waterblock and the CPU does all the work of spreading the thermal paste evenly and without any performance-decreasing air bubbles. Transfers more heat than AS5, even though it's a little more expensive. This little tube provides enough thermal insulation material to repaste your chip 50 times over.

name: Shure Srh440-Bk Wired On Ear Headphones Without Microphone Multicolour
reviewText: These are very analytical at times, and fast headphones. They do really well with all sorts of metal, rock, acoustic, classical, and even electronic. Throw any of your most complex and noisy songs at these headphones and they still still be able to separate everything out and let you listen to everything. As with most full sized headphones, this one is no exception, the 3D imaging is very good and among the best I've ever heard. They are comfortable, but not built from the best materials. They will survive multiple drops for sure, but they creak a lot, even when new. The plastics are decent, but the headband and earcup pleather isn't from the highest quality sources. Also sometimes my ears can feel the dynamic drivers of the headphones! There is no headclamping tho! and they do fold up!Compared to the also really popular Audio Technica M-50, they sound much less colored and professional, but with distinctly dropped low end bass response. The M50's probably are just a tad slower, so they are fine for metal and rock, but their treble is less smooth, the bass is at times too bumbped, and mids are clearly recessed. also soundstage and instrument separation is better on the shures. On the other hand, if sound quality is second only to build quality, go with the Audio Technica's. They are clearly superiorly built. They are made form better materials and have better cushions, although the headclamping was quite severe for my slightly large head. Bought two of these for two of my sons.  They both wear them often, for long periods of time, without complaint, so they must be comfortable.  Nothing has broken.  I appreciate the replaceable cord, as I expect that the cord is the most likely part to fail.  The sound quality is the best of any headphones I have used, but bear in mind that I have not used any high end audiophile headphones.  Plenty of bang for the buck in this item. These headphones produce amazingly clear sound.  I'm hearing details in almost all of my songs that I'd never heard before, and I love that.  The problem is that I can only enjoy the sound if I'm perfectly still, and ideally lying down.  The perfectly-still part is because these things creak *terribly* every time I move my head even the tiniest amount.  I'm not talking about full head turns, just the small adjustments as I look from one side of my computer screen to the other at work, or glance up as someone passes my cube.  It's maddening.  The lying-down part is because they do dig in right at the top of my head after an hour or so.  I don't think I'm at all unusual in terms of head size/shape or amount of hair; it's just that the phones are too heavy to stay in place with lateral pressure (they'd crush your ears) so they have to rest slightly on top instead.  Between these two factors, I love these headphones most of the time but absolutely loathe them sometimes too.  The most frustrating part is how little it would take for Shure to fix both of these problems.  A dollar's worth more metal in the hinges and padding on the top and these would be almost perfect.  How could they come so close and miss? An impressive pair of headphones, I bought them from Amazon after a long research and consideration, and I wasn't at all disappointed, especially after I bought an Asus D1 Sound card to go with it. Sound quality is perfect and you can hear new depths and details in Music when used with a good sound card. This combination of Headphones/sound card gives perfect sound with Classical Music, which is the only kind of music I listen to. Love these! great product and value for the money. These are some of the best headphones I've used. I've been using them pretty much none stop since Jan 2012 and they're still great. These are definitely quality build. Highly recommend for anyone that cares about great sound.
