name: JOBY GorillaPod SLR Zoom. Flexible Tripod with Ballhead Bundle for DSLR and Mirrorless Cameras Up To 3kg. (6.6lbs).
reviewText: I take a lot of low light photography and didn't like always looking for a stable place to put my camera. This solved my problems, Whether it's wrapping it around something or just placing it on a surface it gives me a stable place to set the camera for a timer shot to get those clear long shutter photo's. It's very light to carry around as well. I Don't go out on photo shoots without it! I was looking for a smaller tripod to take with me on a recent trip abroad for slower shutter speed shots.  I had used some of the smaller gorillapod tripods in the past with point and shoot but recently moved up to a DSLR.A few highlights:The ball head feature with level is because I can get the tripod all set up before putting the camera on it and then simply attach the camera.  This makes it easier/safer to get the tripod secure.Unlike a normal tripod, this one will work better on rocky terrain and can attach to things like tree branches or posts and still take great shots.I really like this tripod so far.  Would recommend having a remote shutter release for use. If you did your research on this tripod, you would surely know that it is a must buy for enthusiastic photographers. It is quite a good addition to your gears apart from the typical tripods. I highly recommend it. It is better to buy this bundle where you get the tripod and the ball head for one price.If you need to know more. Check youtube! :) a friend told me that this supports his camera with a large zoom attached....it did not support my nikon d60 with a 70-300mm zoom, I'm disappointed.  Considering sending it back, we'll see... Holds my Canon t3i and 70-300mm lens great. I wrap the legs around my balcony rail and take pictures of the Chicago skyline and other areas around where I live.Easily straps to the side of my camera bag for transport.

name: Aluratek Digital Photo Frame - Black
reviewText: Nice and clear Screen This review concerns the ADMPF108F(hi-def, 512mb built in memory) and the ADPF08SF(standard photo frame)I first bought the standard photo frame ADPF08SF and was completely disappointed. I had loaded all the jpg images onto a SDHC memory card, and only about 7 of the 50 something i had showed up. The others said file not supported, and they had NOTHING in common, file sizes made no difference and i could not rememdy the situation. This frame had no remote, no way to randomize photos, and a very annoying menu access system. Picture quality was fine - on the pictures that i could get to show up. Needless to say i returned this. DONT WASTE YOUR TIME.I then upgraded one step to the ADMPF108F which made ALL THE DIFFERENCE IN THE WORLD. I took that same memory card (even though it has internal memory) and put it in this frame and BAM, perfection. All my files were fine, i was able to get some small videos to play as well as background music going just by going though the menu, WHICH was all accessible by both the back of the frame, AND the remote(which was easier) Quality was just as good. This one has start up and sleep timers, an internal clock, you CAN randomize the photos easily. The remote allows you to switch from pictures to video with one button and music as well. The stand (as always) is a bit flimsy, and you cannot really change the frame orientation, but otherwise fabulous.It included the USB connection cable in the box if you wanted to download photos onto the device itself, but i find memory cards much faster since i update it periodically for my grandfather. It worked at first but them after a day it quit.  I could not get to work again.It was the only thing I ever got from amazon that did not work as had promised. Purchased two (2) of these from Amazon. Arrived well packed and with all parts. All I could do ON BOTH was load pictures. The controls only move the 'cursor' but do not allow one to start or set any functions. E-mailed to Aluratek's customer support but never got a reply. Sent both frames back to Amazon and received replacements. Same problem; the OK button does not work. After 48 h got hold of Aluratek support who could not resolve the problem with out consulting with engineers. Second set of frames returned to Amazon. I got this for my Mom's memorial to show the over 100 pictures I had of her during the reception afterwards.  It worked so well and looks so great that I kept it out in my living room and now just load whatever pictures I want.  I've used family, sunsets, Halloween graphics, Christmas graphics, and vintage postcards.  The timing function works perfectly, and can be used for everyday or just weekdays.  A great item and I'd highly recommend.

reviewText: It works okay.  It is very thin and not as well built as the more expensive ones. This cable is good but not perfect. I was looking for a long cable to hook up my Desktop to my LCD TV. name: Hoya 77mm HMC UV Digital Slim Frame Multi-Coated Glass Filter
reviewText: Nothing special - working as i expected. Good protection for expensive lens.BTW UV protection is not so strong, but better than nothing.Easy to clean up.Think  that it costs money spent on it! I bought this to use with a Nikon 18-300mm lens. I use UV filters as a "cheap" way to protect my lenses, and I always buy glass. I always leave them on. this one fits perfectly on the lens I have. Recommended All I can say is that it works and I don't see any color shift in my images while using this filter. I don't think it went through QC.  The part came defective, the glass was scratched and even broken around the rim.  I immediately printed out the label and returned it. I took this out of the packaging case, put it on my lense, went out and shot a few pics. Everything looks okay on my LCD screen until I uploaded to my PC. There were these little weird coloration dots and blobs on my pics! I thought could have been my lense getting dirty, sensor dust etc, but when I took the filter off, the dots were not there. So I tried cleaning these blobs off with my lense leaning solution and it did not came off. What a bad build. I would not recommend this. In fact, I don't recommend buying anymore UV filters. They are a waste of money. Just get a CPL or ND and you are set.

name: Hoya 58mm HMC Ultraviolet UV(C) Haze Multicoated Filter
reviewText: I purchased this product as protective device for my Canon Powershot G 12 and has worked flawlessly . I've used Hoya filters since the 80's and have never failed I bought this after purchasing a cheap UV filter last time and I have no complaints here. Definitely worth the little extra money to buy this lens. What it comes down to is I'll gladly spend $15 to project a lens worth hundreds of dollars any day. Good buy. This is a very nice filter.  It fits the lens well and does the job well.  It serves to eliminate glare. This filter is made in the philippines and not japan, Is it a big issue? for me it's a NO.. why? Tokina/Hoya has branch factory in the philippines and it's the same company owned by Tokina Corps/Hoya from japan. The reason why it's cheap is because the labor in the philippines are cheaper than japan and it doesn't mean that it has less quality built or CHEAP quality at all. I owned 5 different Hoya filters, 2 made in Japan and 3 made in Philippines and I don't see such a big differences comparing japan/philippines made. Both works great and never fail me yet. Hoya is a very good filter for the money. People shouldn't get bothered where it made from because it's from the same company. Nothing big difference except for labor wise.This filter has nice quality built, Good for protecting lens against dust, I bought one for my 50mm 1.8G, I wasn't going to buy one but it's kinda hard to protect the 50mm 1.8g since it has deep glass, using the hood is still not enough to protect against dust so I thought of getting a hoya. I also debated between this and the pro1 digital hoya that made in japan but why bother spend more money if you can get a nice and cheaper filter? Was very happy at first with the Hoya Haze Multi-Coated (HMC) filters I bought here. But, while on a trip to the USVI the main lens' filter got smudged inadvertently. Never had a problem cleaning filters before, but NOTHING we tried (Kodak cleaner, lens wipes, micro-cloths, warm breath - you name it) worked and we ended up removing the filter from the lens for the duration. When I did a little digging I found lots of "hate mail" and debate about this problem - with a number for folks surmising this couldn't be a problem. The one consistent fix I read about from pros who had experienced this with the multi-coated Hoyas only, was to use Anhydrous Methyl Alcohol (a HAZMAT product). So I've tossed the Hoyas into a "rainy day project" bin to see if I can get the smudges out without resorting to HAZMAT. I'm replacing these with theB+W 58mm Clear UV Haze with Multi-Resistant Coating (010M)and theB+W 58mm Clear UV Haze with Single Coating (010)based on reviews and my digging through the web.Bottom line - when free of greasy smudges (all it was for us was simple skin oil from a finger print), these are nice. Once smudged, look out, or better yet, take off.Original Post: Bought a couple of these for the wife's new digital SLR and we just love them. Really high quality filter and coating. Very nice packaging. Seems to shed dust, if that's even possible. Easy to clean and very nice threads making it a perfect fit with our 58mm-wide Canon lenses. So much cheaper than Canon, too. We're not professionals by any stretch, but these are a great addition to the bag and cheap insurance for the valuable lenses. We took some side-by-side pictures - flash and natural - and cannot tell any difference with the filter on or off under non-hazy conditions. Haven't really tried in hazy settings, but that's only a secondary reason we bought them (protection was the main reason). Would buy again and recommend to friends and family.

name: SAMSON SR850 Studio Wired Over Ear Headphones Without Mic (Black)
reviewText: The Samson SR850 is a over-the-ear semi-open headphone.  They bear a striking resemblance to the AKG K240 but with a different color scheme and vent designs.  They have a 32 Ohm impedance, so they can be driven easily by on-board sound cards, mobile phones, dvd players and etc.  The package includes the headphones, a 1/4 adapter, and the warranty and information card.The headphones are fairly light, with a large pleather headband that rests comfortably on your head.  These have a self adjusting headband so you can just put them on without any adjustment.  It is made mostly of plastic and feel somewhat durable.  The cable is pretty thick and the ear pads are made of a semi soft vinyl.This is a pretty bassy headphone especially if you EQ the low end a bit.  They are extremely good or watching movies and video games as they have fairly large sound stage and sound great.  The bass extends pretty low and is a little muddy.  The mids feel little neutral and the highs have a slight sparkle to them.I feel that these headphones are very good for gaming and are a solid choice for those wanting something like the Audio Technica AD700's with a lot more bass.  The price is very attractive and the headphones perform extremely well.  The only flaw that I see are the stock ear pads, they are very rigid and uncomfortable.  I would highly recommend replacing them with the Creative Sound Blaster ear pads if you like pleather, or the AKG K240 velour ear pads if you like a velvet material.  Because of ear pads, I give this product a 4 out 5 stars. Straight out of the box typing this review while listening to the highest quality .wave music i got. well what can i say, these are definitely light, they look cheaply made, but judging from the feel of them I'd say they're strong (guess we'll see in time). now for the importance of sound because we all know that these are not pretty, not beautiful in any way... out of the box, these headphones seem a little harsh on the ears (mostly in highs), ears started ringing shorty after trying them at a high volume to see how they would sound. now after dumbing* down the level to about volume level 38 they seem good, just right for now, not too harsh but on the limits (but once again, haven't burnt them in yet and I will update with a comment once i do. first thoughts on these, are why is the ambient noise so easy to hear, like a high powered fan in the room, but then again these ARE SEMI-OPEN headphones so i mean i don't blame them in any way... overall, i would definitely mix projects with these in studio use, I've listened to about two separate mixed down projects and they sound pretty good, so I mean i was kinda expecting alot more out of these than the pair of headphones i currently own, but i mean they are way better sounding, but just feel like i would want to be in a closed environment while listening to these (ex: passive/active noise cancelling, makes you feel like your IN the music or its right there with you... these headphones do not have this effect, it feels like your listening to well "headphones" lol. but they do sound good.) the cord is long, the gold plated plug is simple sweet, makes you feel like yes, they did think about quality when making these (the larger tip screws onto the smaller one). once again listening to music whilst typing this review, they do get warm on ear but are tolerable so that's not yet a bother to me. comfort wise, they could be a little smaller NOT MUCH, but just a Lil bit, but the self adjusting headband *Genius*, i like. and well that's all I've got to say hence far.Hope this is helpful from an out of box point of view. These are better than I was expecting. I've seen great reviews for them on a lot of tech forums so I decided to try them out. Gotta say, if I ever break these I will buy another of the same. Was considering beats audio until I found out they are nothing but poop with glitter on top. PC Gamers..As much as you'd like to brag about that nice, badass 5.1 surround sound you have, chances are you have neighbors, like me, and can't exactly blast your gaming as loud as you'd like..So you sport a pair of gaming headphones, ones that have the microphone integrated, or simulated surround sound.. And are content with that like I was. Until I purchased these headphones.Granted, these do not include a microphone.. But a good standalone microphone, like the Zalman ZM-Mic1 I have (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00029MTMQ/ref=cm_cr_ryp_prd_image), clips perfectly on the cord and has amazing reviews as well. .Giving me a combination of a good microphone and headset..The sound card I have on my Desktop PC is an Asus ROG Xonar Phoebus. With this soundcard i've had three seperate headsets. A Plantronics Gamecom 777, Creative Fatal1ty Edition, and a Turtle Beach Ear Force X12. All three of those are absolute garbage compared to these open ear Samsons...Everybody's ears are different, but I have to say that for the money these headphones blew me away. Listening to music after I broke these in was astonishing. I was hearing things I've never heard in my songs before.. And I'm not talking about crappy 128kb MP3s I got from Johnny Vanu down the road, I'm talking about FLAC audio, and 320kb/s lossless MP3s. It's a very versatile headset that I would highly recommencement be paired with a decent clip on microphone for a full, isolated gaming experience (For when you can't break out the true surround sound) I'm not an audiophile, but I don't get why everyone is so high on these cans.  Very cheaply made...cheaper than headphones that cost $20.  Cheap packaging.  They arrived curled up in a way that they were lopsided, cause there was no form holding it in place in the box.  Also smelled like toxic chemicals.  Sound is just mediocre.  JVC HA-RX700 sound better IMO, and cost significantly less.  I feel like rating it a 1 star, but I'm feeling like I'm missing something because these are almost always recommended as the best budget headphones.  If they were $20 I wouldn't complain (as much anyway), but at $50 these seem like a worst buy. RX700, even the ATH-AD300 is better.Also, for people with either a bigger sized head, or someone who doesnt like pressure on their heads, these are not comfortable.  The material of the padding (I use the term padding loosely)  on the cups, cheap headband, and the smallish size, just made me want to take them off as soon as I put them on.  I was tempted to put them on a basketball and buy replacement cups, but really, at $50 you don't need to go through that hassle.  And that would put the total cost in the non knockoff range of the lower end of the better mid range headphones.  haha, if that makes sense.Anyways, these are a try before you buy kind of thing.  Not quite cheap enough to be throwaways if you don't like them.  Lots of people like them, so you might as well.  Just don't expect too much from them.

name: Polk Audio T15 100 Watt 5.1 Channel Wired Bookshelf Speaker with Dolby (Black)
reviewText: Truly surprising sound quality. So impressed, made me decide to see what the higher end Polk RTI A1`s sounded like. Think thats part of Polks clever marketing plan...give you something incredible for cheap...suck you in, expecting you will likely buy more Polk stuff. Bass does lack somewhat as others have said...but it`s not bad either. Mid-upper range is just great. Crossed over around 80~100 hz with a nice sub, to get the lower notes/bass off them, and you got great sound for very little money. Now day`s they have been moved to rear surround duty in my 5.1 set up. Simple, but nice looking, great sounding speakers for the money. Well this little project is done and I could not be more happier with the final results. The Polk Audio T15's came in lastnight, and the joy of using banana plugs make switching out speakers a breeze. I put the T15's through some test music from the following artist:Earl Klugh - Solo GuitarSteely Dan - GouchoTeereny Sutton Band - American RoadJill Scott - Heat of the sun5.1 mode:SW Episode 1 Pod Race BD versionThe T15's are surprisingly much more easier to drive than the LX5's, resulting in less effort from the VSX D510 to produce a warm airy sound that filled the room. The old addage of using matching speakers rings so true with this setup as the T15's blended very well with the Polk Audio PSW 10 sub with one not dominating over the other. I thought I would miss the 360 degree tweeters of the LX5's. but the T15's have a very wide pattern with a detail sound. The most impressive part was the depth of the sound. It just gave a sense of more sound and less roll off (if that makes any sense). I felt the design of direct speakers gave a better center image of vocals and made me check the center channel to make sure it was not working. The LX5's are no slouch, but just need to be placed in the right positions to excel. This room was just a bit to small for them to be able to reach their full potential, unlike the master bedroom where they sing like the birds. I also did a test in 5.1 to see how they would handle BD and DVD's. They worked very well and even found myself hearing things from the right and left channels I had not heard before or should say not in such detail from each channel and I contribite most of that to the size of the room where there is not enough distance for the sound to blend together compared to my other HT systems. I look at this as a classic example of matching up the right speakers with the right room and getting the desired results.I would highly recommend these Polk T15's and you can get them dirt cheap new (under $100) retail. As part of a 2.1/5.1 setup you could do much much worse. ok ill give you the lowdown of my game/cinema rooma huge plasma by panasonic which has great speakers for midsi started with these as my surround soundi have then added two onyo large speakers, a onyo center speakerand recetly two large kenwood bass reflex retailed at 300$and do you know what ? these polk audios are the loudest speakers i own, and have more bass. the blow away all my other speakers that roughly 5 speakers + tv speakers are being overshadowed by two of these. i actually bought these from bestbuy on sale, 90$'s for a set of speakers, i tested them and the sales guy just had me sold on a demo of these and i have NEVER regretted it, by far best sound i have in the house and loudest, and they are bookshelve speakers!!! small and easily portable and fit anywhere, whearas my 5 others are large and clunky i am actually thinking about junking them to get a set of olk audio t15's again and maybe 2 larger models because they just cant be beaten ! After an extensive search for a new pair of speakers to complete my living room HI-FI system, I decided to walk into a local Kenosha WI retailer just to shop around. I asked the store attendant for a good, inexpensive pair of bookshelf surround speakers and he said "These are on sale and they are the last pair left". I really liked the sound reproduction the minute I listened to them. The bass sounded deeper than other more expensive models. At first I thought I'll use them to add to my small family room as left/right speakers. So I purchased them for an even lower price compared to any other offers. When I got home I told myself, let me try these in the living room first, easy wire hook-up and OMG!! WOW!! WHAT A GREAT CLEAR SOUND & DEEP BASS PLUS A PERFECT COLOR MATCH TO REST OF MY HI-FI SYSTEM!! SO THE LIVING ROOM IS WHERE THESE BABIES ARE STAYING!!! I bought a pair of the T15 speakers from Polk Audio for use with my computer to replace the life-less speakers that I was using prior. I bought a class "T" amp with a built in DA converter that plugs into a USB port on the computer and the speakers attach to the binding posts on the amp. This little set-up has made the computer more usable as a listing device for music(the amp also allows me to use my Sony V6 headphones via the jack on the front of the amp). The Polk speakers are great in the mids and the high range, they lack a little on the bottom, but still very listenable, they work just fine using Itunes, but they work better with the higher bit rate songs. I would recommend these for anyone looking to upgrade from the traditional sound card/computer speaker setup.

name: Dayton Audio B652 40 Watt Wired Bookshelf Speaker (Black)
reviewText: At $44 a pair you really can't find a better pair of speakers.  Shipping was free and they came in three days.  I wired them up to my Yamaha receiver and they sound great. First, I'm not going to attempt to compare these to other speakers out of the price range of sub $75/pair.I was expecting these to be a bit chintzy and not be able to deliver a complete, full rich sound, I WAS WRONG!I bought these to have a pair of speakers in my front room to listen to while having company over. I have a decent studio in the back with a pair of HS80's that I love to death.  But it sucked having all the stuff in the back room and having to walk back and forth.My place is sort of empty with wood floors.  I have these over in the corner, facing away and up towards the walls.  They completely fill the front room (900sqr ft) with no troubles at all.This is only my second day using them and well... they are just perfect what I wanted. for the price it made my old stereo sound great, the base and mid range were greatly improved,the look is good to,very good for the money For the price paid, these are far better than they have a right to be. The size is good, the construction is well done, and the sound is awesome....what more can you ask for for under $50.00?? I cant believe the complaints on here about the sound....for what you paid it takes a lot to complain. What did you expect, the best sound out there? The highest quality??You get exactly what you pay for here, and that's not a bad thing. Try them out if your in a small office of for the bedroom, they just might be all you need. Got a pair of these about a year ago.  These new ones sound way better then the old ones.  Love it!  Laptop, LP-2020A+ Lepai (2013 model) plus these speakers and life is good.

name: Ubiquiti BULLET-M2-HP Outdoor 802.11 B/G/N M2HP
reviewText: I had one of these that worked well for two years then quit.  The new one didn't work at all and Ubiquity support was horrible (e-mail only, slow, repeatedly wrong/inefficient advice).  After 3 weeks of trying I returned this product but will probably buy one from a reseller who is willing/able to actually help with any issues.  I should add that I'm very technical but this product, if it doesn't just plug and play like my first one did, is for geeks only.  Any troubleshooting and re-configuring beyond the defaults is not for the technology faint-of-heart. I purchased this for use in a Motorhome connected to a WifiRanger Pro.  The Ranger has a plug for their own version called the WFRBoost.  The Bullet2-HP is higher powered and with a proper antenna can reach an access point MILES away.One caveat is that it is too powerful for close in connections.  Dialing down the power settings does not really seem to help.  If you try to use it to connect to an access point too close you will over power the access point and not only will it not connect but can cause interference with anyone else trying to connect.I mounted mine to an 8db omni directional antenna.  That in turn was mounted to a telescoping flag pole with a mount that slides in the receiver hitch.  That setup allowed me to connect to a public hotspot at a Marina while camped a couple of miles away on the beach.For a primary use in campgrounds and RV parks I would recommend the lower powered bullet2 and a 3db antenna.I dropped a star because to a novice it can be somewhat intimidating.  The interface is intuitive if you have a networking background or are using something like the Ranger.  A beginner will be very confused as to how to set one up. This is the coolest thing ever. It has a sweet user interface. It has a lot of advance features. It may not be for those with little experience in setting up networks. This allows you to do many AP options.I have heard of weatherproof problems. My advice is to put this where there is not much exposure to the elements. For those who have no choice, there is a Titanium Bullet for a bit more $$$. This is a grest access point.  I purchased it with its ethernet power supply and the eNgenius EAG-2408 antenna as a relatively high power HSMM node for amateur radio use.  It took about 15 minutes to get working and is 20 dB more powerful than my previous Linksys system,It only has one ethernet port, so this appears to be perfect for mounting outside to form the mesh, with a Linksys unit inside to connect to the internet if needed and provide connections for the systems.Excellent unit! This is a very good product for its purpose.  There is the usual complaint about Ubiquiti not putting some marketing money into making their product line more "user friendly."

name: TP-Link Nano USB WiFi Dongle 150Mbps High Gain Wireless Network Wi-Fi Adapter for PC Desktop and Laptops, Supports Windows...
reviewText: This is NOT plug and play like some other reviews led me to believe. I do not have a CD/DVD on my PC so it was a slight inconvenience not being able to plug and play. I ended up having to using my laptop to make an ISO of the disc then transferring that to my external drive and virtually mounting it on my PC. My only other issue is that the antenna is on the side of the unit. For me, this meant the antenna was pointing towards the ground and in the way of some of my other wires. It would have been better had the antenna been on the end of it.Aside from that, installation was easy. You simply plug it into a USB port, install the drivers (I installed the drivers only, there is no reason to use the software they provide), waited a minute or so then saw that there were wireless networks available. It seems to work well so far. I haven't tried to do any streaming but it was getting good speeds and wasn't randomly disconnecting me. This installed without problem, but when I did a speed check, the download speeds were around 1.5 mbps.  We usually get around 20 mbps.  I replaced it with an Ethernet cable, and now all is good. I got this to replace a failing Cisco adapter and the difference is amazing.  It maintains its connection without fail, and I am achieving greater speeds than I ever did with the old adapter.  I like that it comes with a long cable so I can position the adapter a little closer to the router. It's also smaller, shorter & has a longer warranty than most other Wireless-n adapters with the same specs.  So I highly recommend it. the product connected me to the internet for 2 sec then my acer computer never recognized it again. i waited quite a while for the delivery and then the device failed me. BUT on the bright side  there was no issue in getting my refund!

name: TP-LINK TL-WN821N 300 MBPS WiFi WI-FI Wireless N USB Adapter, MIMO, WPS Button, Supports Windows 11/10/8.1/8/7/XP, Mac OS ...
reviewText: I purchased this wireless adapter to transfer data from my laptop to main server and back at a speed faster than "G" speed.  My laptop has (at least I thought) a weak antenna and is only capable of wireless-G speed.  This adapter should provide me with higher "N" transfer speed and better reception.  I installed the drivers on a Windows 7 32bit machine without issue.Test results:Laptop Built in Wireless 3945ABG card ASUS G1 :Maximum transfer speed : 1.21 MB/sSignal Strength (-60dbi)TP-LINK TL-WN821N USB Adapter from exact same location :Maximum transfer speed: 1.8MB/sSignal Strength: (-72dbi) *** LESS than built in card even though number higherBy moving closer to the router, the TP-LINK TL-WN821N data transfer speed picked up to a maximum of 7.15 MB/sIs it worth it??  I suppose if you need an adapter, this one will do, nothing remarkable. This WiFi adapter works well.  It always connects and doesn't drop the connection.  I use this on a linux desktop machine running debian.  I did have to install the correct module from the repository to get it to be recognized but that's to be expected on linux.  Have not tried it on Windows but I am sure it will work just as well and of course you would just use the included driver disc for that. Unfortunately, I cannot give this device a good rating.  It's really suited for an individual who knows nothing about computers and just wants a simple connection.  This device is not suited for advanced IT users who want all the features.  It is a 2.4 GHz only device!  There is no separate 5Ghz band.  Because of this you may experience a lot of interference with older 2.4 Ghz wireless devices.  The software program is also very simple and you can use Windows too to connect.  Another issue I had was that it does not support MAC filtering.  It doesn't even have a MAC address printed on it.  I tried to contact support but they ignored my emails.  I got no response.  I might just throw this away or give it to charity.  I went back to my old Linksys device.  For wireless adapters and routers, stick with the brand names.  You get what you pay for! This is my fouth TP Link, an excellent product, I recommend this to extend wireless range anywhere. If you are out side roaming, it is reasonably directional using the extension it comes with, to find the source of a wireless signal. The 300bps wireless n is clean and clear over 300ft of tropical rainforest, so room to room or building to building is no problem. Doesn't work on Windows 7 (even though it says it's compatible). Doesn't work on Linux. Doesn't work on Vista. Complete and utter garbage. I ended up going out and buying a different wifi adapter at Best Buy. Don't waste your money.

name: SanDisk Cruzer Blade SDCZ50-016G-135 16 GB USB 2.0 Pen Drive (Red)
reviewText: The drive works fine and I like the indicator light, BUT you have to hold the slider part AND the outer case with one hand to keep the drive end from sliding back into the unit.  There should be some kind of latch and release there, like on a box cutter.  No problem on my PC, but it is a drag on a USB slot that is not as accessible like the one on my blu-ray player. I bought this flash drive specifically to use in my car for music. I don't change the files on it often, but when I do, I wish I had gotten a faster flash drive. It's most noticeable when moving large numbers of files or large files, at which point I just drag and drop what I need and walk away from my laptop.Otherwise it's a great little USB drive. It feels sturdy, has no moving parts so nothing that will stop working. I just wouldn't use it as an everyday flash drive. It was working well and was being used rarely, so no heavy usage...than one day it won't let me format or delete individual archives. It will show the "write protected" message. Surfed around and found this is a common problem in Sandisk USB Drives, a shame. Delete all of the garbage that comes from the company and takes up half the memory. Once you do that it is the drag and drop device it should be. Really good price for the size. 4 not 5 only because its loaded with junk out of the package There is a reason this drive is so inexpensive. In my opinion this is an extremely slow flash drive. The casing and USB tip of this drive is soft plastic. I do not have high hopes that this drive will be durable. There is no drive access light. If you are going to be using it regularly I would pay a little more and get something better from SanDisk.

name: Micca M-8C 100 Watt 7.0 Channel In-ceiling, In-wall Speaker (White)
reviewText: I have installed 2 of these in the ceiling as the main Left and Right channels(5.1 System). I have a Sony 520 providing all the  power. Music sounds pretty good, but my 10" 300W sub helps these out allot. The sound when watching TV or movies on my 100" Projector screen is very good. I really wish i could have more pivot to these speakers as they point straight down, but the overall sound is solid. I have the matching Mica dual 5" Center Channel and 2 Micca 6" for the rear surround speakers. since my screen is 100" we sit back at least 15' from the screen and these speakers. I get the real sweet sound spot around 8-10' from the front of them. but then I'm more bellow them and therefore I can hear them more clearly.I had 0 Problems with all the Micca speakers in 3+ months. Friends and family all say the sound is excellent. And most of them are hearing it from 20+ feet away in the kitchen. They blend into the ceiling very well. A real nice expensive look and professional quality with Micca. Overall a solid 4 stars. I just wish, I could get a little more full sound out of them. I bought four of these for my side and rear surround speakers. The sound is great, far better than the price would suggest. They installed easily and almost disappear in my ceiling. The wife liked them so well, she suggested that I order two more to replace some box speakers I had in the mater bath and dressing area (yes, I love music that much), so I did. I put them in the ceiling in those rooms so we can enjoy music while getting ready for work in the mornings.Great value-Excellent sound and quality. Buy them!Update - The more these play, the better they sound. Apparently, the woofer needs considerable breaking in because after two months of playing them 30 minutes here and there the bass is really starting to come alive. I loved them before, but they are really developing some thump now that the woofer cone is moving freely and I am thrilled. These speakers will stand toe-to-toe with the big name speakers costing 4 times as much. I am particular about my audio equipment, but I can highly recommend these.Follow Up---Over a year later, I am still completely happy with these speakers. They have sparkling highs, a smooth midrange, and good base for an unbaffled ceiling speaker. As mentioned above; I have 4 of these in my home theater as surround speakers, and two in my bath and dressing rooms for music. They really sound great and they are priced much lower than speakers costing far more. I installed a lot of Speakers in my time these speakers rock for what they cost, can you find something better sounding ofcourse but not in this price range! I saw these recommended at a home theater site so thought I'd try them.  I am very pleased with the full range sound performance and great surround sound experience.  The voice clarity of the center channel is one of the best I have owned. Bass response is good, but I recommend adding a powered subwoofer. They were simple to install and look great in the ceiling.  The grills came out for installation and went back in easily. I have installed the 6" in-ceiling speakers at the house up north.  For my basement rear-surrounds I decided on the 8".  I am not dissappointed.  Great value, nice clean look and sound.  Now if I ever finish the room these will blend in and you'll only notice the great surround.  I'm actually considering these for my zone-2 application.

name: Lowepro Slingshot 202 AW (Black)
reviewText: After reading this please feel free to comment with questions regarding any aspect of the bag. It's always a gamble buying online which is why I now own so many bags. It's been an expensive education so hopefully I can help you.To begin, I've been quickly converted to a Lowepro person. I have many camera bags and while others are a bit more stylish and/or roomy, Lowepro scores the highest for practicality. I own theLowepro Pro Runner 200 AW DSLR Backpack  - Blackwhich is great for slightly more gear but this bag is my everyday go-to for roaming the city or casual jaunts from the hotel when traveling. This and all my Lowepro bags are very sturdy, ever-so-slightly stiff (which can be good and bad) and stitched better than any other brand near this price. As for the stiffness, this bag is much stiffer than the Runner 200. It makes it more rigid but less conforming to your body. The Runner 200 is more in the direction of an everyday backpack as far as style and rigidity but still offers superior padding for gear. Another surprise for me after owning the slingshot for 6 weeks now is how wrong I was when I thought I would never enjoy using a sling-style bag. I don't appreciate sling-style or messenger type bags for any other purpose but for quick access to my shooting gear- I'm now a believer!A small negative for me is the inside organization. I have it situated much like the picture. I own a Canon 60D and usually keep  myCanon EF-S 17-55mm f/2.8 IS USM Lens for Canon DSLR Camerasattached. It's 77mm wide and fits perfect while on camera. The downside for me is I also like to carry a fisheye and 10-22mm. Getting those wide lenses in and out of the compartments on either side of the camera is just the slightest bit of a hassle due to the top of each  compartment being slightly covered by the overhang that the access panel zips to. The hassle is due to literally inserting a round peg into a rectangular hole. Again, only a slight hassle and I shoot with this bag a lot. The aforementioned pockets are however very convenient for all other gear storage such as flash diffusers, batteries, filters, and even a flash. I keep my 580 Exll speedlight in the top zippered compartment separate from the camera cuz the flash is too big to squeeze in the lower compartment with the other gear. Said top pocket is about the size of a  scale lunchbox. I used it the other day to hold my huge flash, a pair of gloves, a 77mm lens hood, a multi-tool and a couple of 77mm filters in individual cases. I often use it for granola bars and fruit if out in the woods.Out in the woods brings up another negative. However, 95% of all camera bags suffer from the same deficiency and that is that it DOESN'T hold a water bottle.  Hey, bag makers! We get thirsty when we're out and about!  Also, a tripod shorter than 19 inches is recommended or it can make the bag feel cumbersome. I know because my tripods are 19 and 21 inches when collapsed and the 21 is a bit unwieldy.Nutshell- Best bag I own! When you're carrying thousands in gear- confidence and convenience are a must and this bag offers the best of both. Let me preface this review with a little history. I shoot photos and video for a studio, they have an older version of this bag from 05 or 06 I think. I have used that bag in the field before lightly loaded (two lenses [14mm f/2.8L, 24-105mm f4L], 5DMII w/ battery grip, & batteries) and it was GREAT. That experience was the main motivating factor for me to buy this bag before I got my new personal camera (next year it will be my back up). I did not recently look at the old bag before I got this one.I'll start with the positives, this bag sits comfortably on the neck/shoulder lightly loaded (one to two lenses, camera, & batteries) this is where the bag really shines. The tripod pocket holds my mono pod like a glove. My pocket strobe fits perfectly in the top pouch under the elastic. For the size of the bag, it has lots of pockets to store stuff. Getting in and out of the bag is a cinch and there is enough room to slide my D7000 w/ battery grip in and out of the side zippered area on the main flap without needing to unclip anything. For a small bag it holds a good amount of gear.On to the cons. After wearing it fully loaded (3 lenses [70-300 f/4.5, 18-70 f/3.5, & 50 f/1.8], batteries, SB-800, mono pod, & a D7000 w/ battery grip) on a job for three hours I found it rather uncomfortable after the first hour. My tripod (Manfrotto 055xPROB with a 322RC2 head) does not fit well enough in the holder to use it that way but I imagine that the added weight from the pod would put it over the edge into the uncomfortable range even if the bag was only lightly loaded. I find that I have wasted space in the bag because: my 70-300 does not fit vertically in the bag (by a matter of millimeters), I can not attach dividers exactly where I want them because of the lack of female velcro (the lack of female velcro inside the bag really, really erks me, it would probably only add $1.50 to the production cost to coat the entire inside of the bag and dividers), and I feel the dividers don't offer enough versatility (size, shape, fit, VELCRO). As I sit here and look at the bag as I wright this, I think the lack of a waist strap is really a downfall for me (I knew it didn't have one going into buying this product, but I feel that a waist strap could alleviate some of the stress), as it is the weight resides completely on the shoulder. The shoulder clip that determines the strap length is located on the clip itself which means the adjustment point is SUPER low, I really don't like this. If you look at most messenger bags the strap adjustment resides much higher (look at a Chrome bag) on the strap. It's really a pain to find and tighten and loosen compared to a quality messenger bag.I really wanted to love this bag but it just doesn't work for me. I would return the bag but I prematurely removed the UPC. I do like the bag loaded really lightly, but that is not how I carry it around 90% of the time, I like a bit more versatility in my lenses and apertures especially on certain event shoots. I also fear that as I upgrade away from my 18-70mm & 50mm to a pro zoom in the next year that this will become unusable as Nikon pro glass tends to run a bit heavier than cannon (24-70mm f/2.8 at 902g vs 24-105 f/4L at 670g). I will be investing in a photo backpack with a waist belt soon as I do some research.TLDROverall Rating: C-Pros:Lots of pocketsFeels good lightly loadedFits mono pod nicely in Tripod holderTop pocket holds pocket strobe nicelySide flap works wellCons:Fully loaded, bag hurts my shoulder after an hourLacking female velcro!!!Divider versatility is low, not many ways to customize the bagToo shallow for the 70-300 f/4.5 to fit vertically, eats up more space than necessaryWeird strap adjustment locationMy tripod does not fit well enough to carry around in the tripod holder Overall I love this product. Very functional and excellent quality. I find that I sometimes play 'blocks' while trying to get the various lenses and accessories I want for the day to fit, but this bag is far superior to any other I've used (or seen) in the past. Unqualified recommendation! (My typical day kit includes a Nikon D7000, and two lenses - I choose from a selection of wide angles, primes and a super zoom - the zoom gives me the most problems fitting). இ Fuzzy Wuzzy's Summary:ѾѾѾѾѾ Highly recommended with warm fuzzies!I had been using the previous/original version of this sling bag, theLowepro Slingshot 200 All Weather Backpack (Black), since 2006.  For me, this is the perfect SlingShot size.  The SlingShot 100/102 is too small for my needs, and while I also have the SlingShot 300 AW, I do not like how it sags too low down on my lower back regardless of how tight I try to adjust the straps to raise the bag up to ride higher on my back.  So I only carry my SlingShot 300 AW if I really need to tote the extra amount of gear inside it.This review is entirely written from the perspective of looking at what Lowepro improved upon compared to their original SlingShot 200 AW model.  I have also uploaded 7 fully-annotated images to the 'View and share related images' Customer Images gallery that describe the side-by-side differences between the older SlingShot 200 and new SlingShot 202 models.I noticed that Amazon currently still offers both the older SlingShot 200 AW model and the newer updated 202 AW model for about the same price.  If both are similarly priced, get this 202 AW instead of the older-model 200 AW.  If you currently have a Lowepro SlingShot 200 AW that is showing its wear after years of usage and wonder about switching to the new version, this updated 202 model offers a number of incremental improvements, but this is not a radical redesign of the 200 model, and that is a good thing since the original SlingShot 200 AW was quite good to begin with.While the well-padded sling that goes diagonally across the back of the bag can be hung over your left shoulder so that the bag loosely rests on your left shoulder blade, it is designed to be primarily worn by slipping both your head and left arm through the sling so that the sling comes over your right shoulder, goes diagonally down the front of your body, and connects to the bag behind the left side of your abdomen.  Once the bag is slung onto your back, a smaller strap coming from the bottom-right of your abdomen clasps onto the sling in the front at chest level to further prevent shifting of the bag.One main advantage of this sling design is that you can conveniently access the bag's contents by unclasping the smaller strap and rotating the sling clockwise around your neck to bring the bag from behind your left side until it rests on your abdomen.  With the bag slung in front of you, you can now unzip the main compartment's lid, and you can proceed to change cameras, lenses, memory cards, batteries, or access other supplies.  I have made changes to my camera before while still slowly walking with the backpack slung on my abdomen as the top-facing part of the bag can be used as a platform to rest the camera body upon.This sling bag provides quicker ease of access to your gear by allowing you to swivel the bag from your back to your front, whereas you have to fully take a backpack off to access your gear.  This convenience feature does not only apply to when you are standing up, but if you travel as much as I do, you will find this ability to quickly swivel the bag to the front is also advantageous when frequently getting on and off buses, subways, and trains.  When I get onto a bus, subway, or train, I quickly swivel my SlingShot around to the front so that it rests on my lap while I am sitting down.  And when I get off the bus, the sling bag swivels just as quickly onto my back again.  This is less cumbersome than taking a backpack's straps off your shoulders, placing the backpack on your lap or the floor during the bus ride, and then looping the backpack's straps onto your shoulders again when you get off the bus.However, some people, notably women, may not like how the sling strap and second smaller strap tighten diagonally across the chest area.  So these sling bag configurations will not be comfortable for everyone, especially since a fully-loaded sling backpack can pull on the entire chest area with its frontal diagonal straps.  The load that is exerted onto your chest depends upon how much weight you are carrying inside the sling bag.  With one camera body and one lens in the sling bag, you may be okay; but once you start adding extra lenses, flash, and other gear, your discomfort may increase.  As is also the case with how different backpacks may fit you with different levels of comfort, whether you find this sling bag's diagonal sling to be comfortable on your chest may ultimately be an important deciding factor in your purchasing decision.  If you frequently carry a "messenger bag" style of laptop bag (e.g. Timbuk2 laptop messenger bags) fully loaded with laptop and books, usually worn with its strap going diagonally across your chest, you should be okay with how this SlingShot feels.Both the SlingShot 200 and 202 models can carry both my Canon 7D with attached 17-55mm f/2.8 lens and Canon 40D with attached 70-200mm f/4L lens (with hoods reversed and no battery grip).  Basically, to convert this from a one-camera SlingShot to a two-camera setup, you rotate both cameras 90 degrees and rearrange the dividers on the bottom of the bag.  I added an image to the 'View and share related images' Customer Images gallery if you want to see what this looks like.  Unlike a regular backpack that uses shoulder straps, the front diagonal straps do exert more pressure on your chest as you load up more weight inside the sling bag, so you may not find this comfortable for carrying two cameras.  While I would not go on a 6-hour walking tour of a city always carrying both cameras inside my SlingShot, I may initially head out with both cameras stored inside and keep them stored as I get into cars/buses/airplanes.  And then once I am walking about, I will take out the 17-55mm camera, leaving the 70-200mm camera inside, ready for use.By far, the most important improvement in the new SlingShot 202, compared with the old 200 model, is the addition of the tripod buckle, cinch strap, and hideaway foldout tripod feet pouch on the side of the 202's bag.  On the 200, you had 3 SlipLock Attachment Loops, 2 on the back and 1 on the side, that you could use to sort of carry a tripod or monopod, but I never felt like it securely held my tripod in place.  But now with the cinch strap and foldout tripod feet pocket that holds the bottom of the tripod/monopod, this is a far more secure and neater configuration for carrying a tripod.  The tripod feet pocket is about 2.5 inches deep.  So you insert your tripod feet into this pouch and then buckle and tighten the top cinch strap.  A 22 or 24 inch long tripod feels balanced and secure when I carry the Slingshot on my back.  When I swing the bag to the front of my chest, the tripod is then positioned underneath the bag and it does not feel very loose because, most importantly, I tighten the top cinch strap very tight.  However, I really wished that Lowepro made this pouch deeper.  A tripod feet pocket that is 3.5 or 4.0 inches deep would have given a more secure fit to hold the bottom feet of the tripod.The 202 is a little more boxy and rigid than the previous 200 model.  You can set the 202 down on the ground or on a table in an upright position and it will stay standing upright by itself.  The bottom of the 200 was not as flat and could sometimes flop forward or backward if you tried to stand it upright on a flat surface.The SlingShot 202 has an extra zippered pocket in the top compartment's zippered flap for extra separate storage space.  In adding this pocket, the SlipLock Attachment Loop that used to be attached to the 200's top compartment's zippered flap is no longer there on the 202.  On the inside of the 202's top compartment's zippered flap, there is yet another zippered pocket, along with an elastic band for securely holding an item.  The top compartment on the 202 is also more roomier compared with the 200.The soft microfiber protective LCD monitor cloth has been repositioned from being sewn into the center edge of the main compartment's opening on the SlingShot 200, and is now moved over to the left edge of the main compartment's opening (on the left side when viewed from the perspective of having the bag slung in front of you and looking down into the main compartment's cavity).  This is nice in that the cloth flap does not get in the way as much when you are accessing the camera.  In both the 200 and 202, there is an elastic mesh pocket that can store the LCD monitor cloth if you want to tuck it away.I also have theLowepro Magnum 200 AW Shoulder Bag (Black), which is another excellent quality bag from Lowepro, and on that bag the microfiber protective LCD monitor cloth is attached to the inside wall of the bag using Velcro so that you can move the cloth to wherever you want it.  In addition, having a removable and relocatable LCD monitor cloth not only gives you flexibility in placement of the cloth, but also makes it far easier to wash the cloth if it gets dirty.  But on all of the first-generation and second-generation SlingShot models, this cloth is permanently sewn into the bag and you cannot move or remove it.  I would have MUCH preferred that this cloth was attached using Velcro the way that Lowepro's Magnum 200 AW was designed!On the inside lid of the main compartment, the 202 has two Velcro-closure memory card pockets.  But on the older SlingShot 200 model, there was actually a single larger Velcro-closure pocket and inside that main pocket were 8 separate elastic pockets for holding memory cards.  This is the only feature that I thought was actually better on the old 200 model compared with the new 202 bag, and I wish that Lowepro had retained the 200 bag's inside lid pocket and also used it on the 202 bag.  On the old 200 bag, this inside lid pocket could hold more CompactFlash cards compared with the 202 bag's two memory card pockets.  The only advantage that I can see for this redesign is that the two separate memory card pouches hold the cards more securely compared with opening up a larger pocket that stored more memory cards inside it.  But I still like the older pocket better!௫ Fuzzy Wuzzy's Conclusion:To summarize, in comparing this SlingShot 202 AW to the previous SlingShot 200 AW bag, the top compartment area's storage space was increased by adding two zippered pockets to the top compartment's zippered flap, and the top compartment, in general, is a bit larger.  The microfiber LCD monitor cloth was repositioned to move it out of the way more when accessing the camera.  And the inside lid's memory card pockets were redesigned.  But the most compelling reason to upgrade from a SlingShot 200 AW to this SlingShot 202 AW is the tripod strap and foot pouch on the side of the 202.  These differences between the 200 and 202 are better displayed and described on the 8 images that I added to the 'View and share related images' Customer Images gallery.  Overall, these are evolutionary, not revolutionary, improvements to an already-great sling bag! Buy with  confidence.  Very  pleased with this purchase. Provides great protection for my equipment  and love the  rain fly the comes from the base and covers the entire pack to  keep evrything dry when  caught in the rain

name: Polk Audio Atrium 4 80 Watt Outdoor Speaker (Black)
reviewText: For the size & price, these are my favorite speakers.  I use 4 of these speakers for our tailgate set-up.  They hit the high and mid-ranges very well.I use a subwoofer with these speakers in order to get the low end really well, but I suppose you could go without one. At $99, these are not the most expensive speakers I've ever bought, and of course not the biggest. At lower volumes you might think they're underpowered. But give them some juice. Everywhere between half-loud to uncomfortably loud you'll be shocked (seriously, shocked) at the clarity of the sound. These speakers sound great. I have one mounted on my deck and another on my patio. These have been mounted for a few months through cold and rain (they are both however underneath an eave) and still work like a charm. I purchased these speakers to pair with a Lepai LP-2020A+ digital amplifier on my screened-in and covered deck and the sound quality is amazing. I was a little concerned about low-end performance given the specs but the bass is reasonably good  - and exceptionally good for an all-weather speaker this small. I have them mounted about 10 feet apart and the stereo imaging and overall soundstage clarity is incredible for a pair of $99 outdoor speakers (my past experiences with outdoor speakers at any price point has been a noticeable compromise in sound in exchange for durability). None of that going on here; I highly recommend them for the intended outdoor use but at this price I would also recommend them for indoor bookshelf use (pair with a subwoofer if your amp supports it - the Lepai doesn't). All the other speakers around my house are JBL but I'll give Polk Audio serious consideration the next time I'm planning a speaker purchase. I live in the Great Smoky Mountains, where winters can get tough sometimes. These Polks, hanging under my open carport, have survived their first winter. I cranked 'em up this weekend to test my new Onkyo CD player, and they were THUMPIN'. The price was good and the quality is great. The supplied brackets made hanging them a snap. Mount them with the rears facing something solid to get the best bass.

name: Lowepro Toploader Zoom 50 AW (Black)
reviewText: I really like this bag for my Nikon D5100.  While it holds the Camera with 18-55mm standard lens, it will also easily accomodate my 55-300mm zoom too.  There is plenty of room in the front pocket for my SB-400 flash and the camera's battery charger. I really like the integral rain hood too.The bag is lightweight, unobtrusive, and (a big plus for me) has a belt-loop, which is my preferred way to carry my cameras.  Highly recommended Lowepro has the good reputaion on camera bags, but first I was very concerned about the size too small for Canon 60D & 18-135mm lens, while I didn't want a big toploader. After reading everybody's reviews here, I was convinced that it should work and I have given a try. Wow, it worked. It's big enough for the camera, or it may be a little tight to somebody else. For me, it is the perfect size. I can put my extra battery and hood in the front pocket, and memory cards inside the lid pocket. If I fly, it can be put in my suitcase or backpack. When the weather is bad, I can easily take pictures and put camera back to it for good protection. For light travellers, it's highly recommended to have this bag for Canon 60D.Update: I can carry 2 lenses: one with the camera in the bag, and another one like 70-300mm in lens bag attached. I can put 60D & 17-55mm F2.8 lens inside. I thought, only Tamron or Sigma 17-50mm f2.8 lens  would fit, and I really wanted to use it to carry my new general purpose lens. Glad to find out that I was wrong. Sturdy, dependable Lowepro construction. I use mine harnessed to my chest to make hiking and moving through brush easier. Both hands are free to carry a tripod or walking stick. My rating: 4.5 out of 5.  The reason is because I would have preferred the padding to be slightly thicker all-around, but the case still provides decent padding.The inside of the case has these measurements:7.5" vertical height from bottom of case without soft shelf.Dimensions of bottom of case is 4" x 3.5";  Dimensions of top of case is 5.5" x 4".INSIDE SPACE: The case comes with a soft shelf that attaches to the velcro sides on the inside. The shelf allows you to create a hidden space of 2" to 3" in height, leaving a 4" space above.  You can put a smaller device in the top for a better fit, or two different devices in the case.  I keep my Canon SX210 Digital Camera in the hidden space, and I put my Panasonic HD Camcorder in the top space.  The shelf can also be used as a divider to create space for two skinnier, but taller devices.POCKETS: There's a flat pocket in the top flap that measures 5" x 3" for fitting about 8 memory cards.There's a pocket in the front that can hold a digital camera, or a personal recording device, or battery and battery charger, or an A/C plug.PADDING: The base has a tough, thick padding, about 1/2" thick. The padding in the rest of the case is about 3/8" thick.  I would have preferred if the padding was either 1/2" thick all around, or even a 5/8" thick padding. It would have been a perfect case then, but it's still offers great protection.I don't use this case for my DSLR. It does fit my Canon XSi DSLR, but not with the lens attached.  I can store the 18-55 lens in the bottom space, and the body on the soft shelf.  The bottom won't hold the 55-200 lens, or the camera body.  It will only hold small lenses.This is an excellent case. The handle is tough and padded well.  The zippers are high quality, zip smoothly, and don't jam at all.  The shoulder strap is a flat, thin piece of fabric, not padded at all.  It's not really uncomfortable, but it would have been nice to have a padded strap.  The strap reaches a maximum of 20" down off the shoulder.  Other than the padding issue, this is a near perfect case based on my use.  4.5 out of 5. My Nikon D5000 with the Nikon 85mm f/3.5G AF-S DX ED VR Micro Nikkor Lens fits perfectly. The padding is rather thick, so protection against bumps and falls should be very good - not that I intend to test that anytime soon.The opening to the main compartment is comfortably large, and the little extra pocket for memory cards is useful, as is the smaller compartment on the front side (for filters, more memory cards, etc...).Rain protection is outstanding, with the foldable and stowable hood - typical LowePro quality.The only minor complaint I have is with the shoulder strap, which does not have any padding. No big deal, since you are not carrying around a ton of equipment in this thing.All in all a no-frills bag for special assignments, when you know that one lens is all you need.

name: Case Logic Qpb-201 Eva Molded Compact Camera Case (Black)
reviewText: We have several compact cameras in our family. Each has its own soft case, which is OK, but not so great at protecting the camera in a loaded overnight bag. That's where the Case Logic QPB-201 EVA Molded Compact Camera Case shines. Its hard shell protects the camera (and a few small accessories) in the most crowded bag, and makes it easy to just toss it into any bag, instead of finding a safe corner for it. We have two Canon Sureshots, an Olympus and a Fuji, and all fit quite nicely. (one at a time, that is.) The Canons are on the smaller size, and the case will accommodate the camera, a folded lens cloth and a couple of extra batteries, as well as the usual SD cards, which have their own little pocket. One of the camera's chargers is also small enough to fit into the case, so there's only one item to keep track of when you're traveling.I haven't used the belt loop - I usually keep the camera and case in a bag with a lot of other stuff we carry while we travel. Though Case Logic makes no claims about this product being waterproof, it did survive a water bottle spill inside a tote bag - I was very happy about that. No water made it into the interior, and the exterior just wiped dry. Overall, I'm very happy with this case. For the price, you couldn't do better. name: Lowepro Passport Sling Camera Bag (Black)
reviewText: Just a little bit expensive for a non-waterproof and only one room for camera. Well it wont be so cool if they make it bigger.Good look. I got this for a trip to Disneyland to hold some essential gear while on the trip. I keep my camera on a carryspeed strap so the bag only had lenses, remote trigger, batteries, cleaning cloths, and ND filters It turns out that this bag has replaced my backpack style camera pack altogether. it's so much easier to get into I couldn't go back to the backpack. It looks like a regular messenger bag. I can fit my Canon Rebel T2i, lens or Diana Mini, and Canon AE-1 Program in the bigger side pocket. Although the big pocket isn't padded, my AE-1 is a tank so it doesn't need padding. This is a great travel  bag for one small DSLR and lens/small cameras like a toy camera or point & shoot. Great bang for the buck. Also, the main pocket expands so I can fit a book. I really like the bag. It fits my Sony A77 DSLR with 18-200mm lens attached. However if you have a battery grip attached, it will not fit. But overall it is alright. The extra space is indeed a great idea. Like others have said this bag doesn't come off looking like a camera bag. A uniquely shaped messenger bag? Sure, but it doesn't shout 'camera', which was my main draw to it. Plus the position of the bag gives it the convenience of a hip holster without having to look like your tourist father. When I know I'm going to be doing some intermittent shooting as I walk around places I'll keep my camera 'holstered' in the bag with the zipper open for easy and quick access. The sturdiness of the padding makes this an easy and secure way to go about shooting. I could still fit more, and sometimes do when carrying non-camera items.Plenty of room, slim profile, discrete, all for 35 bucks. Definitely a purchase I'm happy with.

name: Celestron 71008 SkyMaster 25x70 Binocular (Black)
reviewText: Many pros, the only cons are the weight and size, both of which are obvious from the start. I'd probably recommend something a little smaller. When Comet Ison was headed toward the sun and reports were coming out that if it survives it will put on a heck of a show I figured I would get these since I had been wanting a set anyway.  Well the comet didn't survive, but my spotting scope was also in pieces so this is its replacement.  They are fairly sharp and contrasty, not as good as my Nikon Actions, but not bad. The only real problems I have noticed is that the tripod adapter allows a lot of movement, but most don't even come with one so I can't complain there, and that when you focus from far to near you may have to reset the compensator because one side doesn't always move as much as the other.  For the price it will work just fine. I purchased the Celestron 71008 SkyMaster 25x70 Binoculars on a whim when they were available for $59.99. I already own several pairs of binoculars including the Celestron 15x70 SkyMasters. The 25x70 SkyMasters are very powerful, and have decent optics. There are several drawbacks though. The 25x70 Skymasters have a very narrow field of view, even compared to the 15x70's. For astronomical use, you're going to need a good tri-pod, as they are very heavy, and next to impossible to hold steady enough by hand. Even with a good tri-pod, the included tri-pod bracket is not very good, and will cause the binoculars to shake with any kind of vibration. The optics on the binoculars are good, but not great. In this price range, the optics are more than satisfactory. If you're on a budget and looking for very powerful binoculars, then I recommend the 25x70's as long as you know the limitations. Personally, I think the Celestron 15x70 SkyMasters are a better choice. They have a much wider field of view, and are a little easier to use without a tri-pod.Edit: Just to add 1 tip. Regardless if you wear eyeglasses or not, if you roll down the eyecups, you'll get a much wider/better field of view. The eyecups aren't an issue on the 15x70 Skymasters, but rolling them down on the 25x70's makes a great deal of difference. Product is not worth the money, I am not an expert in bino's, buy have some basic ones. this one is no good at all, returned it the same day. Cheap is not always the best. Delivery was super fast, and they work and look great. Not as heavy as I thought and the eye piece can be changed. This product is excellent.

A basic little high-quality case at a very good inexpensive price, it fits my Canon SD-series point-n-shoot camera very well.  I have even sometimes used it to carry my iPod Touch and earbuds. It's thick too and I really feel safe about throwing the camera in my travel bag before vacations and not worrying about it getting beat up in transit.Good looks, low price and great functionality - they nailed this one. We have been using this with our digital ELPH camera, and it has been a perfect fit.The gray color is sufficiently neutral to look good with anything.

name: Philips SHS3200BK/37 Flexible Earhook Headphones, Black
reviewText: Surprisingly good sound from these, and they stay in your ear pretty well, also.FH Very good sound, for the price tag. I'd definitely recommend this product to anyone looking for good sounding earbuds with a good looking price.Feel free to leave a comment if you have a question or just want to share your thoughts.
