name: Fotodiox Lens Mount Adapter Minolta MD/ MC Rokkor Lens to Nikon Camera for Nikon D7100 D7000 D5200 D5100 D3100 D300 D300S ...
reviewText: While I have never used the more expensive German equivalent this far less costly adapter holds lens and camera securely and allows focus to infinity on the several Minolta MD/MC lenses with which I have tried it on my Panasonic micro 4/3. In fact I have enjoyed using those old and very high quality lenses (I also have Leica and Nikon adapters from the same makers) on the LCD based camera that I bought a micro 4/3 dSLR with an actual, albeit electronic, viewfinder so I can use these lenses in daylight (it is impossible to manually focus off an LCD screen on the back of a camera in bright light) and not under vampire conditions. Adapter didn't fit any of my Minolta lenses. Was a solid fit on my Nikon, but none of the lenses would fit. Sent back. This Fotodiox Adapter does exactly what it's supposed to do, and for a reasonable price. It's nice to bring some good (old) lenses out of storage. I bought this for use on my Nikon D7000.  I have a lot of old Minolta camera bodies and lenses that were my grandfathers.  Some are also Tokina made for the Minolta.  Yes, I was able to attach the lenses to my Nikon.  Yes, I had to use manual focus (as expected).  However, even on manual focus I was not able to get any clear shots with any of my lenses.  I had high hopes that I would be able to get something with manual focus but unfortunately I think those lenses are just going to have to stay in their old leather bag.  For me, it was a waste of money.  The product itself is well made, did not wobble on my camera, and held the lenses just fine.  I think its more of an internal problem having to do with the way that the Nikon is made.  It was a gamble and I lost lol The Fotodiox adapter is certainly a decent piece of hardware for the money. The engineering is very good with one exception; The connection to the Nikon body is very good, but the connection to the Minolta/Rokkor lens, or any other third party lenses I had with the Minolta mount, are a bit loose. I wouldn't say it affects the captured images in any way, but it'd feel better if it were a bit more secure. It's hard to evaluate the included glass element, as there was no way for me to test the Rokkor lenses without the adapter on the Nikon, and the only images I had, were from a Minolta SRT-101 film body. You can, however, remove the glass element and shoot in a macro style although you can't focus to much of anything that isn't very close to the lens. When I compared images shot with a Rokkor 28mm 2.8 or a Rokkor 58mm 1.4 to a Nikkor equivalent, naturally, the Nikkor lenses were sharper, but nothing you'd see if you were posting images to the web or printing something less than an 8x10. Overall, I'm pleased with the Fotodiox adapter and happy to use my old Minolta lenses again.

name: Logitech H110 Wired On Ear Headphones With Mic, Stereo With Noise-Cancelling,3.5-Mm Dual Audio Jack, Pc/Mac/Laptop- Black
reviewText: I have several headsets at home: a more expensive Logitech, a Plantronics, and a Creative Labs headset.Apparently, this one sounds better than all of the others. It's a dead-simple headset, with no switches or knobs, and yet it sounds good for music, and the microphone is very good for voice chat.If you're thinking "cheap can't be good," this is definitely the exception to that rule. Great product. Reasonably good price range. Amazone provide the cheaper price compare to other available sources.Provide excellent sound,easy to handle,portable.I use it in my home and lab. For the price you can't beat this headset. Works great with ICQ, EchoLink and TeamSpeak 3. The only complaint I have is that it does not trigger the vox circuitry in TeamSpeak. Other than that, it's a really good low priced headset. Used for two-way webinars and works perfectly.  Is a better option to using separate speakers and microphone.  No complaints or issues to report. For the price this is a pretty decent headset by logitech. It doesn't feel cheap, it works, has decent sound, records in stereo great...Definitely a good buy for people on budgets...

name: Celestron 93524 Binocular Tripod Adapter (Black)
reviewText: I bought this for my Father along with binoculars and a tripod, this is a solid metal piece that should be much more sturdy than the plastic adapter his binoculars came with (reviews indicated that the plastic adapter flexed at a simple touch or bump which meant shaky viewing) so I am hoping for better viewing stability, and the delivery was fast. I will follow up IF there is a problem, but at this point very pleased. This easy-to-mount item, complements my Skymaster 15 x 70's and mates them perfectly to a Vista Explorer 60" tripod, which had been a missing ingredient for night-time viewing in particular. This basic outfit is working out rather well in that respect! It's sturdy.  Very sturdy.  It's easy to use.  It handles the bigger/heavier binocular sizes without giving me trust issues.  I recomment this item if you are mounting binos larger than 10 x 50 on a tripod. I bought a pair of Celestron 71199 Cometron 12x70 binoculars and they came with a plastic tripod adapter. The binoculars shook like a bobble head doll on it. This adapter is solid metal & the extended thumb screw makes it easier to mount than the plastic one provided. I took one star away because I feel there is too little threading to go into the binoculars. I snug my up but am careful to not over tighten for fear of stripping the threads. Also because this is what should come with such a big pair of binoculars. I used these on a pair of 10x36 monarchs and that I use for daytime viewing.  I didn't even know they were tripod capable until I saw this product and I was not disappointed.  I have used this also as a makeshift rest on any flat surface when I don't have a tripod with me with good results.

name: Micca M-8S 8 Inch 2-Way in-Wall Speaker with Pivoting 1" Silk Dome Tweeter (Each, White)
reviewText: i had an in wall speaker that the crossover went bad. i ordered this one to replace it pulled the old one out 15 min. replaced it with the M-8S TOOK ME TEN MIN. works and sounds great i'm usinig it for a high front speaker. I highly recomend this speaker. I would give these speakers and A rating! Put them in the walls of a large master bedroom. The sound really impressed me. The key to mounting these wall and ceiling speakers is to leave a boxed area behind them with white poly foam. I got my foam in a roll at Michaels. Just goes to show you dont need to spend a lot of money. Ive bought more now for other rooms. I could get by without a yamaha woofer but probably may buy a small one. thou i dont think I need it. Highly reccomend! Very nice speakers at any price. However, at this price, amazing speakers. Note that they are priced each, and not by the pair. Got these speakers about 5 months ago.  Using a pair in the ceiling for my flat screen TV (that alone has terrible sound).  I read a lot of reviews for many different products and this Micca speaker was relatively new with few reviews.  But I took the chance considering the $45 per speaker which is roughly half of "high-end" competitor speakers.  I followed instructions (and other reviews) by surrounding the speakers with insulation, which was a bit of a chore considering there is a fairly large cavity between the ceiling drywall and the second floor sub flooring above.  My main concern was sound resonating through the floor of the second floor, as I have a small child.  I doubled up the insulation, which mostly did the trick.  The "problem" that we had with the bass thumping a bit upstairs is essentially a good "problem" to have as these speakers really do produce a crisp low end bass.  Even with standard (non-subscription) Pandora, and a cheap amplifier, the sound quality is incredible.  I plan on adding a wi-fi enabled receiver which should increase the sound quality even more, but even for now, we are very pleasantly pleased with the sound quality.  The only drawback I found was the construction of the mounting brackets.  Be sure you get the screws PERFECTLY lined up prior to drilling them in place.  If they are just a slight bit off alignment, you could strip the bracket and lose the function of that bracket.  But outside of this, I totally recommend this speaker.  Great boom for your buck! I'm not an audiophile and I've never had any other in-wall speakers, but these things sound good to me for $45/piece.I hooked up two of these to an old receiver and it was groovy. Install was probably 1 hour a speaker including running cable in my walls.Install is pretty easy with the included template. I recommend you tape down the template, drill holes in each corner of the template and then cut the walls with your drywall saw.I did buy some fiberglass insulation (ie. the "Pink Stuff") and stuffed a few layers behind each speaker. I didn't try them without the insulation, as the manufacturer recommends you insulate the speakers. It makes intuitive sense to me to insulate them.I thought the mounting brackets and grille on the speakers are a little jenky, but for the price I can live with it.

name: Monoprice 105346 1.5-Feet RCA Plug Cable for DVD Player (Black)
reviewText: I really needed TWO cables separate.  Doing an NTSC video installation for security camera.  No problem.  Just pull these apart.  You might have to snip the little piece of heat shrink (which is there to prevent splitting accidentally) but then you can just pull it apart.  Nice connectors.  Great price! Is as Described. Theres not much to say about this product.Pros:It worksGood qualityGood PricePrime eligible (for all amazon junkies like me)Cons:None yetBottom line: I recommend this product... Nice cable, and the perfect length to connect my DAC to my Little Dot Amp.  I wish the cables were a bit more flexible, but once they settled into place they stayed put,  They were a bit tight when pushing them onto the jacks for the first time, but they got easier after that.  Can't really beat them for the quality and price.Update:  After using this cable for a while, the ends have loosened up to the point that they can slide off of the jacks far too easily, and have actually slid off on several occasions as the wire tried to return to its original bend.  I am changing my review to 3 stars at this point. These are definitely a good quality cable. They were a great length for what I needed. My only complaint would be that they were a bit stiff. Very stiff cable. Very stiff connectors. I feel like I'm going to break the connector in the back of my CD player putting these cables in.The work...just allow lots of space behind your device.

name: AmazonBasics Wireless Remote Control for Nikon - D5300, D750, D5000, D5100, D5200, D7000, D3300, D3200, D3000, P6000, P7000
reviewText: Working well with my Nikon D90 Well, it's a remote with only one button, so there is not much to write, but it works very well with my camera.  The maximum distance I tried was about 18 feet.  Great for long shutter speed shots. I tried one of these for my 6D and it works fine.  I never used the canon brand one, but I have used original nikon brand ones on my nikon equipment and this works as well as the nikon brand one does.  I expect that this works as well as the canon brand one does too.  If that makes sense. Hi,Pros:  Inexpensive, works wellCons:  Weak signal strengthI bought this remote as a replacement for my lost Nikon-branded remote for my D80. Perhaps it's the battery that came with it, but the signal strength is *not* 16 feet as described. It's more like 4 feet.Also, this remote fires constantly when pressed, unlike the Nikon remote. This is important if you're shooting bracketed exposures, as you might accidentally shoot one too many. All in all, I'm happy with my purchase! I was very pleased--This remote was easy to use right out of the package.  I didn't have to program anything! All I had to do was set my camera to remote mode, and it worked right away.  Be aware that if you let it sit idle too long, you may have to reset the camera to the right mode again.Now it's easy to take a family picture--in fact several in a row--without having to run back to the camera.The description says the remote has a 16 foot range.  We tried it out both inside and outside.  The range inside the house seemed more like 20 feet.  Outside the range wasn't quite as far, yet still adequate.It's great to have the velvet carrying case; however, it left lint all over the place.  So be careful if you plan on storing it next to your camera.  In fact, be sure you don't have lint on your fingers before you touch your camera.Overall, the remote is easy to use, and I'm happy with it.

name: Logitech B100 Wired USB Mouse, 3 yr Warranty, 800 DPI Optical Tracking, Ambidextrous PC/Mac/Laptop - Black
reviewText: ***UPDATE******POSSIBLE FIX***7-14-12I usually don't use a mouse pad with my mouse as I'm used to using it across the top of my desk because its a smooth surface and the mouses optical laser usually responds. Well I was still having that random double clicking problem so I said it wouldn't hurt to see if a mouse pad would help. Lo and Behold the random double clicking started to cease. It may occur once here and there but its slowly stopping. Today I've only had one instance of a random double click. I guess since my desk has a slightly gloss finish on top it was like using a mouse on a mirror. The mouse probably was in a way *seeing* double so every time I clicked it just obeyed both optical streams it saw. That's just a guess though. So I recommend trying a mouse pad with your mouse. The mouse may not be totally useless. I'm going to give it another star since I believe this was not the mouse's error but mine.*ORIGINAL POST*This mouse was good while it lasted. Bought it in May and it just started that random double-clicking people mentioned. I'll grin and bear it till I can get a better mouse. Unfortunately for me this didn't last as long as I expected it to. It makes me think I would have been better off with a mouse from an off brand company. Usually Logitech has pretty sturdy and dependable devices. I still have other mouses by them that have lasted me for years. Hopefully Logitech will look into whether this is a hardware issue or a glitch with the drivers. Either way it was okay while it lasted. I've never been a big fan of the fancy, ergonomic mice when a cheap one works just fine for me. Buttons click, wheel rolls, can't complain. I bought this for my brother. He is into computer games and when his wireless broke this was the replacement. Cheap and fast shipping. I have two of these and they both work well.  I would recommend them as a good, cost effective mouse for everyday use. Very pleased with these. I rebuild 'puters and give these away with the machines. No failures, perfect performance. That reminds me... I have to reorder.

name: Edimax EW-7811Un Wi-Fi USB Adapter (Black and Gold)

name: BlueRigger Ultra Series (Braided/Nylon) HDMI Cable Supports 4K@60HZ, FullHD, Ultra HD, 3D High Speed with Ethernet, ARC, P...
reviewText: The nylon braided cable is slick and it slides all over the place. I made the error of buying a cable that's too long, so maybe this isn't a big problem if the cable is the proper/shorter length. Also, there's no marking to indicate the side of the connector that should be face up when inserted which would help.If you're working in a well-lit area and have the device up on a table where you can clearly see the ports, the slick cable and lack of markings on the connector probably are not issues. But I think most people try to connect everything where the device lives and without disconnecting everything already attached to it. Works really well. Thanx Very robust cable with a heavy re-enforced fabric jacket and heavy plugs.  Works great to send 1080p to my projector. I've ordered two of the 25ft cables over the last few months and am very happy with their performance. I run a cable from my PC to my HDTV in the living room and the video quality is amazing! I really like the braided Nylon as it offers more flexibility than plastic cables. Don't go for Monster or any other cable unless you feel like spending unnecessary money for inferior quality. Ordered 2 of these. One works as it should, the other arrived DOA. Very concerning. Makes me wonder how long the other one will last.The cables themselves are very flexible. The mesh wrap is cool. Picture quality is indistinguishable from a more expensive cable in my current setup.The cables are Made in China (like 99% of HDMI cables).BlueRigger needs to up their quality control, and by 'up' i mean they need to have quality control.

name: BlueRigger Ultra Series (Braided/Nylon) HDMI Cable Supports 4K@60HZ, FullHD, Ultra HD, 3D High Speed with Ethernet, ARC, P...
reviewText: Have a bunch of blue rigger HDMI cables and never had a problem with them. I purchased this cable to replace a cable that I purchased at Fry's because the connector end broke off after just a few weeks.I use this cable to connect my PS3 to my TV, so that I can keep the console close to the couch, so I was looking for something low cost yet something that wouldn't break easily.When I received the cable, I was very surprised at the cool high-tech look of the cable material and the strength of the connection for the connector ends to the cable.  I first gently pulled on the end and then pulled harder and harder, and there was no effect.  I connected the cable to my PS3 and TV, and the picture is perfectly clear and vibrant.  I also played a bluray disk on the PS3, and it looked great on the tv.So, low cost, great looks, strong connectors, and nice picture = 5 stars for me. Work really well. Thanx These cables are outstandingly well made.  1/10th the price of Monster cables for the same length, just under double the price of the cheapest cables on Amazon for the same length, overall very satisfactory. As usual, I'll start with the good.  We used this product to connect a DVR to an HDTV, and we couldn't be happier.  The connectors themselves are quite nice and snap snugly into each device.  We didn't test more than two speakers for the audio, but what did come through was not being hindered by the cable.  No video artifacts or stutters.Now for the bad, although these are hardly reasons to knock the rating.  The plastic around the connectors extends quite a ways around the connector itself, such that I could see how it might cause problems in tight situations.  Also, the cable is reasonably inflexible.  That's not to say it shouldn't fit around tight corners, but you might want to think twice before you put the cable in that situation.Overall, we would highly recommend this cable.  Before this purchase, we had never heard of BlueRigger.  After the purchase, we would not hesitate to recommend this brand.  Not to mention that we can't really complain about the price.

name: CMVision IR110 - 114 LED Indoor/Outdoor Long Range 200-300ft IR Illuminator With Free 3A 12VDC Adaptor
reviewText: It works as expected. The casing is all metal. Seems very heavy duty. If you're mounting it as in the picture, it almost seems like you get more like vertically, rather than horizontally. You can of course fully adjust the articulation of the illuminator.It's difficult for me to really gauge the operation of this, as the area I need to illuminate has a wood fence and the illuminator is attempting to illuminate something behind the fence. What happens for me is I get huge contrast of light reflecting off the fence. Not really anything I can do about that, because for that area there's nowhere else to mount the light.Very well made product and worth the money. I would definitely buy this again. I'm thinking about one for another area already. I use this to throw more IR down my driveway at night.  It really extends the useable night time range of my camera over the limited number of IR LEDs the camera has built into it. When I started looking for something like this, I thought it would be hundreds of dollars, but this is exactly what I need, it draws less than 10 watts and it works perfectly. I'm using it with a Foscam 8910 and it lights up the night. I'm considering adding a couple more around my house. The sticker on it said QC Tested. When I hooked it up to the power supply nine of the led's did not light up. But even with 9 led's out it does increase the night vision distance of my security camera. I got this to use with my D-Link DCS-2332L.  It is the right wavelength and looks promising, it lights up a good 50' or more of my patio, but a few half-rows of LEDs didn't light up out of the box, so it's going back.  It would probably work even better if the whole thing lit up!  If anyone can recommend something similar but better quality let me know!

name: Nikon HB-50 Lens Hood for AF-S NIKKOR 28-300mm f/3.5-5.6G ED VR
reviewText: As a lens hood for the 28-300mm, it does what it says.  But I'm on my third one, as it is poorly designed, falls off all the time when carried in place, and is delicate and easily broken.  At $35/pop to replace, it's expensive for a bit of plastic.  Does anyone know of either a) a metal replacement, or b) a cheaper source, even if non-Nikon?I have a bunch of Nikon lenses, including the whole f/2.8 zoom kit, and I've never broken or lost another lens hood in a fair bit of traveling and shooting hanging off ropes and rigging.  This one seems more cheaply made and more delicate than the others.  Yeah, the pro lenses start at 2x as much, and go up from there, but on the other hand, $1000 is not exactly a cheap lens.  It'd be nice if the lens hood was a little sturdier. Nikon got cheap with the quality of this lens hood.  My original one was loose and it broke after only a few uses.  This is just one of those somewhat necessary evils we sometime need to have.  Check out all the blogs on the internet about the quality of this product. The original Nikon HB-50 shade for the 28-300mm Nikon lens felt shoddy when I first held it, and it locked all right when I first put it on the barrel. It uses a bayonet mount, but the shade is plastic. For an extra several dollars, one would think that Nikon would make the shade carbon fiber or out of metal. But I speculate that they simply want people to buy these shades when (not if) they break.This shade reaches well in front of the lens but does a great job in blocking unwanted flare that hits the lens, whose elements sit right beneath the lip of the barrel. When the lens is set at 300mm, it reaches even farther out, begging someone to hit it. My shade broke when it finally fell off the camera after constantly mounting and removing it (another issue), but the problem is that now, the front element is exposed to being struck.I usually don't want to get a product that is rated at two stars, but what alternative does one have? It sucks raw eggs, but I need this inferior product on the lens. Nikon, shame on you for making something necessary, so very crappy. Photographers deserve better, and so does your name. Fits snug and is attractive on the lens build quality is good easy decision. Always better to go with the hood made for the lens to avoid things such as vignetting. I've never had a hood break in 30 years of photography, but the one that came with my camera did break.  So far this hood has not broken, which is good.  Otherwise, what can I say, it does what a hood is supposed to do.

name: Lowepro S&F 75 AW Quick Flex Pouch (Black)

name: Polk Audio TL1600 RCA 100 Watt 5.1 Channel Wired Speaker (Black)
reviewText: This is a great sound system if you are looking for a full 5.1 setup (speakers only). I bought this for our game room so it's not our main a/v setup. I'm very fussy about the quality of my audio so I was a little wary about spending so little on speakers (the most important and most under-rated part of any a/v system. My overall impression is that this is an excellent system, especially if you are looking for inconspicuous speakers for your home-theater. The system comes with four TL1 satellite speakersPolk Audio TL 1 Sat Speaker (Each, Black), a matched central speaker and a powered subwoofer.  Setup is easy enough (some reviews of the TL1 systems complain about the cable posts but frankly I saw nothing that caused me any concerns - I was easily able to connect each speaker with Monster Xp-CI cable. My one and only complaint is the mounting of the speakers to the wall: there is a small keyhole to hang the speaker from a screw you put into the wall (not supplied); this provides a terrible mount and the speakers really should be supplied with a mounting bracket. They are compatible with most universal mounts so expect to buy four mounts (one for each satellite). I don't know what the folks at Polk Audio were thinking by leaving the mount out but this seams to me to be penny wise and pound foolish (to quote an old English expression). That aside, the sound quality from this setup is nothing short of excellent. I'm powering the system from my old Yamaha RX-V2095 receiver which has excellent sound reproduction. The highs are crystal clear and the bass, once you adjust the subwoofer appropriately is clear and deep. The midrange is excellent for the size of the speakers. I did consider the much more expensive Bose system but to my ear this clearly sounds better and comes at a much better price. Excellent home theater speakers for a small room, only downside is that you need to buy cables separately but some users might find this as a pro. Very nice and good looking speakers. Sound is crisp and provide enough quality sound to any HD sound source.  They are not the smallest speakers in the market but, they are small enough to be part of my living room Excellent sound quality. I paired with a yamaha self-tuning receiver and couldn't be happier. Plenty of sound for a small/mid size apartment. Clear, clean, crisp, full sound - I can hear all the music - and these speakers do not mush the sound together - each part is easily heard.  Great value for the price.

name: Lowepro LP36214 Adventura Ultra Zoom 100 Shoulder Bag (Black)
reviewText: This bag is too big for a basic point and shoot camera and too small for a professional camera.  It is called Aventura Ultra Zoom because it is made to fit those cameras specifically. I like that it has both a shoulder strap and a handle. It is a basic bag with protective padding and a very orange interior which includes three small inside pockets.  Two are clearly for flash cards and one side interior pocket looks like it would hold an extra battery.  I like the movable/removable divider piece with its very strong Velcro and the softness of the inside fabric.  Nothing will get scratched in here. I did a lot of hunting around to find a decent, fairly compact protective case or bag for my Sony alpha Nex-5N.  The Nex-5N is fairly beefy for a point and shoot, especially with the 18-55mm zoom lens attached.  Thankfully, the Nex-5N fits snugly in this case inserted on it's side, even with the 18-55mm lens and flash attached.  It's not perfect, but it has been very difficult to find a workable and not overly-huge case for this particular camera, so I'm quite happy with it.  If you are looking for a case for the Nex-5N or a similar Nex model, keep in mind this case isn't going to hold more than the camera body, whatever lens you have attached, a memory card and maybe a spare battery. I bought this bag for my Sony NEX-F3 and it fits perfectly. The camera is well protected against shock by the extra padding of this bag and there is extra space for batteries and memory cards. Should you drop the bag or fall while carrying it, your camera will survive the incident and isn't that one of the benefits of buying a quality camera bag in the first place. The bag is easy to open and with the top raised it is very easy to quickly grab the camera and start shooting. Don't try to save a few dollars buying a cheaper bag and risk damage to your camera. This is a nice case with lots of storage for those looking for a case for a digital camera that has extended zoom lense.  Wish that it had another piece of adjustable fabric in it to make the camera fit a little more secure inside the case as the one piece was not quite big enough to make the camera feel secure and that it would not move around inside the case while walking with it. This little bag holds the camera, one battery and two sd cards inside with no room to spare. The camera fits with the lens hood, thumb rest and JB grip case on. I use the  detachable divider in the front  to provide a little more security, so the camera doesn't fall out.  I've had it long enough that it has stretched out a little and the camera goes in and out easily.  The little pocket on the back is good for cards, another battery or any thing really small and light.  I also like the handle on the top, which makes it easy to grab the case without flinging it around with the strap.My only complaint about this, and many other small bags, is the lack of a shoulder pad or some effort to make it less prone to sliding around on the one's shoulder.Try it you'll like it.

name: Nikon EN-EL15 Rechargeable Li-Ion Battery for Select DSLR Cameras (Retail Packaging)

name: Xpand X103 Universal Active Shutter 3D Glasses
reviewText: Now its a given every set of glasses acts differently with different hardware.  These Glasses actually do work with the Epson projectors i have an Epson PowerLite Home Cinema 3010.here is the review essentially and make of it what you will.The glasses are wonderfully comfortable and its a shame the rest did not match up.  They fit nice with a good amount of bend and they do not have issues with to much frame being visible.  They also sit on the nose extermely well.That being said its the only great part of the glasses.1.) they do not sync when just turned on.  If its documentation that was missing from my shipment thats  possible but I had to fiddle with it to get it to sync.  Essentially when I first turned it on it would sync for 2 seconds and then lose sync and the IR emitter position is not the problem as 2 epson and 1 sony worked just fine.To get it to work you have to turn them on let them fail and then tap the power button 1 time ( do not hold as they will turn off ).  This sometimes synced first try sometimes second or third but it always worked.  I could of lived with this.2.) The major downfall of the glasses in my evaluation of them was extreme ghosting or crosstalk.  It was very easy to see the other frame in the other eye to the point you could very easily notice it on contrasted areas.  It seemed that the refresh rate was bad on the glasses they just do not get that opaque in comparison to others.  This is a catch 22 with glasses currentl on the market since it was also a pair of glasses that seemed to have less of a tint than the sony or epson glasses.If it wasnt for the crosstalk I could justify a 4 but then again if it wasnt for how comfortable the glasses are I would have given them a 2. These are much better glasses than the Panasonic brand. They are lighter, more comfortable and do a better job on top of eye glasses. I even prefer the long lasting coin cell batteries over the rechargeable ones in the Panasonic. It is great that they will work with other TV's as well. Just compared to a Panasonic glasses that my friend had gotten last year with his TV, and I couldn't tell the difference. It take ssome times to get used to it, and turning on and off is more complicated than it should be, so i take off a star. Given the price, it is great. I like these glasses better than the 2nd gen Panasonic glasses on my GT25 plasma TV. They are slightly brighter and sit closer to my eyes on the bridge of my nose, not to mention cheaper. It took a few minutes to determine which settting was the correct one for Panasonic 3D, but once it was set once no additional programming was required. (One of the pairs was defective and could not be programmed, but Amazon promptly exchanged them for a new pair which worked fine.) Definitely seems like the best option for universal glasses, since Xtend seems to be the manufacturer of most of the TV OEM glasses. These are a good, less expensive alternative to the pricey OEM glasses. Mine are for a Panasonic Viera TC-P50GT25 (also purchased here). Good responsiveness, and cross-talk is minimal. Rear reflections are a slight more significant than the OEM glasses, but in a dark room...it's hardly noticeable.A good buy at half the cost of OEM glasses.

name: Plugable USB 2.0 to 10/100 Fast Ethernet LAN Wired Network Adapter for MacBook Chromebook Windows 8 and Earlier Surface Pr...
reviewText: I was looking for a simple and quick way to connect my mother's older computer to my home wired network when she would visit...this product worked great for that......I'm now able to "help" her update all those software packages she uses. Non eventful installation on an android tv box hooked up to my 55" tv. All I can say is that I plugged this in to the android tv box and my network router and turned on the tv box. Just to make sure, I connected this adapter to my MacBook Pro... of course it works. name: Case Logic SLR Camera Holster
reviewText: இ Fuzzy Wuzzy's Summary:ѾѾѾ Somewhat recommended, with reservations and only lukewarm fuzzies.I love using SLR camera holster bags like this for shorter day outings where I do not want to be weighed down more by the bulk of a larger shoulder camera bag, camera backpack, or camera sling bag.  As long as you are not needing to carry multiple camera bodies or lenses, camera holsters are perfect for shoot-and-scoot situations like walking tours of a city, hiking in the woods or mountains, and social gatherings with family or friends.This is a very basic camera holster in very crowded price range filled with better options.  The primary reason that I rated this holster only 3 stars is that, in the $20-$30 price range, there are better offerings from Case Logic, Lowepro, and Tamrac, among others.  This is a nicely made holster.  But once you also consider the other holster options in this price range, this holster looks to be fairly "average".  With internal dimensions of 5.7"x4.6"x6.25", I can snugly fit my Canon 7D and 17-55mm f/2.8 lens (without a battery grip, but with a tripod plate attached).  So your non-full-frame SLR camera will likely fit inside this, unless you are using a battery grip or require it to hold a 70-200mm lens.  There are two zippered pockets on each side of the holster, and another zippered pocket on the inside of the zippered lid.  The padding around all sides of this holster is adequate and comparable to other camera holsters.  The bottom of the holster is padded thicker than the sides, and that is a good thing since the bulk of the camera weight may be resting on it.All zippers and stitching are high quality.  But the top grab handle is only secured with one line of stitching on each side, and I think that the stitching of this top grab handle could become loose over time with repeated grabbing and lifting by that handle.The holster comes with a very basic 1-inch wide unpadded shoulder strap.  A simple unpadded shoulder strap like this is fine for carrying a compact SLR or point-and-shoot camera.  But it becomes more uncomfortable on your shoulder when carrying around a larger, heavier SLR camera for extended periods.  This lack of padding and rubbing of the strap can be especially apparent if you are just wearing a thin shirt, blouse, or t-shirt.The shoulder strap uses plastic clips that secure to the holster's plastic D-rings.  While I prefer metal D-rings instead of plastic D-rings for durability, I really dislike these kinds of plastic clips when used on a holster like this where you may be frequently clipping and unclipping the shoulder strap, depending upon whether you want to attach the holster to your belt or sling it around your shoulder.  Over time, the plastic clip can fatigue and bend or break with repeated use by pressing down on the plastic.  This will not be an issue if you always leave the shoulder strap attached to the holster, but it is something to consider.Within this price range and staying with the Case Logic brand, I think that theirCaselogic SLRC-201 SLR Zoom Holster (Black)is a far better holster than this one.  It has a larger internal dimensions of 6.3"x4.7"x6.9" than this holster, and includes a shoulder strap that is generously padded around your shoulder.  But on that holster, even though I like its shoulder strap clips better than the totally plastic clips used on this holster, its shoulder strap clips onto fabric loops instead of metal or plastic D-rings.  I prefer D-rings over a fabric loop for clipping a shoulder strap onto.Within this price range and looking at other competing products, you should also consider the Lowepro "Toploader Zoom" line of holsters.  I like their designs better than this holster because they offer more useful storage pockets, and their "AW" All-Weather models come with a rain cover that fully protects the holster in case it rains.  You will get a temporary amount of rain protection using this Case Logic holster (e.g. for darting across parking lots during a heavy rain), but the water will soak through the zippers and seams.  Some people do not think about how rainproof their camera case will be... until they get caught out in the open during a torrential downpour.  To protect my investment in three camera bodies and seven lenses, I only buy camera holsters, backpacks, sling bags, and shoulder bags that offer full rain protection for my SLR cameras.  If you carry your expensive SLR camera around as much as I do, then you will realize that you do not have to live in the Pacific Northwest to eventually get rained upon unexpectedly.If you have a SLR camera that costs many hundreds of dollars or more, you may want to go beyond this price range for a better holster.  In the $50-$100 price range, I am a big fan of the Think Tank "Digital Holster" and Lowepro "Toploader Pro" holsters.  Both of these product lines come with top-notch design and build quality, flexible storage options, heavy-duty comfortably padded shoulder straps with metal snap clips that attach to metal D-rings, rain protection, and an expandable component-based approach that lets you attach various pouches and cases to the holster (for example, to attach a pouch containing your flash, other lens cases, or even attach a travel-sized tripod to the holster).Case Logic makes a wide variety of great protective cases, and I have bought various Case Logic cases over the years, including their cassette tape carrying cases during the 1980s.  But if you had to buy just one holster for your SLR camera, I do think that there are better options for about the same price as this one.  An expensive SLR camera deserves a better holster or carrying case than a $100 point-and-shoot camera. I recently ordered this bag for my Canon 70D paired with an 18-135mm lens and fits perfectly. It has one interior zipped pocket where I keep extra SD cards. It also has two zipped  exterior pockets on either sides. I keep extra batteries in one and some essential filters in the other. One thing that I like about it is that the strap can be long enough to allow you wear it over and across your shoulder. I carry it in a way that the strap is on my left shoulder and the bag is hangs just where my right hand is. Therefore making it very easy to take the camera out of the bag, take photos and put it back. It makes street photography very easy. I bought this case for my Nikon D3200 and I must say that I'm pleased with it. I first started to look among other cases since this was the first time that I buy something like this, and I have to say that costs less than what you receive, this is actually pretty well made, firm, secure, comes with the strap. 10/10 case logic make bad cases. they are not practical, designed bad and don't fit things properly. spend a few extra dollars and go to the store where you can look into the bag and judge for yourself if you buy the right bag.  don't buy. I am happy with it and you cant go wrong with this price. My old Nikon DSLR fits perfect in it!

I like the fairly short cord and the feel on my ears.  I've used several different headphones over the years (Sennheiser, Koss,  Sony) and this is one of my favorites.My only concern is they feel a bit flimsy, and I hope they last 1-2 years.UPDATE: 02/17/2014.  I like them even more.  While at my club, I've adopted the habit of keeping them on even when I have turned my music off.  And I notice that it dampens the annoying ambient noise around me (cell-phones, talking, lifters grunting, overhead music, announcements from front desk, tread mills pounding, etc.) These things are pretty amazing for the price! reviewText: There are not many camera batteries that actually churn out a true 500 pictures per shot (CIPA)I decided to conduct a full CIPA test of this battery, google CIPA test protocol. And I did it twice, on the first test 535 images on the second test 537 images. They are CIPA rated for 500. The printing on the battery itself does not match the Amazon's photo but was matching the original battery that came with the camera. I have 2 batteries and that's all I needed on my trip. My camera was on most of the day; I used one in the morning and one in the afternoon and charged both at night. Didn't miss a shot! It also relays remaining charge information back to the camera, which is really helpful.  Other cheaper batteries do not do this so buyer beware.  This battery holds the same charge and life as the OEM battery that came with the camera. name: Celestron AstroMaster Accessory Kit
reviewText: So, my wife wanted some stuff for telephotography as a Christmas present.  She has a Celestron AstroMaster EQ telescope and a Nikon D7000 camera.  I bought her the T-ring and I was looking at buying T-Adapter with Barlow Universal - 1.25", which is a T-adapter with a Barlow lens (essentially a 2x lens).  That would cost me $44, while I was able to get this kit for $39.85.  It contains a T-adapter with a 2x lens, which I assume would be the same as the Barlow lens, 2 extra lenses and 3 filters.... for a lower price.  I'd be silly to pass up on this deal.  I was able to test the product and everything fit perfectly.  My only complaint would be that covers on lenses were a little bit off, like they were put on sloppily and the packaging looked like it was messed with.  Everything looks new, with no scratches or defects, so I'm happy.  Not only was I able to get the needed T-adapter with the 2x lens, but some bonus stuff as well.  Couldn't be happier. I bought my grandson a telescope at a garage sale but it only had one eyepiece. This item filled the gap and it included the filters. The hard case is handy for storage. The 2x Barlow lens is nice to use, but the 6mm lens is going to be difficult to focus.  The filters are okay for looking at the full moon, but I have not had much success using them with planets.  To qualify my review, this is my first set of lenses which I am using with my first ever telescope.  Before getting my telescope I had never used one before, and had never used binoculars for looking at the night sky before. I did not buy this product on Amazon, but thought of letting others know about my experience with this eyepiece set.With due respect to all the 5 star reviewers, I beg to differ on the quality of most of the parts in this set. I used this with my modest 130EQ Celestron reflector. The filters are probably the worst. The blue filter could not bring out any additional details with my kit 20mm/10mm eyepieces or with the set's 15mm eyepiece. The 6 mm seems better, but it is too much for my scope.The 'power doubling lens' is not at all a decent barlow. After attaching it with the 20 mm / 15 mm, the details became worse with it. The only good thing is the t-thread that you get with it, since that would cost you $10 or more outside.Hence though the set may look cheap on the face of it, there are only a couple of things that I could really use. Looks  excellent,good construction I have it not tested yet I have Celestron Scope C-90  and also waiting for a Celestron  CPC 800 telescope to arrive. also I am waiting for t ring adapter to use in my Canon cameras as soon I have every thing set I will test these lenses and filters.  I took fantastic pictures of the moon with my C-90 using my camera and pointing it through the eye piece,do not recommend this way of take it because it is  very difficult. That's why I ordered the T ring !This  Celestron  AstroMaster  has a very good presentation  come in a box and a case where the pieces  are set in recessed foam,protecting the parts very efficiently !  two eye pieces  the most powerfull is the 6mm that gives to my C-90 a magnification of  208x. (you divide the focal lens of your scope o telescope by the power lens...in this case  C-90 is 1250 divided  by 6=208...just in case you  dont know how to figure it out)  it comes with a Barlow 2x that magnified the eye pieces  two times,comes with  three  filters,one of them for the moon,a cleaning cloth....six  in total....I think for the price you pay for this Celestron  accessory you can not get these pieces  if bought separately at the price for this accesory . Recommended!

It keeps surprising (in a good way) me every time I use it! GET this flash! It's very simple to use, rotates in all different directions, etc. Did well in good lighting & mid level lighting. name: Canon Battery Pack Lp-E10
reviewText: One of the few drawbacks of Canon DSLRs (or at least those similar to theCanon EOS Rebel T3 1100D) is  total reliance on Canon proprietary form-factor batteries and stand-alone chargers. You won't need to stock up onlithium batteriesor make sure you have a USB cable for charging...because these options aren't available.This is the same Canon-labled battery that shipped with the camera. As with any battery, usable charge will vary with conditions and use cases. For modern Canon DSLRs, the primary variables are the abmient temperature the camera is used in (colder air = reduced operation time), use of the camera's integrated flash and the following shooting modes:(1) through the viewfinder *without* using the EOS "Live View" feature (the user guide estimates ~800 images with no flash at 73 degrees (F) and ~750 at 32 degrees (F). With 50% flash use, these numbers decrease to ~700 and ~650, respectively.(2) with EOS Live View: 240 images (no flash at 73 deg (F), 220 with 50% flash use (these decrease to 230 and 210 at 32 deg (F)0.(3) movie mode: ~110 minutes recording time at 73 deg (F) and 90 minutes at 32 deg (F).Charging time when new is around two hours, and generally under an hour after the initial charge.If you have a day or night of high volume photography ahead: get a second charged so you're not cut short by lack of portable power.Prices vary widely, and some are "equivalents" or replacements and not Canon-branded: you'll have to decide how much risk you can tolerate:-) Wao! I turn on my Cannon EOS-T3 at 9:30am, turn off at 1:30pm, 570 picures taken and still shows "Full Charge", this is just amazing! Buy it!!! Works well! This is a great replacement battery for my camera.  Same exact one that came with it, but it needed a new one after 2 years of heavy use.  Would buy again. By only Canon Brand batteries for your Canon Camera.  Other Brands do not hold as long a charge and are not as good quality.

name: SCOSCHE FMT4R TuneIn Battery Powered Universal Wireless FM Transmitter - Black
reviewText: This thing is great. I've gone through so many cigarette lighter transmitters and they all just end up breaking. I thought I'd use this and its amazing. I haven't had a problem yet. Bought this as a replacement for a cheaper one I bought online. This one has a good stereo audio quality. Totally satisfied. Works great. A bit of a pain to set the channels but very little static...If there's interference just move it around a bit and that is usually enough...A bit clunky with the 2 - AAA batteries but not too much. Use good batteries and it will last a very long time...My old transmitter plugged in the lighter and the cords going to the lighter and the Sansa clip wore out/pulled out from the transmitter.  I don't have that problem with this Scosche transmitter.  I use it with a Sansa which is feather weight and puts no strain on the wire going between the two units... If you have a smartphone and a older car stereo, this little device is surely the easiest and cheapest way to get Pandora in your car. Sound quality is better than expected, and I love the fact this runs on batteries so there is not excessive amount of wire. The FM transmitter is easy to use, and works well, except when you are on a road trip and you are approaching an area with a radio station on the frequency you are trying to use - then this unit will make your speakers emit very loud popping sounds - a sign you should change frequency, or upgrade your stereo to one with an auxiliary input so you can wire your device directly. my only other complaint is the cord feels quite flimsy.  bottom line - if you absolutely have to use an fm transmitter, this one works very well if it isn't trying to fight a radio tower for a frequency.

name: Shure SE215-K in-Ear Sound Monitor Headphone (Black)
reviewText: Bought these as a gift for my husband. He LOVES the earphones but hates the plasticky inserts for the ears, If you don't like them either, try using the foam earpieces that come with other brands that are like foam earplugs... As soon as he replaced those, he LOVED the earphones.  He used http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0078JXDRI/ref=oh_details_o00_s00_i02?ie=UTF8&psc=1 and they work great. Ok corny title but I had to do it. Everyone needs to find their sound. I found them in shure headphones. These are by far the best balanced in ear headphones I have heard. I have tried Sennheiser MM50, Klipsch image s4, Apple in-ear headphones, and my Shure ec2 (R.I.P.) headphones. Nothing to me compares to shure headphones. The sound is so crisp and clean compared to the others. MM50 sounded muddy and did the apple in-ears. S4's sounded very tinny (hurt my ears on the high end) Shure headphones have none of that. Tight bass, good highs, and maybe you can make an argument the mid range is lacking a bit but that shortcoming is quick overcome with the overall sound quality. Like my older ec2 (which I used a few times a week before they died 6 years later) the new SE 215 did not disappoint. I used to have a pair of E2Cs.  Unfortunately, I lost them.  This is the newer version of that product.I have been using a cheap pair of earbuds by another company, and haven't been happy with the sound quality.  Luckily, these sound just like me E2Cs.  Great low end for earbuds of this price, and a very nice and powerful sound across the full spectrum.  You may not have the mids and super-fine details of a more expensive set, but you would be hard-pressed to find something better for this price.The headphones are well-constructed, they come with a great selection of cushions, they have a solid and removable cord, and they fit perfectly in the ears.If you are looking for a great mid-range pair of earbuds, these are a great choice.  My music doesn't sound muddled and not "full" anymore! The Shure SE215k is a shallow fit, over-the-ear earphone.  The package contents include: the earphones themselves, a set of S,M,L silicone tips, 1 set of memory foam tips, a cleaning tool for the ear tips, and a soft shell carry case.  The earphones are made of a rigid plastic and the cables are thick and of high quality.  These are very comfortable, but you will have to adjust to how big these are if you haven't owned something like this before.  A nice little feature about these earphones is that the cables are removable and replaceable.  You can either get the original cables from Amazon or Shure, but the cables from  the Logitech UE series earphones just as well and a bit cheaper too.On to the sound.  This earphones has a lot of bass that extends down fairly deep and can sound a bit muddy on some tracks.  With genres such as hip hop, dubstep, EDM, etc, these do a great job and will fulfill the needs of your average bass head.  The mids are warm and very clear and the highs are a bit rolled off, maybe a little rolled off.  Due to the rolled off highs, these are not fatiguing and can be used for several hours before having to take a break.  Keep in mind that these isolate very well, so if you're walking down the street or anything, make sure you are well aware of your surroundings.The Shure SE215K is not without flaws however, there a few things that are bothersome right out of the box.  The first is the fit of these earphones.  While it isn't a big issue, new users might have problems properly inserting these into your ears.  The core of the problem is the memory cord that wraps around your ear.  You will need to bend constantly to conform to the curves of your ear but after a while it will retain its shape.These earphones perform extremely well and for the price, it includes many accessories.  Shure even offers a 2 year warranty with the SE215K which adds even more value to the package.  If you're a fan of good bass, warm mids, and slightly recessed highs, these earphones are a no brainer. Are they good? Well yes. They worth the money. But! You're gonna need to spend another $50 to get Shure Phone Cable if you want to listen music on your phone. Why? Because the plug on default cable is so annoyingly bad it will lose connection with the phone on every slightest move. Even if you don't need a mic, you still gonna need to buy the cable. And you cannot get earphones with already installed phone cable.I miss a pin on the cable. It's slightly heavier than other earphone cables and absolutely needs something that you can pin it to the shirt.Also Shure support left me unhappy. One of the sleeves came damaged. There is a few spares each of different size, but you get only two medium ones. So I asked them to send me one. They told me to call them and order. Here on Amazon, those spares listed for $20. I explained them that the sleeve came damaged, and just because of one sleeve I don't want to send the whole thing back. They refused to send me a replacement and it seems after all I'm gonna need to spend another 20 and buy them myself.So in the end these earphones will cost me in total ~ $170+tax. Is there any better options for that price? Sure, there are plenty. Good headphones, but they trick you to spend more.BTW. It took me almost a month to find a way to properly get them in my ears. Remember, place the earpiece the way that logo would be laying horizontally and would be readable (it should not be upside down), and then turn the cable downwards, so the whole thing will look like G letter and not the way how it looks on the picture. At the point where cable connects to the earpiece, it easily rotates. And don't waste your time bending the cable behind your ears as it says in the manual.

name: Sirui P-306 Aluminium Monopod (Black)
reviewText: I really love this monopod.  It's small and light enough to fit in my camera bag, and half the price of the similar carbon fiber model.  Can't see that the small weight difference is worth the extra cost. This is a well made monopod but it feels heavier than I thought it would.  All my other tri and monopods have the lever type lock and I just got used to that system.  This is a twist lock leg and I just can't seem to get the hang of it yet.  So if you are used to this system, this is a solid monopod, much less expensive than comparable name brands.  Since I don't use a tripod or monopod that often, I couldn't justify spending hundreds of dollars on a lighter carbon fiber one.  So if weight is a big concern, look elsewhere.  If you are on a tight budget, couple this with the Tripod Monopod Metal BALL HEAD Quick Release Plate By Fancier (see my other review) for less than twenty bucks and you've got a pretty beefy and reliable setup.Pro: Solid well built monopod.Con: A bit heavy. I didn't care too much for the twist lock system, but that's just me. I've only had a chance to use it one time, but I was very satisfied with it's small sizes and it is well build.  It more than satisfied my need for the height that I needed.  I would definitely recommend it to anyone who wants a very good mono pod. Really solid monopod! I used this for everything from trail hiking to basketball games and it holds up like a champ! The threaded connection at the top is very clever in that it flips over for a larger diameter for the bigger cameras.One little down side is that you can't take that strap off the monopod without cutting it...kinda silly since I already have a strap on the camera and it gets messy with all these straps. Very sturdy, yet compact enough that it easily fits in the laptop compartment of my Lowepro Fastpack 250 along side my other gear when folded. Most other monopods this size only fold down to between 21.5 and 25 inches, this one folds down to 15. The only downside is that the compass is a cheap piece of crap, but the monopod itself is a very high quality product.

name: Lowepro Photo Sport Sling 100 AW Sling Bag (Orange)
reviewText: This is the best all day anywhere pack. At first I was really worried about this pack only having one strap. Honestly the only reason this pack won in the end was the color. But after a few all day trips with it to Colorado hiking and biking, it has proved VERY useful and VERY LIGHT. When the belt strap is adjusted correctly, as the same with the true backpack, the one strap makes no difference. I love carying this around as it attracts plenty of attention and is great in all types of outdoors. While on a full day trip, I would carry my Rebel XSi with a 18-55mm stock lens attached and either a base Canon 55-250mm or a 70-200 f4.0 L lens in the camera padded section. In the pouch most of the time it would be a gureilla pod and a true tripod along with a few lens hoods. This bag is also what worried me. What was listed above is ALL that will fit. If you own more camera accessories as I do, you WILL need either to forgo it for that day or get a Lowepro certified attachment. I'm still trying to find one large enough to fit my dang mongo phone. I actually bought this bag on clearance for $30. But after owning and using it daily for a month, I would pay the $80 price tag for it. Pros:*It fits my 100D SL1 (I know its a small body, but fits my wife's T3i as well), a 55-250mm lens, kit lens, and 40mm pancake lens all in the camera compartment that zips on the side for easy access. Fits all other minor camera gear (filters, hoods, cards, batteries, chargers, etc. either in the main compartment, outside pockets, or inside mini pouch). The main reason I got this is that the main compartment extends all the way down and isn't cut off by the camera compartment. As a result I am able to fit my 12" Chromebook laptop in there with all the said gear no problem. You can probably fit a 15" laptop in there with a tight fit. There is also 2 straps on the bottom of the bag for a tripod.*I love the lightweight, durable nylon-ish material, solid zippers, and 3-point buckle strap sytem (not only makes it feel secure, but also easy to take on and off). Reflective piping and built-in rain cover is pretty cool, but not so useful for me personally.Cons:*Although its feels good around my back, the one strap can really strain my shoulder when it's fully loaded (not sure if there is a max. loading weight). Also, because the top of the strap is sewn towards the middle of the bag, the top of the bag tends to hang over for me, but this is more a cosmetic issue.*The only padded areas are the camera compartment. So everything outside the camera compartment is left unprotected because the bag material is so thin.*Side water bottle pocket only fits a 20 oz. plastic water bottle with a tight fit.*The top of the main compartment is lined with a transparent, slick residue that started to peel after 2 weeks of use. Nice study camera bag with plenty of padding & space for 2 cameras/bodies plus lenses.  I would like to see a couple of improvements - I'm a 5'6" tall woman so not particularly small but there is insufficient adjustment in the lift loader to suit my frame, so the pack hangs from my shoulder instead of fitting snugly & is consequently a little uncomfortable. Also, it would be great if there was an additional separate compartment for batteries, cards etc. There is a small zipped area, but that doesn't provide much storage or the ability to store items separately. Other than that, it's a nice attractive pack. I love this pack. It holds my nikon D7000 perfect with enough room for several other lenses and a jacket or some other gear. It is very well built, just like my Osprey camping backpack. It comes with a waterproof bag that unfolds out of the bottom. I know it is expensive but this time you get what you pay for. All of the great packs in the world are expensive and that has to do with the awesome construction and materials. This sling is small, but that is exactly what I needed. The dimensions that they give on the description are correct. I needed a backpack to protect my camera gear and give me a little storage for my nature hikes.  I went with this pack and used it for four separate outings and so far it hasn't disappointed.Pros:- Sling style makes it easy to slide the pack around for camera access without removing the pack completely.- Side pocket that allows me to carry a water bottle.- Small storage on top that allows for my second, smaller camera, and a few misc items.- Attached rain fly (which I actually had to use on my first outing with it and it kept my items safe and dry)Cons;- There isn't much I would change.Overall:This is a very nice pack and in the medium size range, it provides a decent amount of storage.  I would prefer a few more pockets, but I realize that this is difficult without moving up to a larger pack.  I also read some reviews that said that this pack is not comfortable, but it has been fairly comfortable for me and, as a rather large guy, it has plenty of room for adjustment.One final note is that it seems fairly tough.  I recently took it thru an area with a heavy amount of briar bushes and had it snagged several times without rips or tears.

name: Nikon Af-S Nikkor 50 Mm F/1.8G Prime Lens for DSLR Camera - Black
reviewText: It's a very slow focus lens with a crippled feature set and a fairly narrow range of uses.For landscape, it's not bad - though it begins to fall over in the higher f-stops.For plants, it's adequate, though focusing close enough to build a good frame filling shot of most flowers requires playing the accordion game in order to find a distance at which it can achieve a decent focus.It's pretty adequate for point-and-shoot type activities, or in full manual mode where you override the AF and aperture.Everything it does well, the Nikon 50mm f/1.8 AF-D does better, and costs less. I got this one as a stop gap when I needed a second 50mm lens, and the local stores were out of the 50mm 1.8D.I'd not recommend buying this lens, but if you get it for free, it's better than nothing. Perfect!! I needed a lens that helped me get clear action pics of my daughter playing volleyball.  I don't get great shots every time, because the focus wants to go to the furthest point in the shot,(learning curve for me) and she isn't always the furthest!! But the few I do get and WAY better than the other lens I used that came with the camera. It's a good lens I just wish it had macro .... It was not what I was expecting when I placed the order after that it's a good lens has all noons are the best for me I had this lens coupled with my Nikon D3000 and it helps me produce some great looking shots. I think this is probably the perfect portrait lens. It works great in low light, and does really well taking shots indoors without flash in situations without the best lighting. The bokeh effect is really prevalent down at lower aperture, and it seems to stay pretty sharp throughout. I would highly recommend this to anyone looking for their first prime lens. you must have one of these in your lens arsenal. The bokeh could be better looking, but the color and tack-sharpness are just stunning.  Great lens for the price!

name: Alfa AWUS036NHA 150Mbps Wireless USB Adaptor
reviewText: For the price a very nice booster or back up to catch them hard to get signals.Great product excellent price, I should buy more lol Ships fast. I've had mine now for over 6 months and still strong. Thank you Alfa Really, really fast card. Works with kali linux right when you plug it in and also supports packet injecting. Just what it is advertised as. Would definitely recommend this to anyone. I purchased this to test out a Kali Linux VM and it worked great!  Of course I have no idea what I'm doing but this USB-WiFi adapter is solid! I bought this adapter, the Alfa 9 dbi antenna, and the suction cup mount at the same time, so let me start by saying that I'm comparing this adapter the new antenna and stuck to a window vs. an internal Dell wifi card.  Hands down this new setup wins, both in signal strength and in speedtest numbers.I'd had an inkling that my Dell laptop (with B/G/N) wasn't seeing as far as I'd like when another computer in the house was able to see and connect to access points that I could barely see on the listing.  This has helped quite a bit, I'm glad I bought this even though it felt like a waste originally since I had B/G/N coverage.  This really helps improve the signal strength at the computer. Having been impressed with the Alfa AWUS036H b/g wireless card I gave this product a shot.  At first it was performing fine but though using a signal strength monitoring program (inSSIDer) I was getting random -10dB spikes across all networks in range which gave me a clue that something was not right with the card.  The card then started to emit an annoying sound at times and when it was making that noise I would lose network connectivity.  The card also would randomly disconnect from the computer for no reason.I thought I just had a lemon and ordered a replacement. I experienced the same issues with the replacement.I used this product with Windows 7 64-bit.

name: Logitech Digital HD Portable 1080p Webcam C615 with Autofocus, Black
reviewText: There are a lot of reviews that go into detail and I am sure you can see sample footage of the webcam in use over at you tube. I have sampled video taken at HD 1920x1080 at the Loseless setting.  Video quality is just ok. Video quality seems to be exactly the same no matter what resolution you use (assuming you don't maximize the video and just let it play in it's native resolution. It is going to look like a cell phone video (from a droid with a good camera).  Keep in mind that the overall camera is about the size of a box of tictacs.  Considering that, the video is good.  Comparing it to my sony camcorder (cx560) and the video is very poor.  But it's not meant to be a camcorder.  I bought this to use with Camtasia Studio to do video tutorials with a PiP web cam video.  Little did I know, THIS CAMERA WILL ONLY RECORD IN A RESOLUTION OF 320x240 when used with Camtasia Studio (CS).  This is not a limitation of the webcam but with CS itself!  This is a known bug with many different models of webcams and CS is working on a fix.....I called up CS and they told me that the Logitech 9000 webcam will work with supporting different resolutions.  I think I will just hold on to this webcam and record the webcam video with the supplied software WHILE recording a tutorial with CS and just combine the two videos in my editing software.A couple notes:-It does not have a lid but you can swivel the cam around 360 so it is not looking at you.-You can zoom and pan the camera using the software.  Range is not great but it is cool, especially if you remote in to your work pc and use the zoom and pan to look  around your office!-Loseless vs. High quality setting= I could not tell the difference in picture quality.  Loseless files will be larger of course.-microphone is not that bad.  I think using "Rightsound" helps quality.  It seems to pick up less background noise.  I will continue to use my Blue Yeti mic though.-You can choose from almost every available standard 4:3 or widescreen 16:9 resolution known to man.-Exports videos as WMV files.  Pretty cool. this webcam does not compress 1080p video on the fly, so the best it can do is 720p 15fps adequately.  in motion capture mode the best video it can manage is a pathetic SVGA.  unless you get to pay 50% off MSRP or specifically need this form factor, I would hold out for a true 1080p webcam with proper on the fly compression capability. I like this web cam.  For the money, you can't go wrong.  The reason I give 4 stars is that the live video quality is not always the best, but it will always be acceptable.  Overall I am very pleased. This is the second one of these cameras I've purchased. I really like it.Pros:1. Compact for travel.2. HD video3. Really good microphone4. Can be mounted on a camera tripod5. Comes with an extension cableCon:1. The USB cable doesn't store well with the unit. It's got this great transformer like design for the camera body and there's the USB cable protruding out of it. Just a minor thing. Good tool, I have an old desk top and needed to add a simple webcam.  Ordered this and plugged it in.  Computer found it and it worked, no hassle, no CD with step by step instructions in four languages. It just works.  It was easy to attach to my monitor, simple.  Again no instructions required.  I know most new monitors, tablets, phones, etc. now have built in cameras.  I didn't and I didn't want to get a bunch of new parts and software. This Webcam saved me a lot of headaches and worked out of the box.

name: Nikon AF-S DX Micro 40mm F/2.8G Prime Lens for Nikon DSLR Camera - Black
reviewText: I have used the 40 mm Lens so much from the day that I opened the box it is a must For the $ this lens is a good buy if you are getting into macro photography and provides very clear images.  I have no complaints about this lens Fantastic lens!!  I originally purchased this for the detail shots during weddings (ie. "ring" shot, table set ups, flowers, etc) and newborns, but I think this will be one of my new go-to lenses for everyday portraiture!  It creates the most beautiful sun flare which coincides with my person shooting style when I shoot into the sun, and generally is just fantastic!  Great price for this lens! It's 40mm. It's pricey. It's claim to fame? The fact it can do 1:1 macro shots!But the fun ends about there when you realize thatthe aperture isn't fixed (it changes in relation to how close you are to your subject causing you to change your aperture constantly)you must get EXTREMELY close to your subject most timesit's very close to a normal 50mm lensand it's just expensive for what it offers.The optics are typical modern day optics from Nikon. Sharp, colorful, somewhat contrasty. It can also function as a normal prime if you so choose.In the end, I ended up selling mine off at a loss, it's just a lens I thought I needed when really, a 135 should be what macro enthusiasts are searching for. Don't be like me and get stung by bees. Buy a longer lens! I am an amateur, hobbyist nature photographer and I have been looking for a macro lens with a reasonable price tag (as a grad student I cannot afford the $700-1500+ lenses). I'll break this down into pros and cons, though the only cons are really just inconveniences; this lens can produce flawless images.Pros:-Tack sharp images, especially with stabilization (tripod + remote, etc)-Manual focus is smooth and works well (good for me because I do a lot of focus stacking)-Works well for macro and landscape (granted these won't be wide-angle landscape shots)-Fantastic for waterfall photography-PRICE!!Cons:-No VR - may need to crank up ISO especially for handheld macro such as flowers, bugs, etc (or get creative with a tripod, rest the camera on a rock, etc)-40mm and need to be close to subject for 1:1 macro, can cause issues with blocking sunlight (depending on the angle you're shooting from) or scaring away the more skittish insects (butterflies); still, if you're sneaky enough and strategic with lighting it can produce great macro imagesI got this for macro (105mm too expensive for me) but the first time I used it was to photograph waterfalls. It worked perfectly for this! I'm also finding that I'm taking quite a few nice landscape pictures as well.Overall a really high quality lens. Perfect step up from the kit lens in terms of image quality.

I have been looking for a case like this for quite some time now - one that fits my point-and-shoot camera snuggly, protecting it from hard bumps and bruises, yet not making the whole affair so bulky that I rather take my chances most of the time and take the camera with me without the case.The camera I am speaking of is the Sony HX7V, which is admittedly a somewhat small camera for a 10x zoomer.At first glance, I thought never, ever will this camera fit in the case. But it does. Fits like a second skin, actually.I do not need all those extra pockets for batteries (for anything that might require more shots than one battery can handle, it would probably be prudent to carry a DSLR anyway ...), additional SD-cards (one 16 GB card in the camera should suffice for most shooting days ...), energy bars, or GPS units. What I need is a plain and simple protective case for my camera.Yes, the ECC-101 also has a built-in mesh pocket inside the case, which could be useful to store some emergency money, or a few business cards. But I really don't need that.The ECC-101 appears to be well made and I can attest to the protective prowess of its shell, which handles normal, not too rough handling very well.It has two zippers which is a bit of overkill to me - one should have done with this very small case. It comes with a strap, which I immediately discarded. I am using the camera strap to carry the whole ensemble, instead. And here, the two zippers make some sense - they allow me to put the camera strap through to the outside.All in all, I am very glad to have this case. But before you go and buy it, please check if your camera fits within the envelope given by the HX7V (101.6mm x 57.6mm x 28.6mm); because of the very snug fit with the ECC-101, even a slight deviation from this envelope would probably result in a non-fit situation.

name: BlueRigger High Speed Mini HDMI(NOT Micro) to HDMI cable with Ethernet (6 Feet / 1.8 Meters)
reviewText: This cable is very well made and comes with a great price. I use it to connect my digital camera to my television. Don't hesitate on this cable, you won't regret it. A - This is indeed what you need - this is NOT a 'regular' HDMI cable. One of its ends is a 'mini' (Type C) connector that may be required by certain cameras such as the Flip MinoHD but is not compatible with 'regular' equipment. And do NOT confuse the 'mini' with the 'micro' (Type D) HDMI connector which is even smaller and works with the newest/smallest gadgets. Check your gadget's manual before you place your order. Tablets tend to require a 'micro' connector.B - You don't mind paying very little. If you search Amazon for 'HDMI mini' you will find quite a few similar items, some of them selling for a lot more but performing the exact same fashion.And, talking about specs, this cable is a 'High Speed' rated HDMI 1.4 cable 'with Ethernet'.- The 'High Speed' rating is largely meaningless, indicating that the cable supports 1080p video - almost all do and no one should ever consider buying anything less.- The 'with Ethernet' badge indicates that if the 2 connected devices support Ethernet AND support HDMI 1.4, they will be able to use the HDMI cable for Ethernet traffic instead of requiring a separate additional phone-like wire. Of course, none of the small cameras that would use a mini HDMI connector talk 'Ethernet' so this 'with Ethernet' feature doesn't really matter much.- 6 ft. length is just about right. The cable is long enough to allow for a connection to the back of your TV or receiver while the 'mini' end can be pulled to the front where your camera would plug. My new receiver came with a front HDMI port and a good-looking 6 ft. cable for playing video on the big screen from my camera is exactly what I needed.- It's pretty. Given that this is a visible HDMI cable, not something that goes to the back of your entertainment center, looking good adds value.I had no trouble to plug the mini end into my MinoHD and the regular into a our receiver and play video directly. Playback was flawless and, even though this is not something that everyone needs or anyone needs often, it doesn't hurt having one around.I am granting this cable 5 stars because it performs flawlessly, the price is absolutely right and for its premium looks. I was working on a project using my Droid tablet and needed to connect it to a large screen. I purchased 2 different lengths just to make sure I was able to make connection during the presentation. It worked great! If your looking for an hdmi cable under 30 bucks this is it. Buy it with confidence , I am glad I did. Will buy more in the future. High quality cable very well designed. Cable was purchased for a couple devices and works great on both of course. It fits perfectly and tightly as is should. It is high quality in it's construction and was a great price. The packaging was as it should be as well. I will buy more cables from them in the future. I am very happy overall.

reviewText: When it comes to speaker wire, many vendors (in brick and mortar stores and online) will invite you to overspend --sometimes at ridiculously high prices) for cabling and connectors of all kinds.Speaker wire is among offerings from those who want you to overspend for something that doesn't offer any substantial gain in performance...even with huge leaps in price beyond what you would pay for a commodity item.I've been hooking up speakers to stereo components since Gerald Ford was president, and have yet to detect an audible difference between generic offerings such as this (or even plain old bulk lamp cord).If you don't need the leftovers from longer lengths available in bulk, this is an excellent choice. One of the twin strands is marked with a continuous white stripe, allowing you to easily differentiate your positive and negative connections.Don't overspend. The marked polarity on the wire helped me make sure that things were hooked up properly to my amplifier. Cheaper than anything I was able to find local, and with 100 feet I have plenty more in case I decide to run more speakers around the house. I used this wire to hookup my home theater system.  Great wire; the insulation does not feel cheap and one of the wires is clearly labeled with a white stripe.  Insulation was easy to strip off and the cable was wrapped around the spool nice and tight.Don't waste your money on expensive cables.  A conductor is a conductor and this does just fine.
