name: MANFROTTO MVH502AH
reviewText: The Tripod head is ok overall but I have am yet to figure out the Panning design.  No matter what tension setting, at the end of a pan, the Tripod heads jerks into position slightly.  Shooting with a Canon 5D Mk iii, it's rather not usable for panning. Once you get to the end, there is a slight springy type movement. My $49 Velflo 8 does not behave like this, it's way smoother for panning and comes to stop perfectly.  The Tilt however is acceptable with the right amount of tension dialed in.I am surprised that nobody has noticed this, unless I got a bad copy... I have to admit - I used to be a fan of Bogen/Manfrotto. But I now know that there's better sticks and heads to be had in photography. And, the Arca Swiss mounts are certainly superior. Enter video with DSLR's and Canon's Cinema series. I fought it, and now I'm doing a series of seminar videos. Go fig. Right away I had to get something besides ball-heads or 3-way pan-tilts. I also didn't want to spend a ton of cash as there's lots of other investments to be made, from rails to audio.Like you, I scoured the web and youtube for ideas of what could be had for under $200. 3 names came to the surface: Fancier, Benro and a couple of Manfrottos. The Fancier was quickly eliminated, and I boiled it down to Benro and Manfrotto. I suppose partly because of the Devil I know, as well as interest in the SYMPLA system, I went with the Manfrotto, and specifically the 502. It was tough between this and the 500, but it looked like the 502 simply had the control I was looking for.As you're probably aware, the biggest complaint about this head is the friction adjustment for the tilt is on the left, the lock on the right. I'm not sure why this is such a deal killer for a lot of folks, other than they've become used to the standard layout. Kind of like how Nikon people think Canon zooms are backwards, and vice-versa. Also, I'm a southpaw - and as such have become completely ambidextrous in many things. So much so that I probably won't reverse the control arm, and am totally happy with the friction control being on the left!When I first got the head and started playing with it I had an "oh no!" moment. When I'd tilt the arm up, down or rotate it - I'd get some push back. It just wouldn't stay and move back just a tiny bit. ARGH! I was all ready to box the thing up and send it back, actually collecting all the packing pieces and tags I'd already spread around my office. But, I wanted to play with the EOS controller and my laptop - so on it stayed for the evening. Low and behold, after moving it around for a bit, and I do mean literally only minutes of play - the problem completely vanished. I think the problem being that the fluid needed to move throughout the channels and even out the pressure. There was just too much pressure or a vacuum or something going on. Two weeks later it's never repeated this problem.I highly recommend that if you're connecting your camera directly to the head, get the Manfrotto quick release plate, or a Giottos if it's going to be a stand-alone or you have other Arca Swiss compatible stuff. I'm going to stick with the Manfrotto on Manfrotto here. What I do is attach my rail assembly directly to the 502 head, and then put the Manfrotto quick-release plate onto the rail system, so I can quickly attach the camera of my choice to that. The plate/rail will then quickly pop off for transportation. You will find if you try to attach a DSLR to the plate on the 502, that the plate tightening knob will hit the camera, preventing you from placing it centered on the head. Oddly, many photos from Manfrotto show the camera mounted directly to the head this way - another ergonomic goof.Oh here's one more ergonomic oddity (maybe) and I'm done. The lock knob for the pan is inside the "bridge" of the head, at the front. So you sort of have to reach inside to lock or release it. This has not been a problem with me (ever). At least the way I use it, I unlock it and that's it. It's nothing I constantly access and lock and unlock while I'm working - just like the tilt lock. I usually keep them both unlocked so I can pan and tilt when I need to - I record presentations and don't know what the speaker is going to do so I need to be ready. YMMV.Aside from some of these ergonomic quirks, the head is fantastic. Granted, if I've ever played with a video head in the past, it's cost as much as a Honda Civic. I've simply never played with a "mid-fi" $3k head. I have played with a few sub $200 heads though, and been way less than impressed. For my 6D on a rail with a Tascam, follow focus and Sigma 70-200 f2.8 OS, it's more than up to the task.Pros:- Fantastic build- Big and wide! Easy to balance equipment on- Holds medium weight with ease- Super smooth motion- Very linear feel- Great friction control- Gorgeous- Easy to use, and fastCons:- Tilt drag control knob on left- Tilt lock on right-  Pan lock in front under bridge- Plate system NOT for "stand alone" use- BigI've now used this a couple of times now for a video shoot - about 12 hours of time. It performed flawlessly with a 6D, rail, follow focus and 70-200 f2.8 lens, along with a lighter lens. The only comment I'd make is that the weight should be as centered as possible if you don't want to have to lock down the tilt. With a lighter lens this seemed to not be an issue at all, but the extra 3lbs makes a difference. Certainly a heavy video recorder could be too much - but a typical DSLR rig around 6-7 lbs is not an issue if centered properly. I could easily add a cage and a matte box without having much more of an affect on it.Bottom line: It's smooth, it holds and it's very well built. It certainly looks and feels as if it should cost a whole lot more - something I can't say about some of their ball heads! Currently I have this mounted on one of my old Bogen 3001's, and it works fine. However in the future I might just consider a specialized tripod, and getting a half ball. I feel this head will stay with me as I grow my system, something I wasn't sure of when I purchased it. Not the cheapest, but not that much more expensive for something that stands next to their 504 for twice the price. It's a keeper and it gets 5 stars. It's ok, nice head, only problem is that i wants to buy Rapid Connect Adapter with Sliding Mounting Plate can be use the same 502 head plate, can't find any< i don't want another 502 head pay $200 to $300. Very smooth panning and definitely much more solid than my old slick 504QF fluid head. It would have been nice for it to come with a 1/4-20" to 3/8" adapter for tripods that only have the smaller thread and also somewhere to store the smaller screw from the qr plate when its not needed.Aside from that it's a great value head and I'm sure that it will help take my work to the next level of smoothness and professionalism. I've been using a Manfrotto 501HD head for the last six years now and it's been a great workhorse for me.  It's biggest flaw was that it wasn't a true fluid head, but rather used grease so there was always a bit of backlash and it was never ultra smooth.  I finally decided it was time to upgrade and thought I'd try the 502 video head before eventually picking up a whole new system and wow, what an upgrade!It's so smooth and because it's true fluid head with bearings it actually took me a few hours to get used to it.  I was so used to fighting the grease that I would move too quickly, and then blow the take.  Luckily it didn't take long for me to get used to the new awesomeness and I was panning and tilting like never before.  The drag adjustments work well and allow for a lot of fine tuning.  Not huge on the placement of the pan and tilt locks, but otherwise I love it.

name: Celestron – NexImage 5 Solar System Imager – Astronomy Camera for Moon, Sun, and Planets – 5 MP Color Camera for Astroimag...
reviewText: I was excited when I received  this product, but after a few days of use I realized it wasn't what I was looking for in my first telescope camera. I want an introductory camera to get me started for a year or so and after a few uses I was able to see this product does not have those kind of legs.I took some videos of Saturn, Mars and Jupiter with this device on different days before I made my judgement. At this point I realized that I wasn't going to get results that I've seen other users get with the same telescope and similar entry level cameras. The image quality is not very good. For a little bit more money there are other options that will give you a lot more detail and better colors.The iCap software does its job, is pretty simple to understand and there are some youtube videos to help you learn how to work it.The software does not work well with Windows 8. The iCap software will install fine on Windows 8, and will run for a bit but occasionally crash the computer when you are capturing or changing settings. Surprisingly this software is the first software to give my Win8 laptop the blue screen of death. And it happened multiple times within an hour. I have read comments from other NexImage 5 users, and some have been successful using it in Windows 8, but others have not been as lucky.Using my XP laptop I had none of the technical issues, and even though my XP laptop is about 7 years old the processor is dual core and was fast enough to capture video at the highest resolution without a technical issue. If you have a reasonably modern multicore intel laptop I think this software should work OK for you.The 5MP setting will make a planet like Jupiter look very small, so using the 640x480 setting is the only way to get a good view of the planets. Simply put, even in 5MP mode Jupiter and it's moons will never take up more space than 640x480 pixels, you will have mostly black space filling up the image. 5MP mode is good for aligning your scope to the target, but for imaging you will want to use a lower resolution. Lower resolutions capture many more frames per second, which is essential to get a good image when using the included Registax software.The iCap software also installs a system idle process/firewire management program that does not uninstall when you uninstall iCap. You will need to find this manually and remove. The idle process program always runs, even when you are not using the capture software and it completely drained my laptop battery within a few hours. Normally my laptop can go a few days on a single charge when it is not being actively used, but this software actively drains your device even when it should be idle.I would not recommend this product to friends. Bought it to use on a Meade ETX-80. It only worked about half the time, and when it did, the image was just dismal. I had to send it back, I got better results from sticking my iphone up to the eyepiece. This is not the first astrophotography camera I've used.  I can only get it to work on two resolution settings, even though there are nine options in the software.  I cannot bin, I get an error whenever I try this.  I was not impressed with the results from one lunar imaging session.  Although I purchased this below the current $200 price, I am sorry for spending the money on it.  I guess for the time being, I'll go back to my other cameras for planetary imaging. Because of the price, this is a great starter camera for anyone wondering whether or not they would like to get into astrophotography. One thing to keep in mind is this camera is equivalent to a 5mm eyepiece so the magnification is huge, requiring you to really zero in on the object. You might consider buying a focal reducer to use on close up objects like the moon. Otherwise your field of view would be small. The other thing to keep in mind is Celestron recommends not using it with your star diagonal. I agree. Remove the star diagonal and insert this camera directly into the OTA. Not doing so will give you problems with viewing and finding the object. I use this camera on my Celestron Nexstar 8 SE. The device came with both the image capturing software and with Registax 6 for post processing. Both work without issue. When it works, the camera takes great shots of planets. I was able to get some really great shots of Jupiter and Saturn with it, and I plan on using it as a guide camera when I get my equatorial mount. That being said, it's ridiculous that in 2014 the only drivers for this camera are for Windows XP. It took several days of toying around to get this to work on windows 7, and some of the functionality (read: resolution / FPS combinations) were not available. It was equally as hard to get it to work on Parallels on a mac. If someone could make an AP, USB camera that was actually a member of the modern age and was literally plug and play, it would be great. But alas, no such camera exists. For what this is, it's a good bargain. Just be prepared to be frustrated when you set it up if you're not on a 10 year old windows XP machine.

name: Canon EF 24-70mm F/2.8L II USM Standard Zoom Lens for Canon DSLR Camera
reviewText: Why the heck did I buy a two-grand lens?!Let's backtrack a bit. My 1st L lens is a 24mm f/1.4L USM II Prime and I still have this. Then I needed something with a zoom for a vacation we were going to-- enter the 24-105mm f/4L USM. And then someone hired me to do a wedding coverage...With the reviews I've read, there was only one thing I needed to do, out with the old zoom and in with the new. I thought I could make do with the 24-105mm but I found someone willing to take it off my hands. Thinking about long term, why not? I was impressed with some photos I've seen taken using the 24-70mm f/2.8L USM (version I), so it was safe to assume this one may render the same quality... or even better.My only direct comparison right now are the outputs from my 24mm f/1.4L USM II Prime. And yes, to some degree, the 24-70mm f/2.8L USM II shoots photos like a prime! Buying this lens actually made me think twice about keeping my prime because sometimes having it may be redundant. But, with the falling price of this prime, I'm not sure if I want to take the hit as opposed to keeping a f/1.4 that really comes handy in low light situations. I'd probably faint once Canon launches a version with an IS, which I heard is coming out pretty soon-- late 2013, early 2014?Overall, this lens is superb and I'm always excited when using it. If you can wait it out until the one with the IS comes out, wait. In my case, the wedding I'll be doing is coming up before that so here I am 'suffering' with this lens in my hand.07/24/13 UPDATE:Signed another wedding client after showing some sample wedding-themed shots using this lens. Meeting with a prospective client to do senior photos in August.Also, if any of you got wind of the weather down in Orlando, FL in the early weeks of June this year then let me tell you that Canon wasn't joking when they said "weather-sealing" (with filter of course, your camera should have weather-sealing too). I was 'forced' to test it out so you guys won't have to, but in case you're as 'adventurous' as myself then feel free to do so. :)Brought this lens with my prime but stored the latter in a safety box in a Disney World hotel 5 days out of 6. In fairness to my prime, it just didn't suit my needs at the time due to absence of a zoom. So far, I would still recommend this zoom lens with financial considerations aside. This is my 7th or 8th L lens.  Professional wedding photographer.  It really lives up to the hype.  Very sharp.  One star off because my rubber zoom ring came loose after one year.  Get on that canon and you will have a perfect lens. I can confirm that the second version of the 24-70 f/2.8 lens is better than the first version. I had a persistent sharpness problem with the first version of this lens, and micro adjustments didn't seem to correct it. I was so happy when I tested this lens through all focal lengths and found the sharpness to be as good as my 24mm f/1.4 on the wide end and it was damn close to the 85 f/1.2 on the tele end.Since my only complaint with the previous lens was the sharpness, I spent less time evaluating the bokeh, vignette, distortion, and other optical qualities of this lens because it's a zoom and I have prime lenses if I want the best bokeh or contrast. But, nothing stood out to me as being undesirable and the images overall looked beautiful. This is a must have buy if you don't already own a normal zoom lens for these focal lengths, and is a highly suggested upgrade if you have the old Canon EF 24-70 f/2.8 USM. Brought this lens 2 months ago and its pretty good. I am using this with the canon 5d mark ii. Overall satisfied with the image quality (super tack sharp).I am not too fond the of the build quality of the lens, which is why I gave it a 3 star review. The lens feels cheaply made when i compare it to the canon ef 17-40. The 24-70 feels almost plastic like and not metallic. The zoom ring was very stiff, but got smooth as I started using it more, but still feels stiff. I think the zoom lock is kinda stupid since it only locks at the wide angle. The new hood doesn't look as cool as the one for the mk i.Pros-Sharpgood color/contrastlow cafast focusgood flare controlCons-82mm filter - can't use my 77mm filers :(construction feels cheapzoom ring not smoothPrice - Is it worth 2k? I say no unless your a professional. I'm a career photojournalist and bought the Canon EF 24-70mm f/2.8L II lens to fill that yawning gap between my 16-35 f/2.8 and 70-200 f/2.8. Recently I used this lens to shoot a variety of editorial, business, PR and party assignments. Here are my initial impressions:1. Dang, this sucker is expensive! I coughed up about $2200 with tax.2. As everyone says, too bad it doesn't have IS.3. Somewhat chunky, but anyone who handles pro gear will hardly notice. One disappointment is that the front section slides forward 1-1/2 inches when zooming from 24mm to 70mm. I'm surprised this Canon upgrade didn't incorporate an internal zooming mechanism like the 16-35 and 70-200. This weather-sealed lens uses a latch to lock at 24mm for travel and running around.4. The lens analysis in DPreview.com is dead on: you see significant vignetting at f/2.8, but it settles down at f/4.0 and nearly disappears by f/5.6. Some minor barrel distortion.5. Superb sharpness and contrast even at f/2.8, comparable to the legendary 70-200 f/2.8! Excellent color.6. Truly superior lens flare control, even when shooting directly into light sources! Locking lens hood (included) is shallower than I prefer for optimal protection of that massive 82mm front element. My lens came with a standard snap-on lens cap; I replaced the Canon cap with a Fotodiox 05CAPT82x1 82mm Inner Pinch Lens Cap and it works nicely.7. Close focusing is okay. Not macro quality, but close-ups at 70mm are acceptable, even at f/2.8.Conclusion: this is a real workhorse that will remain attached to one of my full frame bodies from now on. Horribly expensive, Canon is charging all the market will bear. But since I will probably use it for the next decade, I'm not complaining--too much!LOW LIGHT UPDATE: last week I had an assignment to shoot stills on the slasher/suspense movie set "Killing Mr. Right." I used this lens to shoot handheld existing light at f/2.8 the whole time. I was blown away with the razor sharp images! I was tap dancing right at the edge of usable existing light, but the photos turned out great! Yeah, I wish it had IS, but this lens is sharp enough to cut ya!

name: Jabra Speak 410 USB Speaker (Black)
reviewText: I found this speakerphone for voice-over-Internet to be every bit as good as the Cisco version I use at work, at about one-third the price. I like the styling better as well, it's cleaner and takes less space. I have had bad experiences with less expensive brands which are less sturdy with inadequate sound quality or volume.If you do a lot of voice over Internet and have a good enough Internet connection that the microphone/speaker is the bottleneck in communication quality, I think this could be an excellent choice. This little speakerphone, about the diameter of a CD, performs like a champ. It's very easy to use, and sound quality is excellent in both directions. It's on the expensive side for home use, but if it's in your price range, buy with confidence. And a small office that doesn't want to invest in a high-end system could do a lot worse.Unsurprisingly, documentation is minimal, and if there's one knock on the unit, it's that the touch controls and indicator lights are not super intuitive. However, it doesn't take long to get the hang of things. Once you figure it out, you'll be fine.The unit is truly plug & play. I didn't even touch the included mini-CD, although I was amazed to discover that those are still being manufactured! When I plugged it into my PC's USB jack, it automatically downloaded the proper driver and was good to go.There was one incident where the speakerphone suddenly stopped functioning. I simply unplugged it and plugged it in again, and it was back in business. I delayed my review for a while because of this, to see if it would be a recurring issue, but it's been a few months now and there have been no further glitches. Opening this speakerphone, I could not help but think it reminds me of a portable speaker I haveAltec Lansing Music Speaker. I also own a few Jabra Bluetooth headsets and car speakerphones so with everything combined, it was very easy to navigate.I installed the software and it immediately let me know there was a more current version which I upgraded to. You are downloading Jabra PC Suite. I did not know, but this speakerphone is compatible with Avaya, Cisco, IBM Lotus Sametime, Microsoft, and Skype. What versions and what operating systems can be found on the Jabra website.The size of the speaker is a lot smaller than I would have thought. I have used it with Skype and I was amazed at how well it worked. All of the buttons worked for me. In fact they are very sensitive, if you are not careful, you will accidentally hit one without realizing it. Once you have it connected through your USB port, it takes over as your main speaker. I thought it would default to the speaker and microphone but I had to drop down and select each of them while using Skype. It was no biggie though. Calls seemed really clear and I was told I came through clear as well. One feature I really liked is my volume control is on the front of my laptop. I can control the speaker volume up and down with the main computer dial which I am more used to. Sure you can turn it up and down on the top of the speaker, but I found it easier to use my speaker dial.Another great feature is that you can use this as separate speaker to listen to music or watch videos. I was rather impressed at how loud the sound got. I was able to turn it up half way and it was rather loud. Again, it will override your computer speaker but the sound is wonderful. I would not turn it up too loud though as it does get a bit distorted if too high.So far I am enjoying this and carry it with my with my two PC laptops. It comes with a convenient carrying case that appears to be made of neoprene and has a zipper. When done using the speaker I wrap the cord around the speaker, place it in the sleeve, and place it in what computer bag I might be using that day. I also like that it is powered by the USB port and not battery operated.I can tell I am going to get a lot of use out of this little speaker whether it is using it with Skype or as an extra speaker to listen to music or videos. Jabra has impressed me over the last year and again, they did not fail with this product. I use Skype, but often have trouble getting to my screen, refreshing it, and clicking a button.  I decided to give Jabra a try.When a call is coming in, I just click the green button now.  Very convenient.  When more or less volume is needed, clicking on +/- works very well, and white LEDs appear to show the current volume level.  The speaker/microphone combo works fairly well.The USB cord is about a meter long, and wraps around the base when not in use. I needed aUSB Extensionfor my set-up -- I keep my non-noiseless computer in another room.The only drawback i've run into is that occasionally the speaker thinks it is the main speaker when I launch some games, and I'll hear Diablo coming through the Jabra speaker rather than my stereo speakers.  This takes a few seconds to fix on the rare cases where it happens.  My old set-up often required a few extra seconds to answer the phone, and I's much rather have an occasional minor Jabra problem for having easy phone answering.Recommended. I ordered this as I am often on skype on my phone and computer with both business partners and relatives that are not local. For the computer connection this unit is great but I haven't gotten my 4 connection cord to hook my phone to this unit in just yet. Though it works well with just audio put to it.The touch sensitive buttons on the unit make for easy adjustments while in a conference call and the quick mute access is perfect for use when clarifying information locally before continuing. Also the LED read out of volume level & Mute status is a great feature, along with the audible selection notification.Key features:Each button press returns a static like beep notification to let you know the button press worked.Buttons are touch sensitive, not tactile (no actual pushing of a button).Functions include:Answer call, End Call, Volume up and down, Mute.Muted: all LEDs around the perimeter of the speaker turn red and stay red until mute is deactivated.Un-muted: The bottom center LED remains white to let you know that mic is active.Volume level is indicated by the volume of the tone returned with each press of the - or + buttons along with the LEDs that form a circle around the speaker increasing or decreasing in the number that light up. These turn off after a couple seconds of the most recent button push.Volume is good for large offices, even with minor discussions taking place, microphone clarity is very good as well.A very good product overall, it would have just been nice to have gotten a proper cord for use with a cell phone as we often use a cellphone connection during interactive presentations for products.

name: JJC Waterproof Extremely Tough Memory Card Case MC-2 for 4 CF Cards 8 SD Cards
reviewText: This case gives me peace of mind. Very tough, can pack a lot of media cards. I could use two or three more of them heavy duty but the inside rubber is so rigid, that when I inserted my SD card it popped it in two.  Never really thought about it but the card itself is pretty brittle, thin plastic, so when I pressed it in, the memory card came apart at the seams, rendering it useless. Ironically, I want something to protect my cards, and I break it by using this very thing. And I've never damaged a card prior. This memory card case is adequate and does what it is advertised to do. For the price, I say but it. Small and light.  Haven't tested the waterproof feature.  Don't think I will test it either.  Cards fit snug but not too snug.  Easy purchase.  Seems like a quality product.  Would buy again. This is a nice case.  I think it would protect my memory cards from any damage if it were dropped, kicked or stomped.  It's too big to be really "convenient" like for a shirt pocket. But if you are interested in protecting your memory cards, it will be great for that.

name: Sandisk Ultra microSDHC UHS-I 32GB Class 10 Memory Card with Adapter (Upto 30 Mbps speed)
reviewText: A little hard to remove from backing but I got it. looks good on my Escape and seems that it will stay. Bought this for my son and he gladly uses two of those (black and blue, of course). Rubber feel nice to touch and seems quite reliable so far. Having a spare battery is essential when you're not able to charge your phone for an extended period. It's very easy to replace the battery in the Samsung Galaxy S4. Love it. I choose this skin because it was something from my childhood. I also purchased a black skin that is similar to this skin. Although they look great, they are more of a gimmick because of how loose the skin is on the Samsung Galaxy S3. They are not functional in everyday use because of how loose they are. But, they do looks cool and if you can figure out a way to make the skin tighter, then it is a five-star rating! I gave this 4 out of 5 stars because while this case looks and feel great you can tell that there is a tiny bit of play on the sides between the case and phone.  But maybe that is just me being nit picky.  But i do recommend this case for its great grip and sleek design.

name: Case Logic TBC-402 Point and Shoot Camera Case (Black)
reviewText: I bought this b/c another review said that it fit the Sony RX100 perfectly. However, I didn't realize that the RX100M2 is slightly thicker than the first version (RX100). My camera doesn't fit so I had to send it back. It looks like a great case and plenty durable, but don't get it if you have the Sony RX100M2. I use this case to hold my Canon Powershot S110 camera. Fits the camera like it was made for it. It's a soft case; I don't think it would protect too well from drops. But it's perfect if you don't want your camera rattling around loose in your bag or backpack.The fabric, clip, and zipper all seem sturdy, especially so given the price. There's a separate external pocket that I use to hold a spare battery and memory card. Perfect size case for my Kodak playsport. Well made lightly padded case to protect your purchase. Cant beat the price! Fits my Canon Powershot A4000 perfectly and side pocket easily holds 2 batteries. Seems like zippers and stitching will last long time. The 402 is a little larger than the 302.  It would also work great for the Canon A1400.  I am currently using several to hold USB/Charging cables and wall outlet adapters for Olympus point and shoot cameras -- SZ12 and VR-340.  (Side note - I use a Case Logic DCB-302 for the camera, extra battery, extra memory card, and cleaning cloth for each of these two cameras.  The DCB-302 is an entirely different case than the TBC-302).  If you are looking for a camera pouch for a Canon SX160 or SX170, or a Nikon L620, definitely take a close look at the TBC-403.  The 403 is a little deeper and accommodates the size of these three models very nicely.Case Logic are excellent cases.  They will serve you well once you find the right size for your camera and accessories.

name: Case Logic DSLR Camera Holster Tbc-406
reviewText: The item was returned as the camera I ordered came with a case..However the case was very well made and fit well. I have a Canon T4 and fits perfectly. The side pockets are a bit tight but this is mainly because the charger is huge for this camera so I have to put the charger on one side and the cable in the other so dont have any more space there.Front pocket is tight but perfect for a memory stick or a remote. I needed a case to help protect my Fujifilm X-S1 "bridge" camera when not in use, which this holster case does very well. It can hold the camera and its USB cable, its battery charger and a couple lenses. It's too small for the battery charger's AC cord and metal "petal-style" lens hood that came with the X-S1.If you're looking for a case to contain your DSLR camera and all of your accessories, you might be better served elsewhere (like Amazon's own AmazonBasics Large DSLR Gadget Bag). Seems to be well made and my camera with the 50MM lens fits nicely. Comfortable to carry and lightweight but with reasonable padding. I do wish the side pockets had a little more room to carry an extra battery or other items around that size. Overall a good buy. When I received this I was in doubt about it fitting my Fuiji camera with 50x closeup.  It fit my camera perfectly with room to spare.  The only thing I didn't like is that I thought there were more pockets for storage, but that's alright I'm just happy that the camera fit and the quality of the zippers is excellent.  Would definitely recommend this to my friends.

name: Ceptics Europe Travel Adapter, India to Europe (Schuko) plug - Type E/F European plug adapter, Universal adapter for Europ...
reviewText: It works in France as advertised.I did not have any issue with plugging this into the hotel sockets and my phone charged without issue. Works perfectly, very well built. Good for switzerland plugs. Tested and works. It should work with all household loads which do not have exceptionally high power requirements. Avoid using it with press or big microwave. Bought these to use recently on a trip to Australia and New Zealand.  They worked well.  We combined them with travel-size surge protectors for our camera, phone, and computer gear.  The surge protector verified that these adapters were providing a fully grounded charge.  They fit all of our devices and all of the outlets that we came across on our trip. More stable than the typical two prong adapter. Work just fine. What else can I say. The others are not grounded.

name: Logitech BCC950 Conference USB 2.0 HD 1080 Pixels, 3 Megapixel Cam, Optical, Black
reviewText: dropped in to the conference room for our training courses.  works great.  plug and play with windows 7.  may get another for home. Speakerphone is excellent without any echo and allows for conferencing within a room of 6 participants easily. The camera features coupled with the remote allows you to zoom and focus to the right person who is talking. Clarity at 720p is commendable. This little eye on a stalk does a pretty good job turning your chosen computer-based calling solution into a real live conference phone. Skype, Google Hangouts, join.me, Uberconference, etc. all work great with this device.Obviously, the most important thing is sound quality, and this does a remarkable job with both the speaker and the microphone. It's even tamed a wicked echo in the conference room at one of our offices.The camera is also very good quality - Logitech seems to have gotten that down. The pan and zoom are a nice feature, but since they require someone in the room to man them, it's easy to forget / fall behind. However, auto-follow is the domain of much more expensive conference solutions - and even those don't work that well - so I don't hold that against it.The look is... interesting. But I suppose the bobbing eye look is a fine trade off for getting more eye level for everyone. This webcam is a very good small conference room camera. The microphone works well and the picture quality is very good! I love the PTZ function on it and the sleek remote control. We use this for WebEx conferences and we love it so far! I bought some of these as an experiment with tele health at the company I work for.I was very impressed with the ease of set up, and quality of the image.  Given the price I was not expecting an amazing HD experience, but truly they surpassed expectations by quite a long way.  If you compare this to the typical built in web cam you might find in a laptop, these are a serious upgrade.

name: Manfrotto Quick Release Plate with Special Adapter (200PL)
reviewText: It's great, strong sturdy and easy to use, Just screw it to camera and then just put it on tripod, very easy to remove. Very sturdy system, you know it's solid and won't move. 4 stars because they are gray rather than black...? Would it cost so much more to dye the metal Black? Solid quick release plate that works flawlessly.  It stays snug on the head but is very easy to remove when needed.  The rubber will wear over time, but you will get good use out of well before you have to replace it. Nice, heavy duty. Works very well with my cameras. Very nice tight fit for a firm hold even on my Sony 70-400 G zoom lens. This is the normal small Manfrotto please. As plates go, it's OK. The one thing I don't like about the design of these plates is they will go on backwards and semi lock in (not securely). The Sachtler plates are better because they lock in securely in any direction. Anyway, it's great to have one or two extras in your kit because a missing tripod plate is the one thing that can ruin your day. It's easy to forget and leave them on other camera bodies you don't have with you. So buy one or two extras because they are cheap!

name: Canon EF-M 18-55mm f3.5-5.6 is STM Compact System Lens
reviewText: Defective. Started giving me Error 60 which is the lens. I gave it a shot, maybe a glitch. It got worse as I used it. Aperture would be at 0 and the screen would be dark. It would not take a picture. I had to reset by removing the battery. But it kept on getting worse. Returned the item to Amazon. Wished it worked. My 22 mm is now back and it never gives me any Error messages, ever since new. I still would like to get a replacement for the 18-55mm but I want one that works. Thanks. Because the other reviews describe this lens very well, I'll focus my attention on handling.While this lens is very good for the price, I find it a bit clumsy to carry and take pictures. I usually would prefer to use my feet to zoom closer than to use this zoom lens.  And, while the zoom lens is sharp enough, the prime lens is sharper - and don`t forget it`s wide open aperture is f2.Yes, the 18-55mm zoom is very good technically.  But, between the slow focus, the small camera body, and stiff zoom, it's awkward to handle quickly.  With this lens and no viewfinder on the M, I would miss most of my shots.  When I go out with the intention of shooting, like at the dog park, I use my Canon Rebel EOS T4i with my 50-200mm Ultrasonic zoom lens.  It's heavy with the battery grip, but with it I always get the picture.The M-zoom really is a good lens.  I think it's better than the regular Canon zoom lens of the same zoom range.  And I purchased it through e-bay for under $80.00. I do recommend it despite all my bitching.  But do shop around for price. I found this lens to be quite sharp and well made, and it focuses fine on the eos-m.  Good buy. All in all, I am very favorably impressed by the 18-55 STM.  It is sharper and smaller than the ef-s 18-55 Canon offerings.  It's also sharper than Sony's NEX 18-55 (I've owned all of these).  It focuses quickly and silently.  I had no trouble with focus noises in a couple of quick videos I did of my son playing basketball.  The only apparent drawback of this lens is that it will flare if there is a direct light source in or near the frame (especially the sun).  I know it is a common complaint about Canon, but they really should have included a hood with this one. This lens autofocuses faster than the 22mm STM pancake, but even with the new firmware update, the EOS-M is too slow for my needs (toddler). I found myself carrying around the camera with the 22mm simply because it could fit in my pocket, whereas this 18-55mm, which has very good build quality, was just too big.The EOS M isn't a DSLR replacement, it's a point-and-shoot replacement for DSLR owners and makes a great 2nd camera, but unless you carry it on a strap or have a purse/fannypack, it's not portable enough.

name: BlueRigger Audio RCA Cable with Gold Plated connectors (1 RCA Subwoofer Cable 8 FT / 2.4 Meters)
reviewText: Overall a good cable and it could be a little better if....Okay I have to say I have more experience than most. Lot's more, I'm an electronic tech, I've created the systems in a half dozen recording studios, I've created more club and concert systems than I can remember. What I would have different is a more flexible cable, which is more convenient, so more flexible for routing and maybe so a sub could be closer to a wall. The other thing is what's called strain relief which is the couple of inches near the end being strengthened to keep the strain off the wire to connector connection which then allows for a more flexible cable that's easier to route, see?I purposely headlined this review the way I did because there are no magical properties to a subwoofer cable and if you want, you can use any line level RCA to RCA cable. You'll find that a pair from HOSAHosa Cable CRA204 Dual RCA To Dual RCA Cable - 13 Footmight be less expensive and can be split for two sub cables while being more flexible with strain relief or maybe you already have a cable you can use. Likewise you could buy two of these to connect a device like a DVD to your receiver, because they're the same type of cable. Nice tight fitting ends, almost too tight but I like that. The ends are securely integrated into the cable and it has a nice heavy feel indicating it has proper shielding. My sub-woofer sounds great with it, and it easily carries all the signal without any noticeable degradation. The item was shipped quickly and arrived timely and was exactly as described & pictured. Good quality, good price, and works great with no problems even though I run the cable along many other cables (speaker, power, and Ethernet) that could possibly cause interference.I bought this to hook up a second SVS subwoofer, and they said this cable would be fine... and SVS knows subwoofers.I thought 35 feet might be a little long for me, but it wasn't. I'm glad I got this length and they offer it.Also, MADE IN CHINA (in case anyone cares)... and can't beat the lifetime warranty. Solid cable that is well-shielded with substantial connectors on each end. I do wish one was right-angle, but that was corrected easily enough with an adapter. Its ok. good price and gets the job done. all you can expect from a wire. looks good and delivers.

name: BlueRigger Bundle - Premium Mini DisplayPort (Mini DP) to HDMI Female Adapter + HDMI Cable (6 Feet / 1.8 Meters)
reviewText: There aren't really any negatives here.  I needed to get a replacement HDMI cable for my Raspberry Pi and an adapter for my Dell XPS13, and this bundle has both.  Each item performs as expected with no issues. I've bought several cables from bluerigger now, and have been pleased with the product each time.  I bought this bundle after doing some research on the specs necessary to play 3D content (HDMI 1.4 support needed) from a Surface Pro to my Asus VG23AH monitor (passive 3D - also a good product, though some of the reviews are negative on this well-priced item because the reviewers weren't using the right settings), and the bundle works perfectly for viewing 3D bluray movies.Cord and connector are great.  Only wish they had it in black! Haven't used it a lot but I did connect it to all of the displays that I have and it worked fine. At this price, this is a great product and well worth it. I am using a surface pro 2 and I had no problems. Plug and play, no drama, and at a really good price. Works very well with a Dell XPS 12 ultrabook/tablet convertible. This product is excellent. I have been using it for presentation and watching tv. Excellent quality output and I would recommend it.

name: BlueRigger Bundle Mini DisplayPort (Mini DP) to HDMI Female Adapter + HDMI Cable (10 Feet / 3 Meters)
reviewText: This cable was purchased so that i could use the mini DP on my surface pro and use my desktop monitor as an extended display. Both the HDMI cable and mini DP adapter work extremely well and feel very well built. If you have a surface pro (or any other device with a mini DP port) and wish to marvel at what it has to offer on a big screen, this is what you need! The adapter and the cable is a good combo. Good quality. It supports audio as well - no special settings other than telling your mac to use the HDTV speakers from the sound in preferences. I had hdmi cable, but it did not work and the cable that came with this helped me figure that out. The combo is worth it. Recommend this product! Supple cable. Tight connectors. Perfect connectivity. Great price. Will definitely look out Blue Rigger for future cable purchases. The end. Great for the price.  Sturdy with a good build quality.  Saved me a bundle by not having to pay sixty bucks for the Microsoft Surface version and works flawlessly with my first gen surface pro. I have had no issues using this product. All I needed to do was plug in the cable and it was ready to use. It works as it should with my Macbook Pro.

name: Sony SEL35F18 35 mm f/1.8 Prime Fixed Lens (Black)
reviewText: This is a very well made lens with optical image stabilization. The focal length is equivalent to a "normal" les in 35mm format. The f1.8 makes it a great lens for available light photography! It's a bit pricey, but, a whole lot less than the Carl Zeiss 24mm! If you bought a NEX-7 like I did and want a lens to replace the kit 18-55, this is one of the best candidates. F1.8 makes it really fast, and also creates very nice bokeh. There are other reviews from more intelligent users that compare this with other lenses, go into technical details etc. I don't have all the knowledge. I can only say that the image is sharp (as sharp as the NEX-7 will let it be, that is), AF is fast although I mostly use MF and the 35mm creates a nice field of view, although on a APS-C sensor it is gives the appearance of a 50mm.Also, prime lenses force you to think before you shoot, to frame the picture, compose it and if necessary walk around to find the best spot and angle for your shot. Zooms make you lazy, but they can be useful too, I suppose. :)I took my kit lens off and put this one on. The only time I put the kit lens back on is when I need a wide angle shot, otherwise this one stays on for 90% of the time. This lens is not noticeably sharper that the 3.5-5.6/18-55 kit lens as measured by a few casual tests to determine if I could see an improvement. Nope. I mainly use it on my NEX-5N at indoor events with friends and family for casual shooting without a flash. At f-1.8 It's much better than the kit for this kind of use and is the reason I got it. An obvious disadvantage of any fast lens is that depth of focus can be a problem you need to be aware of. And sometimes a wider angle requires a swapping with the zoom. These factors reduce its usefulness to me.I've had problems with the aperture blades not working. The aperture simply stays full open (1.8) resulting in a number of totally overexposed shots. IOW, the lens views and focuses while fully open as it should but does not close down to the proper higher f-setting. If this continues I will have to get a refund or replacement.I decided not to return it yet only because at 1.8-2.8 I can get handheld shots that are otherwise impossible. It has good image stabilization and focuses noticeably more rapidly -- especially in darker settings -- than the kit. If it were in the two hundred dollar range it would be a reasonable buy, but at twice that it's not. Great lens especially for street photography. I bough this lens for my NEX-6 and it's a very nice lens.  With the 1.8 focal length, you can get a nice Bokeh effect.

name: Monoprice 5 Pairs Gold Plated Speaker Banana Plugs, Closed Screw Type
reviewText: MUCH nicer than trying to screw the speaker wires down to the posts. These are simple to attach and easy to use. Remember to match the black and red tips to the same side of each speaker wire. These were a great price and are of great quality; I would buy these again rather than at Home Depot or Lowes. Shipped quickly These are pretty well made but I still haven't found these that are really convenient to use.  But they do the job and look nice. Makes my theater setup look a lot better than plain wires.  Easy to put together. These are very high quality, durable, and easy to use banana plugs.  I use these on 14 gauge speaker wire and have had no problems.

name: D-Link DWA-182 Wireless AC1300 Dual Band USB 3.0 Adapter, Black
reviewText: I bought this adapter along with D-link DIR-865L AC1750 router to be able to transfer large files fast over the wireless connection. Installation of both the router and this adapter took no more than 10 minutes, and I was happy to see 585Mbps connection between my Windows 8 desktop and the router... until I tried to copy a 2GB file from my desktop to my NAS drive. The transfer speed was just 11MBps (approximately 88mbps), just a little bit faster than my old N300 router could handle... and that's not even the worst part of the story. During the transfer, my desktop lost wireless connection. I opened device manager and couldn't find wireless adapter under network controllers at all. It simply disappeared. I removed it from the USB port and put it back - nothing. Put it into another USB port - nothing. Both USB ports on the front of my desktop just stopped working. My desktop couldn't recognize any device connected to them. I turned off my desktop, removed power cord from the wall outlet, and, after a few minutes, turned on the desktop. This time, thanks God, both USB ports worked just fine. From my experience, such kind of things happens when some device, connected to USB port, requires more power than the USB port can supply. Long story short, I tried 16 different USB ports on 2 desktops and 1 laptop (let me say, modern desktops and laptop with both USB2 and USB3 ports) and found a few ports which could handle this adapter's power requirements while transferring large files better than others. Even now, most of the time, I wasn't able to transfer any files larger than 3-4GB. I think this adapter has a major design flaw which could probably be fixed by firmware or driver update... but let's see what's the latest driver's date on D-link website. It's dated 10/29/2012, and it's major advantage, according to D-link - "Supports Windows Vista". It doesn't even officially supports Windows 8 (but in fact works with it, I must say). Six months without any updates... Well, I better return this thing to Amazon and buy adapter from another brand. I use with a Dlink AC 1750 and it performs great.  No real install problems.  Using the adapter on a home theater PC for streaming to internet base content as well and recorded TV.  I use the 5GHz band for media streaming, and the 2.4GHz band for routine networking and internet access for everything else.  No complaints. By itself this is a good card, like if you have a Desktop PC. On my laptop however it breaks the Realtek Driver. Microsoft has a knowledge base page that explains the issue and basically says you can't run this adapter with another brand's adapter. This wouldn't be such an issue if it weren't for the fact that even when this adapter isn't connected the other won't work. I've been using the DWA-182 for the past week now, with an Asus AC66U wireless router, to see if 802.11ac was really all that. My initial thoughts were that this USB device was huge and that it would block lots of USB ports. Another concern I should voice is that it is still only USB 2.0, so you will be limited to the bus speed of 480Mbps (about half of the 867Mbps promised). Connection has been very stable and although the driver has not been updated since the initial release, it does seem decent and works well on my Windows 8 x64 system.My biggest complaint is about the transfer speeds. Using this adapter, connected at 867Mbps (according to Windows) and sitting 15 feet from the router (no obstructions), I was able to transfer an 800MB file in 42s to a computer hardwired to the router, on Gigabit Ethernet. Same file took 40s using my internal 5Ghz 802.11n Intel card, with the otherwise same setup. With other files, the transfer rate in MB/s that Windows 8 reports is about the same on both wireless cards consistently. I'm not entirely sure what this is about, but I do think you should wait for a new USB 3.0 version with better throughput, or use a PCI-E card if on a desktop system. Bought this adapter and a d-link router to match it. Not really so great. I bought the adapter in November 2012 it died today 5/23/2013.Using my old adapter now. DWA-140 seem to work just as well.

name: Transcend TS-RDF5K USB 3.1 Gen 1 Card Reader (Black)
reviewText: Bought this to make it simpler to transfer pictures from my Canon 70D and it does exactly that.Cheap, fast and means I don't have to plug the camera in (or make sure I have sufficient battery power remaining) in order to transfer pictures. Also connecting it to a USB 3.0 port sees much faster transfer speeds than I would have experienced with the USB 2.0 built in to the camera.Works great on Windows 7. its so fast I had the Kingston USB reader before this one & it was bulky and felt cheap. This one doesn't feel that way, plus it doesn't block your other USB ports. It just works, plus it's very portable. I'd recommend getting this one over the Kingston one. Contrary to what some may say, there is absolutely nothing wrong with Transcend memory products. The little RDF5 USB 3.0 reader is a typical Transcend product. The USB flash card reader is small in size and will read all SD, micro SD memory cards including UHS-1. The reader allows the user to use whatever SD or micro SD memory card volume size is needed to contain the data, not limiting the data files to the capacity of a USB "flash drive".  Reading and writing from the memory card is like any other USB device. Backward compatible to USB 2.0 devices and ports. The most current firmware is available for download, as well as a image recovery software from Transcend. 4/5 Good unit, reads cards and doesn't conflict with anything on my older XP/Linux box. I down rated it because the side connect for SDHC cards is awkward. I would much prefer the SD cards in the end of the stick (like the old IOGear units). It does what I bought it for and it works on ALL my USB equipped devices (media players, routers, NAS storage, laptops, and desktops)

name: micca MB42 75 Watt Bookshelf Speaker (Black)
reviewText: The website description list the Impedance as : 4-8 Ohms.Not being a physicist, an electrical engineer, or someone with advanced expertise in audio equipment, I assumed that this meant that these speakers would work with my 8-ohm receiver.HOWEVER, the speaker manual that is delivered with the speakers reads: "The MB42's impedance VARIES between 4 to 8 Ohms. Care must be taken to ensure that the amplifier is capable of handling a 4-Ohm load. ...  ... Improper amplifier selection or setup may result in permanent damage to the amplifier or speaker."IF this information was included in the website description, I would not have purchased these speakers. I am just a guy who wanted to buy a pair of speakers on-line, plug them in, and enjoy them without having to worry that they might damage my receiver, and without having to invest the extra time into figuring out whether or not my amplifier is safe.Being a normal busy human being, returning a box of speakers via the mail is quite an inconvenience. I discussed this situation with some electrically savy friends of mine. One of them said that as long as I do not turn the volume up too high, I should be fine. Since I had been needing a new pair of speakers for sometime, and was not looking forward to wasting my Saturday morning going to the post office, I decided to plug them in. At first they sounded great. Then over time, I found that the sound quality seems to vary from great to good to "dirty", for a lack of a better descriptive word. Now, after 4 weeks, I experience a phenomenon where I am enjoying my music at my desired volume and then, suddenly, the volume lowers, on it's own. The volume then stays at this lower level for some time, say ten - fifteen minutes or even longer, until it eventually shifts back up the the originally set volume. Again, I am "assuming" that this phenomenon is being caused by the varying impedance of the speakers. I finally decided to invest a few hours this morning to take a trip to the post office to return these speakers, only to determine that the Return "Window" expired last week.Now I will wearily utilize these speakers until I have the funds to replace them with dependable speakers and discard these speakers, while hoping that my amplifier survives unscathed. UPDATE: Much later, after replacing the bad little "woofer" these speakers have held up very well... and I listen to dubstep at insane levels for hours at a time, so you know they are good, going from 4 stars to 5 stars...UPDATE: The little "woofer" was covered under warranty and is easy to replace.  They sent me a replacement and I am all good now.  Upgrading to 4 stars for prompt response to the issue.I bought these speakers a few months ago and one of them is already buzzing and getting worse.They are a little tinny sounding to begin with, if not paired with a good sub-woofer, they wouldn't be very good. Pros:These speakers really astounded me.  I was looking for "decent" speakers and super cheap.  I ended up with INCREDIBLY clear sound, natural tones, and surprisingly robust low end! No, they're not audiophile quality, but they perform like significantly more expensive speakers!  Not only that, they're pleasant to look at, and they even have solid post/banana connections for heavy gauge wire!  I'm not sure how well they'd handle high power, though.  I've got them on a 90watt Pyle Amp and they do great!Cons:None to speak of! I haven't heard the least bit of distortion or muddiness from these wood-cabinet speakers. We just replaced some much bigger, 25 year old speakers with these.  They sound better and their small size is great!They are a terrific value. We needed a sound boost for our flat screen TV which sounds, well, flat. Paired these speakers with the little Lepai amp and it sounds fantastic!

name: Microware HDMI Audio Splitter Converter Supports 3D/4Kx2K to Analog Audio Left and Right Channels 5.1
reviewText: This did not work for me. I got it specifically for the Wii U which has no optical audio out. A lot of sounds did not come through like weapon reloads and other things even though the main soundtrack could be heard. I was pretty disappointed so if anyone else out there is searching for a work around with the Wii U sound this isn't it. The Tivo mini does not have separate digital audio output, only two channel analog or HDMI.This adapter lets me receive multi channel audio with my older TOSLINK-only receiver.My only concern with the adapter (instead of giving it 5 stars) is that the behavior I noticed did not match the Kanex website's documentation or FAQ.The Kanex website says that it will simultaneously down mix to 2 channel audio while passing multichannel audio.  (I planned to use this for my analog-only zone-2 application.  The adapter does not down mix.  It will only drive both digital and analog outputs with 2 channel PCM sources.Lastly, the documentation's information regarding status light meaning is exactly opposite of my experience in real life. I have an older (by today's standards) AV Receiver. It does not have HDMI inputs/outputs. It did have optical inputs. I just bought a new smart tv and a Sony Blu ray player that has only one HDMI and one coaxial output. Obviously this will not allow for my audio to play through my receiver. This device does exactly what it says it does. I take the HDMI output from the Blu ray player into the Kanex input and route the HDMI output from the Kanex into the TV and the optical output goes to my receiver. I now can play CD's and play them through my receiver (5.1 channel). it sounds great. A simple device that does exactly as its designed to do. I can't be more pleased. It did the trick.We have a control room where the computer is and just outside we wall mounted a monitor for the users to see the screen and HEAR when their training is expired. This worked well as a solution to get auido out of the computer and the wall mounted TV. I'm sure this box works great for some people, but with my setup, it did not. name: Big Mike's Pack of 2 LP-E12 Replacmenet Batteries for Canon Rebel SL1 EOS-M Mirrorless Digital Camera + More
reviewText: I recently purchased a Canon Rebel SL1 and the first thing I did was buy extra batteries. There's absolutely no worse feeling than trying to get the perfect shot when "Replace battery pack" shows on the screen. This 2 pack of replacements is very inexpensive, however I feel like I get every bit as much life from them as I do from my original battery. I haven't actually tested to see exactly how they compare, but I haven't noticed them lasting a substantially shorter amount of time than the stock batteries. I figured if they didn't quite have the capacity, at least I'd have two. Now I happily have 3 good batteries for my camera. The next question will be how many charge cycles they last through, but for the price, I don't mind buying another 2 pack if I need to down the road. These are far less expensive and give me the same amount of shots at the original Canon battery.  I don't know how they will hold up across time, but for the price difference, I'll be able to buy new ones and still come out on top. Batteries are good and hold charge. I think my Canon battery is defective. Canon battery wears down faster than these batteries. One thing that needs to be addressed is the shipping box. I got the product with the clear screen protector bent. So it was useless. At the time of this review this battery is made by Bower, model XPDCE12 For Canon LP-E12, in China.  It is rated at 7.4v 1400 mAh and the original Canon LP-E12 battery is rated at 7.2v 875 mAh.  In a few cycles of charge and discharge I have yet to notice any battery hysteresis, but they seem to hold a charge a little longer than the OEM.  Again, this is not scientific and I don't have any conclusive data at this point. It is based on initial observations. I have seen no detrimental performance in the EOS M mirror-less camera at this time.  For the price and performance it seems to be a winner. I needed a cheap alternative to the Canon OEM batteries for my EOS-M and these did the trick.At less than half the cost, they have roughly 70% of the capacity of the OEM batteries and work great to augment the relatively short life of the OEM LP-E12 battery.The battery indicator is a bit wonky with these battery in that at times they go from a full charge to flashing low, and this may be due to these 3rd party batteries lacking the computer chip on the OEM battery.Either way, they serve my purpose of letting me shoot for several hours without needing to re-charge.

name: Just Mobile Headstand for Heaphones with Headband (HS-100)
reviewText: I like this stand. It is so much better than plastic ones (I have plastic one as well). name: Wasabi Power Battery for GoPro HD HERO3, HERO3+ and GoPro AHDBT-201, AHDBT-301, AHDBT-302
reviewText: Unfortunately GoPro sucks the juice down faster than it should, resulting in horrible battery life & frequent change-outs required.  That's not Wasabi's fault, so I give them a 4/5.  The -1 is for the tape peeling off as you try to lift it out of the GoPro.  I'm not sure if it's just the type of battery, but it seems to take 2hrs to charge for ~ 30 min video, not very practical. I get between 20-40 minutes more life out of this battery than the one my Hero3 came with. I am not sure if that is because that battery is a year old or this is better? After 4 months of use no issues with the battery. I have also never had my camera freeze up on me with the battery. The stock battery the camera will sometimes freeze and require me to pull the battery to reset it. It has never done that with this battery. more juice than stock hero 3 battery, charges just as fast as stock battery.  only as with other comments mentioned, the tape at the back is quite soft and not firm, and is a bit tight fit thus harder to pull out I took off one start on principe because these batteries seem to have slightly lower true capacity then original GoPro battery, no matter what the label on the battery claims.  I don't like when manufacturers overrate specs on the label.Said that, in real world use it is not really that bad.  If I let camera record video with freshly charged battery until battery dies, I get about 1 hour and 13 minutes with original GoPro battery, and about 1 hour and 10 minutes with Wasabi battery (using same recording settings, under same conditions, etc).  At half the price of original, 3 minutes less of recording time isn't that much of an issue.  If you want to buy two of these, Wasabi also sells 2-pack combo that comes with dedicated wall/car charger.  If you go through multiple batteries in single day, definitely buy 2-pack combo with charger instead of two individual batteries, so that you can charge multiple batteries in parallel (one in camera, one in dedicated charger). Perfect for the Gopro hero 3 or 3+. The tab on the battery is a little more flimsy, but does not affect any performance. Still able to pull the battery out easy enough.

name: Jabra Speak 510 10 Watt Wireless Bluetooth Portable Speaker (Black)
reviewText: As with other reviews, the folks on the other end heard lots of echo.  I had to return it. I was looking for a speaker for my daily conferences. I nailed it! You can be hear and hear other clearly. Good improvement to our meeting room. Switch between your computer phone (Lync) and your cell phone with a push of a button. I've used this in the car (similar to a built-in blue tooth) as well. It is generally easier to hear and be heard than most car stereo systems. It's also great for road warriors who find themselves needing to attend a conference call and learn the conference room they're connecting doesn't have a phone. Pull out your cell phone, BT-connect it to the Jabra, and you have an conf-call quality phone connection.I owned the unit prior to this that did not feature the Bluetooth. While it was a good product, the difference in value of having BT functionality goes well beyond the $10 price difference (though I suppose the older model was discontinued). This device does a great job at being a mobile speakerphone. It also plays music. The battery lasted me about 6 hours and it charges via micro usb. Setup is a breeze. It comes with a case. Music playback is just average quality but gets very loud. People had very little trouble hearing me in an office...All that being said... I'm actually in sales. I have lots of friends in both outside and inside sales. I have no idea why this product exists. I cannot imagine much need for a mobile speakerphone outside the office that a descent cell phone wont be able to handle. Also this will amplify your connection. It won't magically make it better. So if you have poor reception (more likely if you're traveling with this device some place far from an office) it will magnify all the hissing and noise. I use this unit as an external speaker for my laptop, and it does a great job.  It's compact, has good volume - enough to fill a conference room sized room.  All I had to do was unpack it, plug the USB jack into my laptop, sit back, wait for a driver to load, and it was ready to go!  Easy.It has its own volume control, and intuitive controls for switching between modes.This speaker pulls its power from the laptop, so there's no separate wall plug to hassle you.I also like the neoprene sipper pouch that comes with it, so I don't have to worry much about it getting bonked while it's in my shoulder bag with my laptop, etc.I you are looking for a small, yet powerful external speaker, this unit may work for you.5 stars - does what it is designed to do, easily and with a shallow learning curve.

name: Nikon 8245 ACULON A211 8x42 Binocular (Black)
reviewText: This one is the first real binocular i bought(previous ones were more of cheap roadside stuffs), therefore i do not have a lot to compare with. name: Nikon ACULON A211 10x50 Binoculars
reviewText: A few years ago, I bought my daughter a pair pair of $600 Leupold 10x50 roof prism binocs that wee exceptional. She's an avid birder! But recently, I wanted to update my 7x26's so tried out a lot of binocs. For about $120, this pair of porro prism binocs performs exceptionally well. They are not water-proof, fog-proof or light weight. There is some curvature of field, and some chromatic aberration at the edges. But the view is fantastic!Seriously... I don't go bird watching in the rain, and frankly, the bird is always centered while trying to ID. So all those 'negative' aspects that raise the price to $1,000 or more just don't offer true value for money, at least for me. If you have been following binocular design for a while, you will know that porro prism designs are much easier to optimize, and that many early roof prism model were very dark and had similar negative properties. Some birding sites actually recommend similar Nikon porro prism models for quality of view. I also like the rubberized grip of this model, they fit the hand well and have good eye clearance, though I don't wear glasses.If you can, visit a store that lets you try out a number of models... you'll be surprised at how much binocular $120 can buy! these are a great size, excellent clarity, good zoom feature easy to use and a solid investment, definitely satisfiedthanks Nikon I bought these Aculon A211 10x50 Binoculars on sale from a retail sporting goods store. I was able to test them out in the store and also outside. I liked the bright,sharp and contrasty view these Binoculars provided. Everything looked great at the store so I decided to buy a pair.They feel solid in the hand and all the adjustments are smooth and well dampened. The rubber coating is solid and provides both protection and grip. Nikon used a different texture on the thumb grips similar to what my Digital SLR has.The optics are very sharp compared to an older pair of Minolta 10-22x50 Binoculars that I was borrowing from my father. While this particular pair on Aculon A211 is fixed at 10 power I can actually see more detail in every type of lighting condition compared to my fathers Minolta's at 22 power! The images are free of distortion once you are focused on your subject. However I did notice that if something is out of focus the bottom of the image will have a sort of fisheye effect until the image is brought into focus. Once focused on something the distortion disappears.One more benefit to these A211's is the generous eye relief. So if you wear glasses like I do then you won't have any issues. The shoulder strap is the same size as the one on my Nikon D7000 DSLR so its plenty big for a pair of 10x50 binoculars like this. The Aculon 10x50's are not heavy at all.These Binoculars come with a nice sized case which has plenty of room to fit the Binoculars in. You don't have to fiddle with anything just slip the Binoculars right in and your on your way.The front and rear lens caps are good not great. The rear cap slips on easy, but the front caps clip onto the inside rim on the rubber overhang on the objective lens. They have a secure fit but I think they might get lost easily if you don't pay attention to them.Overall I'd recommend these to anyone. They are sharp and well made Binoculars at a great price. These binoculars are perfect for my wife and I to view wild life, etc., as we camp and fish as well as travel. They are steady as you try to hand hold and view images. The focus is easy and exact. These are the best binoculars I have ever owned. It seems like I have owned dozens of Bushnells and Tascos. Not only do these brands have inferior optics but they do not hold up either. They tend to come out of alignment over time and thus are rendered useless. The Nikons have a bold and bright image and are exceptionally clear. It is the first binocular I have ever owned without wanting to upgrade. The downside. They are a little clunky and heavy. If you are a pure fan of portability than these may not be for you.I,however, am a happy camper.

name: Nikon ACULON A211 -10-22 x 50 8252 Binocular (Black)
reviewText: Most of the others I've used lose acuity on higher settings. These stay sharp and are easy to focus. In my opinion, Nikon offers the best dollar for dollar value in binocular optics. name: Sony NP-BX1/M8 Lithium-Ion X Type Battery (Silver)
reviewText: No problems using it interchangeably with the original battery that came with the camera.  Works as well as could be expected. One thing I've learned over the years is that you get what you pay for. Although most brand specific items are a bit pricier on one hand, I've rarely had issues when it came down to where the rubber meets the road. Photography is a passion and I used to use "other brands" to save money. Well... it's a 50/50 shot as to what the ultimate satisfaction will be.This battery is an extra, to have ready when I need it. As with other Sony batteries, I've only had one, in the past 8 years that's had an issue. It turned out to be a crooked contact within the top cap. Amazon sold it direct and I had a replacement within a day and half, sending the other back through an easy and simple process, dropping it off with UPS. Done deal.Yes... it's a little more than most, but I still have many of the spares after all these years and have never had an issue with charging, sudden or dramatically shortened use cycles, or someone passing off a fake that looks like the genuine Sony product. I've stated many times in other reviews that buying an items that's directly from Amazon or Amazon playing the intermediate, has proven the way the go. Mind you, there've been rare occasions I've purchased from "other" sellers and the inevitable happened a couple times. Read everything and save a copy of the actual description page for that seller. Trust me... it usually will turn out in your favor, as it should.But, back to this item, you can't go wrong and it's been used in my Cybershot camera's with no signs of degradation after using and charging at least 3 complete kill/charge cycles a week sometimes. They get used in the DSC-HX50V and the DSC-RX100 v1, which I bought recently and will review. All I can really say is that it's the perfect battery for both of those cameras. Paying a little more in the beginning has given peace of mind that they'll work when I need them to and they'll last a good while before needing replacement. It all comes down to the usage patterns. It's not that much more expensive than a 3rd party battery.  I trust the manufacturer's battery always.  I'm always out on long trips, and swapping out batteries for my camera is a must.  I don't have to worry if the battery will bulge and get stuck, catching fire, leaking, dying early, etc..  Just spend a bit more for some solid peace of mind. You never know when you need another battery.  I stayed with the factory Sony because the cost (compared to generic unknown quality) isn't worth the loss of video time.  If you paid for an expensive vacation where you are using a camera like this, it doesn't make sense to depend on an unknown generic battery that may fail or damage your expensive Sony camera. So sticking with a known brand at a higher price - sometimes that's the correct choice. does not hold a charge well.  I had to end up  buying a whole battery charger setup (since the battery charger is through the camera.

name: Manfrotto Lightweight Fluid Tripod Video Head with Flat Base (MVH500AH)
reviewText: I'm a freelance photographer and videographer, and I've been building up my gear piece-by-piece for a while now, and I needed a fluid video head. I'd cruised around and looked at hundreds of heads, and debated between this and a cheaper, highly-rated Cowboy Studio brand head. I decided that it was worth the extra little bit of money to get the Manfrotto brand, and I was right! I have experience using a heavy tripod set with a heavy-duty Manfrotto head, and this one performs fantastically!I have not had much field testing experience with it yet, but these are my opnions and findings:- It's smaller than I thought it would be, but it still has fantastic quality. Luckily, smaller is sometimes better when it comes to portability.- The fliud drag controls are easy to use and are effective for making small adjustments. These are not 'on/off' controls, but rather incremental adjustments for how much force you have to use for pans and tilts.- The tripod plate attachment mechanism is new to me. I've used the slide-in method, and this is a side-slide-in method. Is it better? I'm not sure. This does seem a little more secure, since if the clamp is nottightened, your plate (and camera) still will not fall off, although they will slide around. I think it's a clever system, but I can see how it could be slightly frustrating with bigger camera bodies or rig setups. There's a chance that if your setup is too wide, you won't be able to tilt it enough to slide the plate in.- The handle is well-made with a good rubber grip on it (not much else to say about it, it's a handle).- The pre-weighted balance on it will help those who have a large DSLR or a medium-sized video camera, but you will be frustrated if you're slapping a GoPro/Handycam on it, or a heavy-duty studio quality camera. I use a Canon 5D Mark III, and the balance is just about perfect with the body and a mid-sized lens on it. With some balance tweaking, it can easily handle attachments (mic/light/monitor).- Something I wasn't expecting, but I am pleasantly surprised about is the 3/8" attachment on the left-hand side of the tripod head. This means that with the right attachments, you can put a magic arm or mount on the side to hold a monitor, mic, audio capture gear, or light (heck, maybe even a cupholder!.......although I wouldn't recommend that).- The instructions are mostly visual instructions with a small amount of written ones. If you're familiar with video fluid tripod heads, then this won't be an issue (although I highly recommend reading through the instructions and visuals anyways). If you're not familiar with the way these heads work, definitely read the instructions or look up Manfrotto's video tutorials on their website or through YouTube.- Your tripod head is only as sturdy as your legs are. Please, please, PLEASE don't spend money on a quality head and slap it onto weak, broken, unsteady, or low-quality legs.- Keep in mind that balancing camera gear and getting smooth, fluid pans and tilts is more of an art than a science. You will get better shots the more you practice with this, so don't be frustrated if your first few shots aren't quite where you thought they'd be. Practice, practice, practice!I put this on top of Oben AC-2320LA 3-Section Aluminum Lateral Tripod Legs, and it seems like a very sturdy setup!Bottom line: This head will hold most photographers/videographers gear (if you're shooting DSLR/medium sized video camera), and will allow you to get solid, smooth pans and tilts. It's hard to beat this for the money. If you're on the edge about whether you need a bigger head or not, I would recommend Googling more reviews comparing different tripod heads (or go to your local camera shop and try them out!) I own multiple Manfrotto heads and this is my favorite for DSLR shooting because of it's smaller profile and awesome quick connect plate that lets you snap a camera in from the top instead of sliding in from the rear of the unit. Absolutely love it. It's made my videos so much cleaner and it's easy to use once you play around with it and get a feel for it. The price isn't too bad for it either but you honestly get what you pay for. I recommend this to anyone who is getting into videography or even photography I have started shooting more video with my 5D and wanted something other than my ball head for video. I already have a Manfrotto 055X carbon fiber tripod and wanted something that would go onto that quickly. What a breeze! Just unscrew the ballhead, screw this one on and away you go. Probably 30 seconds to make the change. What I wanted was something very lightweight and compact. This head fit the bill perfectly. The fluid movements are really wonderful.
