Perfectly dampened and with springs to help return it to level. Smooth as silk! The sliding baseplate is plenty long enough to balance the camera with a long lens attached. I have the Canon 70-200 and there are no issues balancing. It is not necessary to use the lens mounting option at all. Just slide the camera back with the plate on the camera and balance is quickly achieved. The finishes are very nice and everything seems to lock down properly. It would certainly support a heavier camera. Overall I am very very happy with the purchase. The pan/tilt handle can be locked in most any position and used on the left or right side. This is really a GREAT choice for smooth pans and tilts and you really cannot beat the price for this very high quality head. Buy it and you will not be disappointed! I needed a fluid head to take videos of my daughter in rowing competitions.  After some practice, this did the job perfectly.  It has the right combination of size and utility for the amateur videographer who needs to get a good, clean, fluid pan.

name: Manfrotto MTPIXI-B PIXI Mini Tripod (Black)
reviewText: I picked this up at a local store since it seemed like a good option over a pistol grip for my camera. As a mini tripod that costs $25 I'm not all that sure what people expect it to do. It holds a camera steady as a tripod and offers a stable hold as a grip. Its a no frills, easy to use tripod. Costing $25 you should realize that it is made out of plastic and isn't a carbon fiber mini tripod with an included hydrostatic ball head with a clutch design...lets be real people.Some state the ballhead isn't smooth and is "sticky." If you look at the design the metal is textured to assist with increased grip and decreased creeping with your camera attached. One look at it and anyone would see this was done for a reason.The button is not simple to push but upon taking it apart the mechanism is designed this way to allow for the maximum hold in consideration of the materials and obviously the price point.This holds my OMD EM5, GX7 with a Panasonic 35-100 without issue. My 7D with a nifty fifty shows minimal creep but it does hold well.Overall this mini tripod does what it claims to do and for the price its actually a good deal! this is a good small tripod and when folded it fits nicely in the hand to hold the camera stable while you shoot. Ergonomic sturdy and functional. A very nice little tripod with a one button release/adjust mechanism. The legs fold in to make a very comfortable hand grip. Unlike the Gorillapod style tripods, these legs will not sag with the weight of a camera on them. Awesome look and feel... Fits in almost anywhere in a camera bag, light weight and easy to use. Only downside is the ball is kinda stiff and I'm hoping it loosens up with extended use... Manfrotto are great mid range products. Stiff and useful.Little push-hold strength on the Logo(safety button for the head join to move around).I recommend for a optional use for a tripod.

name: Lowepro LP36576-PWW 250 AW Transit Sling Bag (Slate Grey)
reviewText: I have wanted a sling back for about two years now. Although I have a bag that perfectly and snuggly fits my Canon Rebel with the kit lens, I sometimes prefer to carry multiple lenses, or to use my camera backpack to store all incidentals such as a wallet and glasses, etc.This bag is this bag. It's sturdy, durable, lightweight, comfortable to sling around, doesn't get dirty easily. I can't sing its praises enough. I like it more than a camera backpack because of its spacious dividers, but not as large of a volume of the bag itself.In lieu of sounding like a fangirl, I really love this bag! I've owned a couple of Lowepro camera bags and they always have surprisingly good hidden features.  The general build quality is high and I know from experience that they generally use materials that last.Here are the features of this particular bag:1) Single shoulder strap - not just less dorky than a double strapped backpack, the real advantage of this system is that you can move the drop the bag from your back to your side without removing it, by rotating the bag across your body.  This is only useful because one of the two ways of accessing the bag is a side-mounted pocket that's perfect for a mid-sized camera body and medium lens.  If you need additional support, there is a hidden strap on the right side that plugs into the single shoulder strap about half-way up.  I thought this would create a waist strap, but instead it gives you a very strange triangular attachment that leaves all the weight of the pack on a single (right) shoulder but prevents excessive lateral movement.2) Waterproof cover - one of the major selling points of any Lowepro bag, this is a little poncho for your bag that stores in a pocket in the base of the pack.  If you're caught in a sudden downpour, it's convenient enough to pull out and cover the bag within a few seconds.3) Tripod carrying system - a fixed loop, an adjustable loop, and a pocket that drops out of another hidden pocket conspire to give you a way of carrying any reasonably compact (max 15 inch collapsed height) tripod.4) Internally re-configurable - lots of velcro separators and a clever panel that's the width of the pack but contains a lens shaped cut-out means you should be able to accommodate some combination of a small-bodied SLR-type camera with a lens attached and a couple of other lenses OR a full-sized SLR with a zoom lens that protrudes 8 inches from the body.  The maximum internal dimensions of this padded pack are: 14 x 8 x 4 inches, although the shape of the pack means if your lens is longer than 8 - 9 inches and you want it stay on your camera you probably need a bigger bag.5) Extra pockets - a tablet/document pocket right next to your back (but still well padded), an outside zip pocket for small items, a mesh pocket for lens caps, and an internal zip pocket with a key loop all give you extra flexibility6) Lightness - by any standards this is a lightweight pack - it feels like it weighs about 2 pounds at most.This is great for traveling with your camera for quick access, but only if you're carrying your camera as a carry-on on an airplane - I wouldn't trust my camera to the luggage hold in this bag.  It's great, but it's not indestructible... Usually, I just take my camera with one fixed lens and one mid-range zoom to everyday events. I have been using larger backpack type bags, but they have more room than I need. I also tend to carry more stuff in the larger bags I don't really need. If it were lost or stolen, I'd end up losing more. This sling bag is just right for my son's soccer games or other local events I find myself going to. It is has secure storage for the camera and 2 lenses, as well as smaller stuff like extra batteries and sd cards. There is a portion between the back and front designed to slip flat things in, but I think a tablet is more appropriate than a laptop, which may not even fit.I like the way it is designed so the camera with a short lens can fit side ways in the bottom portion or you can open a flap in the middle to stick the camera with a long lens suspended downwards. I just noticed the images on the product page showing a guy wearing the sling strap over his head. I never thought of that. I have been throwing it over my left shoulder then securing it with the front cross strap that snaps to the sling so it stays secure. Either I'm wearing it wrong or it can be down either way. Still, it works for me.So, I like this because it is small and just the right size for small, everday events, but I also have a larger backpack style camera bag for situations I want to bring more lenses. perfect bag for city sightseeing or traveling light  it fits my d7000 with 17-50mm lens perfect  it is light and comfortable to wear for long time This is a really nice sling bag. The best feature is that you can quickly slide it to your front and unzip the quick access zipper to get your camera in and out quickly. You don't have to take the backpack completely off every time you want access to your camera. The only issue I have with this is that when you adjust the height you have to wear it a bit lower on the back than I like in order to have it low enough when I slide it to the front. Maybe this is just because I am a bit short (5'4"). A taller person may not have this issue. If I wear it a bit higher up like I prefer, then when I slide it to the front the bag is a bit too high and awkward to use. The fact that there is a reinforcing strap that comes off the bottom of the bag helps make the bag more stable though.Overall, this is a great medium sized bag with lots of compartments. It is well padded and keeps the camera very safe.

name: SMALLRIG Super Lightweight 15mm Railblock 3 with 1/4"-20 Thread for Red and Other 15mm DSLR Camera Rig - 942
reviewText: This railblock, although just a tiny piece of black anodized aluminum, works well in conjunction with a number of rail applications when mounting camera gear. We used this piece as our veritable linchpin to hold together a RED Scarlet clip-on mattebox whose mechanism was damaged, and it worked out perfectly. …and the extra holes, threaded and not, are very helpful for customizing my rig.Also the repositionable tightening screws make for a cleaner setup. Smallrig rod accessories are very well made and should last a very long time. They look good, have no sharp edges and come in a large variety of sizes and uses.And when you tighten them to the rod, they really grip. Not going anywhere.One of their best features is the adjustable thumbscrew. It gives you excellent leverage, but if it runs into anything you can pull up the spring-loaded handle and reposition the handle to clear obstacles.Machining is uniformly excellent and precise. Threaded holes are in logical places and allow a lot of flexibility in mounting.This particular mount is more of a bridge, with various threaded holes in it.It's lightweight and well built.I've bought a lot from SmallRig and will probably buy more. Best value and great for my DSLR cage. I was able to rig it with my Wooden Camera cage as a top rail system. Saved over $100. Small Rig is the best value for cages. Solid material and construction. Love the ratcheting knobs. Locks down nice and tight. The variety of screwholes on top and sides make it very versatile.

name: Monoprice 4-Channel Speaker Selector - Black Up to 140W Per Ch. Distribute Speakers, Perfect for Home Theater Audio
reviewText: This works great , i am an electrician and i used my ohm meter to confirm that this keeps the system balanced at 8 ohms and it does . As long as your speakers are all the same ohms 4 or 8 this little box does great . For anyone who doesn't have an ohm meter your going to have to trust it . The protection button needs to be in if you are only using one set of speakers , but that is the only thing you need to remember I have this hooked up to a mini Yamaha stereo and use it to send audio to the speakers it came with as well as to a set of monoprice ceiling speakers. It also comes with a pack of stickers to label the buttons. Good quality, metal casing, better than I expected.  Used it to control 3 zones throughout the house. Does the job, no complaints. One stereo pair in - 4 stereo pairs out.  4 speaker on/off switches.  No power plug.  No volume control.  Nothing complicated here.I have this unit in a home with three pairs of speakers, driven by the Sherwood RC-4015 100 watt workhorse.Couldn't be simpler or more effective. I have a yamaha RX-V675 with a powered zone 2. My house has speaker pairs in 4 locations (deck. kitchen, living room, and dining room) in addition to the main zone (family room). I'm not an audiophile so I had to research how to get the music to those locations. This type of device seems to be the only way. Hooking it up was very easy and the build quality is better than I thought it would be. Based on the price, I thought it would be cheap plastic but the outer casing is actually metal. I also like that it comes with little stickers so you can label the buttons. The only thing I noticed is that there can be some crossover or bleed through to a speaker pair even if it is not selected on the device. Now it could be how it's hooked up but I did double check the connections. It's not bad though. The bleed through sound is very quiet and I can eliminate it by turning the volume control knob (preinstalled when I bought the house) to that speaker pair all the way down. Again, I suppose this could be unique to my system or how it's hooked up. That being said, I would still buy this item again. Works well and does the job it's supposed to.

name: micca MB42X 75W Wired Bookshelf Speaker - Black
reviewText: I purchased these as my rear speakers in a surround system (5+1).  I'm running B&W; 602's in the front with an AR 10" subwoofer being driven by Denon AVR1802 receiver.  I haven't had a chance to hook these up in the rear yet, but out of curiosity I set them on top of the B&W;'s to try out as front speakers.Granted, they're new out of the box so they're going to sound a little tight until they're burned in for a bit, but with these little guys being backed up by the subwoofer - unbelievable!  The accuracy, imaging, and neutrality are amazing for a speaker in this price range.  I don't expect the depth that something like the B&W;'s provide (at about 8 times the price) but the sound is very clean and I expect these little gems to work very well as the rear speakers... I am an AV enthusiast, so picky about AV gear. I just needed something for my desktop and didn't want to pay up the butt for good powered speakers like: Audioengine, Emotiva, PSB, etc. I already had a Topping mini amp and FiiO DAC I dabbled with in my garage, so I brought them into my office to tryout with these Miccas. I am using these leisurely with a late MacPro (iTunes, FCP, games, etc.) I didn't need higher end studio monitors as I'm not producing a music album or anything. So, this setup works very well for me. I am very impressed with the SQ of these. I have them toed in and about 4" from the wall. Is this audiophile grade? No. But I like this setup a lot better than something cheesy like Bose or Logitech speakers. I bought a pair of the Micca MB42X to use in a 12 x 20 family room.  It's been a while since I bought a pair of smaller speakers, but based on the others who reviewed these, I was convinced they were the ones to get.  And, I was right.  They have a tight sounding bass (no, it's not going to shake the room, and I wasn't expecting them to), clear and crisp highs.  The voices are articulated very well.  They definitely will fill the room I have.  I've coupled it with a Dayton powered 10" SUB-1000.Well worth it.  One of the best purchases I've made in audio. I wanted some satellite speakers for music in my bedroom when I was playing music throughout the house.  I first bought the Polk equivalents to these, from Best Buy.  I couldn't stand walking from the main room into the bedroom, as their sound was soooo tinny and muffled.  So, based on the reviews here and elsewhere, I decided to try these.  What a difference!  I won't say these are anywhere near the Bose 161's + Subwoofer I have in the main room, but I can at least walk in the room and the sound is good.  Yes, they are not big bass...but I didn't expect that from these tiny things.  But they do create a nice crisp, well balanced sound.  So, I am happy! I review audio products, both on the low end budget and audiophile grade end. On the Micca MB42X speakers I just received, I used an Astell & Kern DAP as the source running through a Dayton Audtio DTA-1 T-Amp. Audio files either being 16 or 24 bit FLAC. This pair of speakers sound fairly unnatural out of the box. They exhibit the 'digital' sound you would normally find in DSP speakers, but in this case, a bit more is apparent to my ears. Mids are almost nonexistent. Low ends are squishy sounding. Not quite fart cannons, but instead sound filtered somehow, as if the lows were being passed through fabric, if that makes any  sense. In any case, the lows are only 'okay'. Also, the lows tend to be hiding when volume levels are low (9'oclock). Crank up the volume to 11 and they come out of hiding, giving a nice dollop of bass that many people tend to enjoy for gaming, EDM and any genre that feeds of lows and highs. The bass is still fun and not bad if you dont mind the lack of accuracy in the low ends and slam you normally find in high end speakers.As I mentioned, mids are gone from these speakers. But, the highs are quite nice. This is the only reason I would recommend them as value budget speakers because the highs have a nice little sparkle to them and are fairly clear. Mixed with the mushy bass, I can see these speakers being good for energy music, such as EDM, electronic, house and the such, where low end accuracy is not important.Now, there are other speakers to be aware of in this price range that perform as good or better, for less money or just a little more. The Sony SS-B1000 are excellent value speakers (which I own) and are less expensive than the Micca's. The B1000's also have a cult following similar to the Micca speakers. The B1000's have good highs (not as sparkly as teh Micca's), good mids and good low end. They sound fairly natural and are for the most part great all around speakers for the price. I find both the mids and lows to be a bit better than the Micca's. The bass on the B1000's are more accurate (not by much) yet don't sound as digitally enhanced as the Micca's sound.I used the Micca MB42X to replace the B1000's in this desktop setup. I do not play my music loud often. So, most of the time the audio is at 9 o'clock on the volume wheel. I listen to music on this desktop setup when working from home in the evenings. Unfortunately, due to the speakers not sounding full enough at low volume levels, I  will have to return these. They sound just the way I described them in the beginning of this review only at higher listening volumes. But, for study or work, normal listening levels leave these speakers sounding quite dull and boring. I think a subwoofer would do the Micca setup wonders, but I do not have one available that I can use for this review.Happy speaker hunting! -dave

name: Nikon Af-S Dx Nikkor 18-140Mm F/3.5-5.6 G Ed Vr Zoom Lens for DSLR Camera - Black
reviewText: I leave it on my camera all the time now, only changing it for my macro lens or my 300MM zoom lens.  This lens is just superb.Highly recommended. The range is awesome. For those who are thinking to buy the 18-200 dont do it. This lens is great. The quality of the pictures is awesome. Im just beginning. But with my d5300 has been working great. The colors are amazing. Super sharp lens. Its all plastic so you need to be carefull. Just the mount is metal. And the weight is just right. For the money and the quality of lenses, this is the best lens that I use. The range from 18 to 140mm is amazing. This lens is nice and clear, great range and easy to use. Much better than the 18-55 kit lens for range and ability. I would highly recommend upgraded to this for your walk around lens. Finally a lens that I can keep on my camera most of the time. Arguably my best photos were shot with a 28-200mm Quantaray lens on an N80 film camera. Ever since I moved to DX cameras I have had to carry two lenses with me all the time, a 18-55mm and the 55-200mm; I kept missing shots, composition and timing are crucial in photography. This 18-140mm DX lens is equivalent to a 27-210mm on a full frame camera and it comes with the latest generation VR, up to 4 stops of compensation. I have now taken several dozens of photos with this lens and I am happily surprised by how sharper it is when compared with the 18-55mm kit lens. I had borrowed a 18-200mm lens, nice but too heavy, this is perfect. Beside this lens, only the plastic-fantastic nikkor 35mm 1:1.8 prime lens will remain in the camera bag - a lens I also highly recommend. Now at $600+tax, it did take a moment of weakness to hit the buy button; notified the wife after-the-fact.

name: Creative T15 2.0 Channel Wireless Bluetooth Speaker
reviewText: It was difficult to review these, because I had to adjust my expectation to go along with the price. I set these up in the garage for when we are out there piddling or I am doing my craft painting with furniture. I may be out there for several hours at a time. The speakers pair easily with my iPhone, iPod, and iPad. There is a midrange and a tweeter--I wouldn't call the larger speaker a bass. As long as I don't turn it up too loud, it is fine. If I turn it up all the way, I get a lot of distortion.This is good for lyric music like Dylan rather than jamming music like Emerson, Lake and Palmer. The sound is clearer on the easy listening type of songs. There isn't a profound separation of sound, but it is decent, adequate. If you are an audiophile who requires the best of sound for any listening device, then you may be disappointed. It can be difficult to recommend speakers for all, because everyone has a different ear, just like they have a different tongue for taste. For an audiophile, I would give this 3 stars, but if you are just wanting some companionable music for a limited time, then this will fit the bill. And for the price, it is certainly a serviceable and satifactory pair of Bluetooth speakers. Capsum: Creative Labs created the T15 wireless speaker for almost my situation. Light on weight and heavier in sound. Not as mobile ready as I’d expect for something so portable, and it has little place in a computer home theater setup. For simpler stereo needs I recommend these speakers.<Review>Kinda guy who whistles while he works—that’s me. Music takes the tedium out of the job, the drive, or the writing. When the whistle goes dry, the player turns on. Kinda need speakers for that.Good thing the T15 wireless speaker set came down the Vine: I tested them for you folks on four devices, in both Bluetooth and analog cable configurations:>Bluetooth desktop PC.> Kindle Fire with stereo jack.>HP netbook with stereo jack.>Bluetooth cellphone.My PC is wired straight into aOnkyo TX-SR608 Home Theater Receiver, putting out HDMI sound over a set ofPioneer Bookshelf Loudspeakersand aPioneer Center Channel Speaker. With audio integrated right into my video card, I use the mobo mainly for recording and haven’t bothered with a discrete sound card or dedicated PC speakers for years.However, for places like my workshop, I need a set of speakers I can plug ‘n’ play, and that’s where Creative Labs has re-entered my computing picture. Here’s what the T15 does and doesn’t do:> Connection: 1) Bluetooth wireless. 2) Analog 3.5mm stereo cable, line-out only. No PC wi-fi or USB connection.> Speaker Setup: Stereo only. There is no software suite or data connection to a PC or AV Receiver.> Sound Quality: Much fuller than laptop, tablet or phone, but obviously weaker than a proper HTPC setup.> Bluetooth Range: Short, even for a personal network (PAN) device.> Power: AC plug only. No batteries.> Build Quality: Sleek, black, and sturdy enough. Bigger than typical computer speakers with the additional drivers. Clearly built for desktop duty, but are decent for mobile duty.< Out of the Box >The T15 speakers are tightly packaged with no plastic display shell—it’s all cardboard, baby. No drivers, no firmware, no accessories like a stereo cable or protective sleeves. Just speakers all the way.As a pair the T15 looks sleek, glossy and black. Speakers contrast well with wood, even when perched on the cord of firewood in my shop or on my cheap particleboard bang-me-up work table. They sit nice and flat; while the front face and speaker cones are tilted up, the bottom remains parallel to the supporting surface. Little pads keep the shell from scraping around, and they seem well attached.All controls and jacks are located on the right speaker. The pair is connected by a simple fixed audio wire. The lack of a reinforced wire or a supporting lanyard is your next clue, after the AC power, that these boys really aren’t intended to be trucked around with your tablet. And due to their hefty size, you can’t pack them in a laptop case. The speakers don’t snap or stack together.If you do decide to go portable with these guys, consider something like theTargus Compact Rolling Backpack for Laptops. These kinds of packs will take your laptop, phone and tablet all in one go, with a big compartment left over for the speakers.Plug in to wall power and activate the Bluetooth pairing button on the right speaker. Pairing varies with the device, but tends to be as simple as searching for the T15 in the Bluetooth dialog box of your computer or smart phone. It won’t always show up as named; on my Win7 system it was just identified as a generic device, while the smart phone recognized BT speakers.<On with the Music>There does not appear to be any out-of-the-box way to configure T15 as wireless side or rear speakers. And there is no additional output for a subwoofer or for traditional connections to an AV receiver other than 3.5mm. As the Amazon title says, these are 2.0 jobs. I’d be interested in hearing any method of getting these guys to take a rear channel stream in a surround setup.For their size and the kind of files they have been playing, the T15 sounds pretty good. MP3s play clearer and heftier than anything my netbook or Kindle speakers can manage. I can load up my 106-hour video games playlist and hear every track across an 1100-square foot shop space at half volume. Uncompressed WAV files also sound good compared to the tin can speakers of a mobile device, although again you are going to lose some feeling versus a bigger full-range speaker. As other reviewers said, the sound is “balanced”. Not great bass or treble, and on the other hand little or no distortion at higher volumes. Obviously, your speaker separation is limited by the length of the of fixed wire.Wireless range is also caught short. In my apartment, the T15 is unable to pair or to receive BT stream two rooms over from the smartphone. Likewise, they don’t range as far from my PC as myPX51 Wireless Gaming Headseton BT. Overall the T15 offers a reliable distance of 20 feet in my tests. I know these speakers are using a PAN, but I didn’t expect them to drop off so quickly. Unlike a radio which fades out, you either have a stream, or you don’t.<Advanced Use>Because of the Bluetooth capability, these speakers imply more mobility than they actually have. Aside from their physical design, there is no ability to stream from wi-fi or USB, which I consider beyond obvious to an absurd oversight for any modern PC speaker. You can’t get more “duh” for a digital link.At first glance, Amazon doesn’t stock any tote or bag for carrying what is ostensibly a portable sound system. This in turn makes me a little concerned about that little wire connecting to the left speaker. I know that’s a common, economical design for PC speakers in general and for smaller jobs like these in particular. For a more portable or flexible variant, or just to get wider separation, it would be nice to have them connected with a mono patch cable.Finally, there is the matter of power. Knowing these are fundamentally PC speakers, their portable promise suggests they should have a battery option. Sure, these boys are too small for C-cells and too powerful for AAs. I say mobile consumer tech has long exceeded the point where modern high capacity rechargeable batteries should be available for more than just cell phones and laptops. And yes, I accept these hypothetical batteries would still rapidly drain—wireless draws a lot of juice—but so does my tablet and my laptop when I spent a lot of time on the wi-fi. Willing to bet the same goes for a lot of you, too.<Money Talks>Mobility matters when laptops and tablets are otherwise perfect for T15. So too are crowded desktops that can’t fit a nicer surround system. The sort of accessory you should be able to take into work, hook up, and return home at the end of the shift. A netbook and a set of these speakers are the 21st Century equivalent of a boom box, and they can sort of live up to that ability.So the money question is answered by folks looking for something other than a hefty setup for Home Theater PC, but still wish to stream music and video on a regular basis with good results. With no subwoofer and the wireless built into the right speaker, the footprint is tight and tidy. Especially if you are streaming MP3, ACC, or similar compressed formats, they will sound fine. Uncompressed audio is totally decent for what these guys can do. These speakers arrived just in time, as far as I am concerned, because my younger brother's Mac Mini needed better sound, giving me the perfect opportunity to plug them in and see how they worked. Simple answer: fairly well.After you get past the miles of tiny-print instructions, warnings and warrantee information (there are three fold-outs of all that), it's fairly easy to set these speakers up. The speakers themselves are standard-sized and have only one or two cables (thanks to the Bluetooth), so with the instructions it took about ten minutes to set up, install and start playing sound from the computer (using the same methods that you Bluetooth-adapt anything).However, he power adapter is a bit difficult to put together, and at times it's hard to know what plugs into what.As for the sound quality, it's fairly good. It sounds a bit tinny at first, but it's pretty good overall -- clear and sharp.One small caveat: these speakers are clearly intended for desktop computers. You could apply them to a laptop, but only if you plan to place them on a shelf and have them play from there. They're too big and heavy to be effective portable laptop speakers. I always wanted to have a decent external speaker system for my laptop, so I could enjoy Redbox Streaming and Xbox Video Streaming more. Teeny audio kills the watching experience, but I often am too lazy to move to the TV. These speakers are really easy to set up, as I've successfully paired them with two Toshiba laptops as well as my first-gen Surface. The sound quality is more than adequate, and it makes watching videos on the laptops so much more engaging. The speakers are well made, and the fact they are wireless makes it easy to place them. I wonder if Creative offers a subwoofer that can be integrated with these little but powerful speakers. All in all, I'm quite happy with this product! I really like these speakers.  There's just a plug for electric and one to connect the speakers.  No clutter! They have a sharp black glossy finish.  Setup was super easy with the creative Bluetooth audio usb transmitter (bt-d1).  Sounds great.

name: GoPro Tripod Mount
reviewText: The whole GoPro experiences is new for us, so every accessory I get for it is partially a new experience of learning how it works the best. After I get more familiar with it rating could be a 5 star I gave it a 4 because it appears to be well made and couldn't rate from experience of using at this point. It is an original GoPro Accessory and that means it will work with the camera. What you would expect from GoPro parts. Fits well, works as designed and easy to use. Would recommend to anyone looking for GoPro attachment for their tripod. These two tripod mounts come packaged together and are nice mounts.  They are GoPro branded and one mount is small and has a secure threaded 1/4x20 insert to fit standard camera tripods.  The other is a quick-disconnect base and has two inserts on the bottom, both standard 1/4x20.  Very happy with the products. I bought these to attach my GoPro Hero3 to a tripod, and they work perfectly. I love them. You can use the smaller, rounded one to mount directly onto the tripod, or you can use the larger, more rectangular one to mount to the camera via one of the standard clip adapters (not included) that came with your camera. I tried both, and I preferred the larger rectangular mount because it made it very easy to remove the camera from the tripod. Not much you can say about this mount.  It fits the tripod correctly and does what it needs to do. Great price through Amazon.

name: GoPro Suction Cup for Camera, Plastic, Black
reviewText: Awesome suction cup mount. Has held up to 60 MPH so far, mounted on the side of a truck bed. Works great on any flat surface. The product description says that it has an industrial strength suction cup that can withstand up to 150mph.To be honest, I wouldn't risk it... the suction cup has fallen off several times when attached to my kids' push car! I have cleaned the surface and followed the instructions, but it still fell off.Maybe on glass or car's body it might hold better... but I personally wouldn't risk my camera falling off at a high speed and hitting the asphalt! I used this to fasten my Go Pro to the plexiglass windows in my airplane so I can shoot out the window while I am flying.  Installs easily, does not come loose.  Very well made, and I love all the little accessories that allow me to configure the suction cup in dozens of different ways. Suction cup is strong!  I like to fabricate mounts brackets etc or go with 3rd party companies to save that $$. This time  I wanted to make sure that the camera won't be moving around since my car is lowered and the streets of San Francisco is pothole central. Im glad I went with the official Gopro suction mount. This bad boy does not move at all! Used this mount on the windshield of my truck while on vacation in Colorado and it never budged. Never took it off the entire trip (I will admit I had it tethered just in case it were to come off). Got some amazing film that I otherwise wouldn't have been able to get. I leave it stuck to the inside of my back glass in my truck so I can put it on at a moments notice.Wonderful Product!

name: Yongnuo YN-14EX TTL LED Macro Ring Flash Light for Canon
reviewText: I was very suspect on purchasing this unit as it is a quarter of the price of the Canon model. The fit is perfect, I use it with my D7 and an assortment of lenses. The first this you need to do it take this out of automatic mode and put it into manual. Then you can unleash all of it's flexibility.The manual is the only weak point as it is a poorly translated handbook, but you can figure it out.The ability to balance the flash left to right is a great feature for shadows and special effects. The unit is OK because the light pattern is so narrow. The center part of the photo lid up so well but the edge is so dark. What can I say.  Compared to the $500 and $800 Canon macro flashes, and the ultra cheap third party alternatives, this is a steal!  I use a lot of Yongnuo flashes, and have been very impressed with the quality and value, and this one is no exception.They are made for Nikon and Canon, so you have no reason to buy the OEM flash if you use one of those brands.  Not sure if they are made for other brands of DSLR's.Hopefully at some point Canon will get the message that their accessories are stupidly overpriced. As far as I can tell, the YN-14EX flash does almost everything the Canon MR-14EX II flash does for $450 less!  Good solid build quality feel.  Primary differences between the Yongnuo and Canon macro ring flash units:  Yongnuo GN=28 vs Canon GN=46, Yongnuo flash adjustment 1:64 vs Canon 1:128, Yongnuo fits 52mm, 58mm, 67mm, 72mm vs Canon 67mm only.  Every other feature is pretty much the same (e.g. E-TTL, Camera flash control, R/L flash tubes,...)In addition to macro flash photography, I have used the YN-14EX to take interior real estate shots as it eliminates shadows from objects such as ceiling fans... drives me crazy!Highly recommended.  The price is right.  It's a full flash unit, not an LED "light" masquerading as a flash. I've used this twice for portraiture and what's great is that you always get a catch light. Dead eye is a thing of the past. If you want a large catch light, you'll need a larger ring.

name: AmazonBasics 67-Inch Monopod (Black)
reviewText: I do like this for my still camera.  It is just the right size for those tighter situations but I also like to use it for anything I think needs a bit more steady hand when shooting.  This does not help me with video I need a full tripod for that or there is too much movement. I would like the adjustment clips that you flip to expand it to be a bit more flowing -they are rather tight and difficult at least when new.  You cannot put the bottom of this into a stand, the threads are not really accessible even with the rubber rolled all the way back and that rubber tip dose not come off.  I love the cushion soft handle and the light feel of this. I love photography- but I am not a huge fan of toting a tripod where ever I go- I find it cumbersome.  This is a good alternative. The monopod does stabilize my photos and is easy to switch between cameras as I tend to shoot multiple cameras. None of my lenses are too heavy so this is a nice alternative to shooting freehand photos.The monopod is adjustable in height by quite a bit and I have never ever in the short time I have been using it felt that it wasn't tall enough or short enough- so the built in height adjustments works well for me- and I am 5' 4". It's compact and lightweight so it's not bad to carry (and it comes with a handy carrying case- which frankly- I personally do NOT use at all).  What is nice is the monopod also has a spike/rubber tip at the foot so that you can use it to secure the monopod on different types of surfaces. You can also use it as a light walking stick while hiking for those nature shoots.I am pleased with this product and would recommend- as long as you don't have too heavy of a camera lens on it. This monopod is a great tool, it's light weight and yet well made.  It has a nice traveling case with an adjustable strap that will keep it protected from rain, weather and wear from rolling around in the back end of your car and makes for hands free portability.I like the versatility and portability of this monopod.  I very rarely use my tripod, it's old and big and cumbersome and honestly I would feel like a goofball pulling it out and setting it up.  But this monopod is small and can be set up without a big to do, and no one except the people nearest to you will even know you have it.It's easy to open and adjust to the right height and gives my hand constant steady support at a great price.A very nice item. I am extremely impressed with this monopod. Purchased to help me video my high school wrestler without all the shakes I was getting before. The grip at the top of the pod is indulgent - meaning very well padded and "thick". Throw in the 3 individual adjustments which allow for virtually any height up to 67". Also comes with a black carrying case which I probably won't ever use, but a nice touch. I recommend highly if you're in the market. This is a sturdy monopod and should work well for what I intend–which is to use it as a stabilizer when I film with my iPad. I will have to get an adapter as the threads are only good for cameras with a threaded socket. But the price was right and I should be able to get a good adapter fairly easily. If you know of a good one please mention it in the comments. Many thanks!

name: Fujifilm Instax Mini 90 Neo Classic Instant Film Camera
reviewText: Bought this because I always wanted my own Polaroid Camera, this one has features that other polaroids don't have, meaning it cost much more.First the camera, it is plastic and feels like a toy. It is a solid piece of plastic though, not sure how well it will handle a drop and I don't feel like testing. It comes with a strap so you don't have to worry about dropping it, worry about it swinging around though if you are putting it over the shoulder and body. Camera itself looks very nice, retro looking with the gray and black. Looks like a toy Fuji X-100.My favorite feature for the camera is the double exposure. Fun to play with because results are instant. Just be careful though because films are expensive, but then again every picture I take with this seem to always come out nice.The problems I had with this camera are holding the camera and the viewfinder. I know I am probably holding it wrong, but I can't seem to find a way to hold it comfortably. Next the viewfinder is small, again maybe because I'm doing it wrong. I can't seem to look through it properly all the time.Overall the camera is fun to play with, great pictures all the time, just need to spend a lot of money because of the film. I had an older poloroid years ago which I donated to Goodwill, boy was I dummy. I was researching photosbooths for my up coming wedding and kept seeing ideas about doing your own with an instant camera. I started searching and came across the Fujifilm instax mini 90 and immediately fell in love. The style and functionality is nothing like anything else on the market. This became my birthday gift and has been a lot of fun using. It's a chemical process for the photos, not a printed, so don't expect super crisp, extremely colorful photos, use as a novelty as it is intended :) I thought my kids would never learn about the evolution of cameras and film, but this little thing is a great learning tool.  They understand that sometimes, you only get one shot, so make it count.  They are learning that film developing is different than a printer. I AM IN LOVE. I had the Mini 8 and I loved that camera! I collect old camera and have a fascination with polaroids but it's hard to find film (or it's $30 for 10 prints) and sometimes they aren't very portable. I was so happy to find this line of instant cameras. I used my mini 8 for everything possible. I took pictures of my nephews and niece at there birthday parties and hand out photos to everyone! I took pictures of my vacation in North Carolina! I was using it as if it were my phone. Snap Snap Snap. It's easy to be happy with every photo.THEN I saw this guy all over instagram and had to have it. It is 100 times more amazing than the others in the mini series. I can do so much more and make beautiful mini pieces of art! I love all the features (light, dark, double exposure, etc etc) I have seriously taken 20 or more double exposure photos. I am driving people nuts I always want to take a picture with this camera and make them my test subjects.It takes better pictures than the mini 8 or maybe I am so in love with the neo classic that I am putting my blinders on. It so amazing to people able to adjust the darkness or lightness of a photo. I use to put electrical tape over my flash on the mini 8 so pictures were 1) over exposed 2) still to bright out for a decent photo. Also this camera has an on/off switch for the flash. BAM! So many problems solved with just two of the many upgrades!I read a lot of people's complaints about the photo size! I love the size I am into junk journaling, art journaling, smash booking, and these pictures are perfect for all those things and make for easy smashing! I think I enjoy my smash booking so much more with these little photos. I think they turn out amazing. You can't ask for a better instant camera! It does so much more than any other instant camera!Sorry I am not good at writing coherent reviews!If you have any question feel free to ask. Everyone love it. I love it. The people I shoot love it. The reaction I get, as someone that is always taking photos is, oh its him again, then the magic happens and the photo pops out and their faces light up... very enjoyable for nights out at bars or parties.. always, always gets a smile. Camera works well, setting easy to change, photos pretty good if you remember to get in close to your subject. I love it and the price per photo is livable....

name: ExpoDisc EXPOD2-77 2.0 Professional White Balance Filter 77 mm
reviewText: great little tool! This works way easier on my Sony NEX 6 then my Canon 6d. But that's more of an issue with the hardware rather than Expo disc. This really will save you lots of time in post! If you're serious about white balance, you owe it to yourself to get this.  I shoot lots of Infra-red, and this is a must have.  Don't bother with the low cost alternatives.  Do your research, and you'll see that none of them give you quite the accurate white balance.  The ExpoDisc does. I use this product on the majority of my shoots, with usually pleasing results. It is better than relying on the camera's white balance. However there are 2 instances where it will not work well.1. If you have an on camera flash. You need to point the camera at the light source in this case the light source is on the camera...they say you can point you camera at a white surface bounce the flash then try to get a reading. But that can be tricky outdoor and indoors if your surface is not perfectly white the you ll have a color cast.2. If you are late in the afternoon in a big shade area on a sunny day, where you can't see the light source. Such as behind a big building. Taking the reading of the blue sky will give you the wrong white balance, as well as taking a reading by pointing the camera around...In cloudy days things work better.In other words if you can't point this thing at the light source(s), you are out of luck... The last wedding I shot was about 3000 images and this baby nailed the WB better than any other tool I've used. What a time saver in post! I went cheap at first and bought a Mennon which works just ok but this blows it away. If you're like me you've bought and tried almost every gadget to save time and sanity just to find you've spent $50 on a piece of plastic that does almost nothing. Not the case with this! I couldn't be happier as it's paid for itself on the first shoot already by saving me hours in post. Thanks Expo! This is my second Expodisc! I would buy it again,  this is a must have tool is you shoot interior architecture, Events, or anything where you have multiple types of lighting. They hand check each one to ensure it meets specifications (18% Grey). unlike a grey card the light flows through it so you don't have to mess with temperature in post processing... Get it you will not regret it!

name: Micca MB42X-C Center Channel Speaker with Dual 4-Inch Carbon Fiber Woofer and Silk Dome Tweeter, Black
reviewText: I got this guy to match up with a pair of the MB42x bookshelf speakers I got to redo the front of my HT.  I originally bought the MB42X's for my computer.  I was so impressed that I wanted to put some on my HT setup.  This guy completed the front setup and so far I'm very happy with the results.  The vocals are very clear and project nicely across my room.  If you're looking for a low cost HT setup I really think you should look at this speaker with either two more for L/R or a pair of the MB42Xs. Good center speaker and fits our entertainment center perfect. Wife and I are very happy with our purchase and it arrived a day early too It exceeds expectation!! When watching movie in Dolby mode, the center channel has very clear high and deep bass. The human conversation can be heard just like some one talks in front you. I am totally impressed by this speaker that only costs $69!!!!  I've been recommending Micca's for 5.1 surround sound for well over a year and the biggest hurtle has been no matching center. I would just advise people buy another full pair of the MB42's and keep one in the closet and use the other. Those days are gladly over. A pair of these is as impressive as the bookshelves but louder. I haven't done an A-B on them to see if the low end is greatly improved or popped the crossover out to take a look but on the first few days worth of impressions, I am impressed.When you stand up a pair they are narrower than the MB42's by about a half an inch but are about an inch deeper so these will fit in some odd places should you actually want to hide them somewhere special. The magnetic grills are super clean and impressive as always and although the rear 5-way terminals are of good quality they are still 7/8ths spaced which means normal dual 3/4" banana's wont fit and you will need to wire directly or with single banana's instead.If you have Micca's already and want to push to a 5.1 or higher these are your speakers. You can even consider buying three for your entire front assembly.  LEFT - CENTER - RIGHT all these and finish off with the standard MB42's in the rear.

name: Audio-Technica Ath-M30X Wired On Ear Headphones Without Mic (Black)
reviewText: No need to waste money on some billionaire's mediocre headphones.Buy a pair of these and you won't be disappointed.Great studio-style headphones - great for recording.Very long cord and it includes both plugs. The sound quality on these is incredible, the noise-cancelling is good, and the comfort is great. They also weigh much less than I imagined them by looking at the photo on Amazon. Highly recommend, especially at this price! They are big and bulky, but really comfortable. The ambient noise isolation and the sound quality are very good. They also seem well made and robust. The product is great not that good of a bass other then that it is great comfy and fits well. I really like the way these headphone fell.  They are well balance, light and sound great.  This is my first headset in a decade, I had moved to earphone for portability, but when size is no issue these are great.  The do a good job of reducing noise and not feeling overly snug. The only thing I would change... the length of the cord, I believe it is 9 feet.  I would have liked one about half the size, but this is a minor issue not worth a star.

name: Audio-Technica Ath-M20X Wired Over Ear Headphones Without Mic (Black)
reviewText: These Headphones sound terrific after having used turtle beaches for a little over a year, and the build quality is extremely solid for the price, the only down side is the heat and the long attached chord.  The chord I wish you could replace and the heat gets annoying and requires you to pull em around your nech to cool off after around 2 or 3 hours.  Over all I'd recommend them to anyone! These headphones have really full sound and help cut out the bleeding of music from the headphones into the mic when recording vocals. They arrived quickly and work great. Excellent pair of headphones, sound quality is better than beats even at this low end model. You just don't get as much bass.  Build quality is very durable but no detachable cord like on the M40x or M50x.  Cord is long but does not get in the way.headphones are very comfortable and can make your ears hot if using them during a workout. I'm not even going to say you can't go wrong for the price. These must be my favorite pair of headphones ever. These headphones are clear sounding, have a very flat frequency response range, the cable is very long, but not too long, and to top it all off, they're only 50 bucks. Buy these headphones! I get this in a perfect price. I really feel unbelieveable that this product just need this price- $49.99. The product is perfect. After I wear it, the only sound I heard is the music. It is very comfortable and not heavy. Good tough feeling.

name: SoundBot® SB510 HD Water Resistant Bluetooth 3.0 Shower Speaker, Handsfree Portable Speakerphone with Built-in Mic, 6hrs o...
reviewText: We use this little marvel in the shower.The sound quality is great. Pairing was a breeze and It sticks to the glass really well.The microphone feature doesn't work nearly as well, so I won't suggest buying this as a hands-free speakerphone. I almost returned this because I mistakenly thought I had it on max volume with my phone volume at max and it was so quiet.  I WOULD HAVE MISSED OUT!  So it turns out that it has it's own independent volume control so that you can adjust volume in the shower when you don't have the phone near you, and it arrives from the factory at a low setting so I would never have known if I hadn't read the instructions.Press and hold the "next song" button until it beeps to tell you the max volume has been reached.  Then you can also control it with the volume on your phone if you want, but that's independent of the speaker's setting.The sound is FANTASTIC at HALF the cost of even the cheapest other speakers!!! Man, I wish I had to shower right now that I figured this out!!! Lol I bought this to listen to the radio through my ipad air in the shower.  I charged fully when it arrived (a little over an hour).  I initially had a little difficulty getting it to pair with my ipad, but after a few tries (5-10 mins) I finally got it to connect.  It works well enough, but the sound is not very loud and I sometimes have trouble hearing it when the water and bath fan are running.  It is working fine for now, and I will keep it and update after a while. I have no idea what the naysayers are writing about. I charged it, it plays - I don't charge it, it doesn't. I brought this out to the pool area just for S&G's - worked great. Only issue I had was when it was in the bathroom charging, I forgot to turn it off, while in bed I played a YouTube video on my iphone and the sound came through the speaker 35 ft away. scared the crap outta me. I was very disappointed with this product.The volume is pretty low, although it's usable. One really annoying aspect is the proprietary charging port. Instead of just using micro USB and allowing me to charge it along other devices, it's uses some arbitrary charging hole.Lastly, I am having a lot of trouble getting the suction to work. It can usually make it through a shower, but falls down later.

name: Nikon 18-300 Mm F/3.5-6.3G Ed Vr Af-S Dx Nikkor Lens - Black
reviewText: I have the predecessor to this lens, and it works beautifully as an all-purpose lens for garden photography, but it is way too heavy to be practical for me. This is a HUGE improvement in terms of weight, and there is no discernible difference in how it works. In a book on close-up photography that I got from Amazon, I found a suggestion for turning this zoom lens into a close-up lens by adding a Canon 500D lens. I was skeptical, but after taking it out on two outings, I think it will work well for me. The only problem is that the two lenses fight each other a little bit, and the Nikon lens tends to shift focus slightly as the lens wobbles, which naturally affects the photo. It takes some getting used to, but I'm starting to get the hang of it. Ultimately, I see these two lenses working in tandem as the workhorses of my little photography stable. Today I had the best day ever in 3 years of D-SLR photography, thanks to the new and improved 18-300 mm lens and the Canon 500D. Nikon should reintroduce its own close-up lens to provide the perfect complement to what I see as a nearly perfect lens for everyday use. I can't wait to see how time will improve it. Is a compact 400 mm lens on the horizon? I looked at a lot of lenses before settling on this new Nikkor 18-300, and I must say I'm very pleased with the choice.  The lens is compact but has a great zoom range.  I shoot pictures for a local sports team, and the versatility of this lens is just great.  I've also done nature photograph with it as well.  I'm pushing 800 pictures since I got the lens, and I've very satisfied with it.  There is some distortion at either end of the lens (barrel and pincushion), and there can be some vignetting, depending on aperture and zoom, but these are easily correct in a photo editing program and/or RAW editor. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this lens. I got the lens 2 days ago and made several photos outside and indoor using it on Nikon D7000 in P mode. It is not bad. It is not 'super' either. The focus feels a little slow (maybe because it is quiet?). It is sharp. The color and contrast are good. The image is almost perfect in sharp areas. As soon as it gets less sharp it gets noisy especially at max zoom.  I also own Sigma 18-250mm (very good lens). The bokeh on Nikon is not as pleasant as on Sigma (it looks smudged). Nothing can obviously bit the range. Overall I rate at as 'good'. I wanted this for a trip that is coming up so I don't have to change lenses constantly. I do like to limit myself to fixed focal length lenses but when you want an all in one as your go to lens this is the best one to get. This is almost the exact same size and weight of the 18-140 that is also an awesome lens but I personally wanted something with a longer focal length and was an all in one solution. Nice and balanced, fast accurate focus, great zoom and all around if this is the only lens you have I can't see how you will be disappointed. This is a nice addition to my ever growing assortment of lenses. I often contemplate going with something off brand but always come back to Nikon lens for my D7100. Love It.  I had purchased a Nikon 55-300mm lens and was planning to take it on a lengthy European trip.  Spent a week at home getting to know it -- decided I hated it.  Hated the clarity, the color, the contrast, the sharpness.  Everything.  Very mediocre uninspiring  images (I'm sure a lot of blame belongs with the photographer).  Traded it in at a local shop (sorry amazon) for this 18-300 f/3.5-6.3 lens.  LOVE IT.  Getting wonderful results -- from my D5200 body.  Someone said to me that lenses are like acoustic guitars -- some are real winners -- some dogs.  Can't speak to that; except my new lens is a winner.  Am now in Europe, been getting wonderful results.  Very very pleased with this purchase.  The old 55-300mm is not missed at all.

name: Sony RX100M3 Premium Compact Camera with 1.0-Type Exmor CMOS Sensor (Optical, DSC-RX100M3), Black
reviewText: I will not go into the technical details of the camera. Professional reviewers did and will review it much better than me. All I can say is that for such a small camera, and from a still-photo perspective, there is almost nothing you cannot adjust. The photo quality is amazing even at high ISO. The viewfinder and tilting screen are more than rare in such cameras. My only take, and it is not worth taking out a star, is the size. I have a Canon PowerShot S120 and it is "pocketable." I am a big guy, and I can still cannot fit it in my pocket. It is still small enough though and truly worth buying. You can imagine camera manufacturers trying their best to squeeze every possible feature into a compact camera body while still keeping it priced reasonably. In my opinion, Sony has innovated the most and made the third iteration of the RX100 the best of the three, as well as when compared to the competition.I have both the original RX100 and the RX100M3. I bought the first model right away when it came out a couple of years ago. It is still an excellent prosumer camera in 2014 with a good, basic feature set.I did not buy the RX100M2 because I felt it did not have enough additional useful features to justify the added cost. Visually, the protruding multi-function hot-shoe also made the camera less aesthetically pleasing.I bought the RX100M3 because of the following reasons:1. The excellent Zeiss lens offering a wider wide angle (24mm) and much larger aperture (f/1.8 to 2.8) while trading off a smaller zoom range (24 to 70mm vs. 28 to 100mm), when compared to the original RX100. I use the wide end of a zoom lens much more often, and frequently in low light, so this lens is more suitable and useful for me than the one on the original RX100. For shooting in the bright outdoors, the M3 has a built-in 3-stop neutral density filter that helps to keep the aperture from stopping down for a pleasing blurred background effect.2. The built-in, pop-up Electronic ViewFinder (EVF) which allows picture-taking the traditional way (up against the eye/body for more steadiness), is useful, unobtrusive, and more convenient than an external one. It is also a necessity when the shooting environment is the sunny and bright outdoors, where the LCD screen cannot be seen clearly. An external EVF is available for the RX100M2, but beside additional bulk, it costs $450 extra. The built-in EVF is great not just for composing a shot but also for checking exposure after a shot (or a video) is taken. You can't appreciate this feature enough until you find how frustrating it is trying to compose/check a shot under a bright sun, looking at a dim and washed out LCD screen.3. An even more versatile tilt screen. The RX100M3 now allows you to take pictures from a low position, above the crowd, and of yourself. Without the protruding hot-shoe of the RX100M2, it was then possible to design the M3 screen to tilt up 180 degrees for taking selfies (self-portraits). You may be surprised how much you will use this feature now that it is possible. No need to risk asking strangers to take pictures for you anymore when you want to be included in a travel scene.4. Last but not least, the RX100M3 is a vastly better video shooter compared to the two previous models. The new BIONZ X image processor permits full-sensor readout and XAVC S compression (requires SDXC memory card class 10) for excellent quality video comparable to the Sony RX10 bridge/superzoom camera. Video frame rates now include 24p, 30p, 60p, and 120p (@720p).The RX100 series cameras utilize a 1-inch image sensor in a compact body while most point-and-shoot cameras use 1/2.3 inch sensors. A larger sensor can gather more light so its image quality tends to be better than a small sensor. But compared to 1/2.3 inch sensor cameras, a 1-inch sensor camera's lens size needs to be physically bigger and its zoom range much smaller, given a limited camera size. With these constraints, I deem it a wonder that Sony can come up with the RX100 series camera with so many features while keeping it very compact. Sony also makes cameras in the Compact System Camera (CSC) category that feature an even larger sensor (APS-C) and interchangeable lens capability, but they are not "pocketable" and an equivalent 24-70mm Zeiss lens costs $1,200 alone.While I have other cameras, the Sony RX100M3 IS the one that I carry with me all of the time. I suggest using Sony's well-designed LCJ-RXF jacket (ever-ready) case to carry around your RX100M3. It allows the camera to be well protected until the moment you want to use it. I waited patiently for 2 months to receive what is now the third version of the RX100.  I read everything about it that I could ahead of time and recognize that this is a camera enthusiasts dream.  All of the other reviews focus on the positives of the camera so no need to repeat that except to say that the build quality is excellent, the software nearly perfect and the image quality just stellar for its size.  It's a technological marvel.But, after using the camera for just a brief time, I realized that I just cannot live with the immensely small (2.9x) zoom.  It's even less than the last version.  As good as this camera is and as spectacular as the image quality ends up being, the camera is just not practical for me without more optical zoom.  It barely zooms which essentially means you have to be right up on your subject which, for me, means missing out on many shots.I get that Sony made tradeoffs to get such stellar picture quality in such a form factor and my hats off to them for their remarkable advances.  But, for me, I realized after using the camera briefly that I'd happily trade slightly less quality for much longer range.  Most compact cameras nowadays have outstanding picture quality at longer distances.I'm sure many will be extremely happy with this camera, and there's a lot to like about it, but it's just not for me. Expectation:The camera should be compact so it can go anywhere, focus quickly, focus accurately, and take sharp/high quality photos that are rich in color. As an added bonus, it should take high quality video and do well in low light without a flash.With that expectation in mind, the following pros and cons were found while shooting extra fine jpeg images and AVCHD 60p 28M(PS) videos.Pros:1) Compact enough to go everywhere.2) Takes excellent photos in low light without a flash.3) Takes beautiful macro shots that are rich in detail.4) Focuses very quickly.5) The background can be forced out-of-focus to create a professional looking effect.6) Takes high quality video at 1080p.7) Easily takes panoramic shots.8) Zooming in and out is nearly silent.9) The screen flips up for self-portraits.10) The "Fn" button brings up a highly customizable quick menu.11) Several buttons including the control ring can be customized.Cons:1) The "Wide" "Focus Area" setting frequently results in the image, especially the center, being out-of-focus. Half pressing the shutter button will correct the issue... sometimes.2) "Intelligent Auto" shooting mode is not a dependable mode to leave the camera in.a. It ALWAYS uses the "Wide" "Focus Area" in this mode (see con #1).b. Scene recognition frequently selects the wrong scene. Taking an image of a car passing at 25 miles per hour results in a blurred streak.3) When the "Center" "Focus Area" setting is selected, images still lack sharpness when compared to a Panasonic Lumix DMC-ZS3 from 2009.4) Colors are dull, especially when compared to images taken by a Panasonic Lumix DMC-ZS3 from 2009.5) Auto white balance (AWB) sometimes produces shots that are too warm.a. If two shots are taken back-to-back sometimes one will be warm and the other accurate.6) In a space the size of a living room, using a flash at distance frequently results in overexposure.7) When shooting handheld, it's difficult to maintain the proper grip and use the control ring due to the size of the camera and lack of an actual grip.8) The screen is cluttered with an excessive amount of icons that cannot be individually shown/hidden. Given that individual icon control is unavailable, the following seem like unnecessary icons for these reasons:a. Infrequently changes: image ratio, number of megapixels, video formatb. Simply unneeded: SteadyShotSummary:There are several pros when it comes to the RX100 III but they seem to center around physical camera interaction and less frequent uses such as, low light and video. When it comes to daylight photos, which is a very frequent camera use, the bottom line is that pictures are not sharp enough or rich enough in color. Furthermore, you need to be ready to take a picture at a moment's notice and that requires a high quality and dependable automatic shooting mode that is lacking in this camera. Had the original 100, and this is a step up in all ways except zoom length.  As with my first one... Extraordinarily sharp, clear, detailed and saturated photos, faster shot to shot and better low light performance.  Little heavier, little thicker, very well made.  I would easily have given up the EVF for a touchscreen... I suspect Sony knows that by now, and i have no doubt it sill be on the next model.  Cons: The flash is now a manually actuated pop up, even when forced "on" in the menu, which seems dumb... and not well thought out, especially since the menu hasn't changed.  Why have a forced flash menu option when you have to manually pop it up?  Form factor still REQUIRES the addition of the rubber grip, or you WILL drop it.  How Sony got that one wrong is a true mystery.  That being said, yes... I ditched my Nikon D7000 and lenses and could not be more happy, not to be lugging it all around.  Under almost every circumstance, you cannot tell the difference between the DSLR shots and the Sony.  I have been a photographer for 40 years, and this is the first real game changer that made me ditch all the gear... Its just not necessary any more.  I fully understand that this is a subjective review, not technical.  If you need that, there are many technical online reviews that come to the same conclusion.  You will not be disappointed.

name: Canon EF-S 10-18MM f/4.5-5.6 is STM Zoom Lens (Black)
reviewText: I own the Canon 10-22 USM and love it, and I also had good experiences using the Canon STM lenses.  So the combination of both wide angle and STM just makes sense.  After first inspection, the lens is just slightly smaller than the 10-22 mm, made of solid durable plastic, and amazingly light.  The only real major thing missing form the 10-18 is the distance scale and maybe the extra 4 mm of zoom from the more expensive 10-22.  Combined with the Canon SL1, and this is one light duo.  The focus speeds between the two lenses are negligible.  USM is very quiet but after using the 10-18, STM is absolutely silent.  I even put my ear up to the lens to try to hear any focusing and nothing.  Video can be taken in Liveview using autofocus with no mechanical noise.  Both lenses produce great image quality.  The game changer is the IS.  In low light with the slightest shake using the 10-22 and the picture is out of focus.  With the 10-18, there is a higher chance of images coming in focus with minor shaking or motion.  Upon further inspection, the 10-18 produces sharper images, but I didnnotice some grain/noise overall when zoomed in.  My 10-22 produces much smoother images with noticeable less sharpening.  This could be a deal breaker for some people but I prefer the ability to use IS and have my images sharp and in focus.  I noticed that the front lens glass element does not sit flush with the zoom zoom/focus ring and body of the lens at 10mm.  It will sit flush when the zoom ring is set to 14mm.  This worries me because I mainly shoot wide open at 10mm and I leave the lens in that position when it goes into my bag, potentially allowing dust or cause damage to the lens.  Can anyone else verify that with their 10-18?  I find I use this lens much more than the my 10-22.  It has been a good run with the 10-22 but I think there is a new king of ultra wide zooms for the APS-C sensor Canon cameras. This is a great lens for landscape and night photography. It's lightweight but produces images that rival those of much heavier L lenses (except prime L lenses, of course). Like the old Canon EF-S 10-22mm and practically all ultra-wide angle lenses, images are a little bit soft in the corners at 10mm. But at 12mm and up, even the corners are sharp. This lens will most likely bring down the price of the old 10-22mm and other third party wide angle lenses. I took one star because of the "kit lens" build quality. As a long time photographer who's scaling back from big glass for the carry around convenience I was really surprised on how great the images were and usability of this lens compared to my 17-35.  One of my favorite lenses for my 70D This an excellent lens especially for indoor or outdoor architectural photography.  Nice price point and good quality glass.  Would definitely recommend if you are shooting real estate or interior design work. The EF-S 10-18 4.5-5.6 IS STM is the least expensive and smallest APS-C wide zoom among a small field of contenders. Here's what I thought about it after a couple weeks of shooting:CONSTRUCTION: Save for optical elements and electronics, it's entirely made of plastic. Plastics are high quality and the barrel is well finished in semi-matte. I could detect no wobble or play in the mount or zoom extension. This petite lens is a featherlight 240g and easy to slip in a coat pocket or purse.FOCUS is internal--no front element extension or turning--and fast, but silent to onboard mics. The STM drive rendered pulls and Movie Servo silky smooth on a 70D. I found STM focus equally effective for both video and stills and surprisingly surefooted in low light. The electronic or "by wire" manual focus is smooth, finely pitched and has a long rotation (100+), making pulls and fine adjustments a snap. While the FTM feature allows full time manual focus without flipping a switch, the gotcha is it only works when the camera is powered up with the shutter button half-pressed. The focus ring is thin and tricky to locate by feel.ZOOM: The ribbed zoom ring is large, grippy and smooth in rotation. During zoom operation, a small nested barrel extends from the main barrel at 10mm and 18mm, and is fully retracted at 14mm. The 10-18 range is only 1.8X, but short ratios are the norm for ultra wide zooms.IMAGE STABILIZER (IS) gives me two additional stops of hand holdable range at 10mm and three stops at 18mm. But not the four-stops claimed by Canon. Somebody with a more steady hand might squeeze out another stop. Also, IS was very quiet and I was unable to hear it on video with the built-in mics.OPTICAL PERFORMANCE wide open is sharp center frame but slightly soft towards the edges. Stop down to F8 and extremities sharpen up nicely. Sharpness is consistent across most of the zoom range, with only minor degradation towards the long end. There's slight barrel distortion at the wide end but distortion is negligible as you zoom towards 18mm. Chromatic aberration is well controlled with only a pixel or two of magenta fringing along high contrast edges. e.g., tree branches against a bright sky. However, it's easy to remove in DPP, LR or Aperture. In normal light you'll never notice magenta fringing.Photos of sunsets, spotlights and other bright light sources were sharp with well controlled flare (no filter installed). I could invoke flare with the afternoon sun (summer) in the frame and stopping down to F11 or 16. Use of a hood is highly recommended to help protect from stray light, doggie noses and raindrops. Unfortunately, the EW-73C hood is considered an accessory and costs a cringe worthy $29. I expect a price drop and/or inexpensive EW-73C knockoff to be available in the near future.Light falloff (corner darkening) is pronounced: heavy vignetting at 10mm from F4.5 until F11. It lessens as you zoom toward 18 and/or stop down, but is always there. If you shoot JPEGs, Peripheral Illumination Correction can automatically reduce light falloff. RAW shooters may correct with a few clicks in Lightroom or DPP.The dilemma is choosing between this lens and theEF-S 10-22mm f/3.5-4.5 USM. Image quality is a tossup so choice revolves around other features. For example, the USM lens has 4mm of extra reach (2.2X vs 1.8X), faster aperture, better build, internal focus and zoom, distance scale and metal mount. On the other hand, the STM lens is $300 less (!), smaller and lighter, includes IS and the STM drive is better for video.LAST BLURB: Obviously, Canon cut corners to swing this price point but managed to do so with few compromises in optical quality or function. The result is a marvelous lightweight zoom for landscapes, tight quarters or any situation a sweeping view is desired. Anyway you slice it, the EF-S 10-18mm f/4.5-5.6 IS STM is a great performer and value.
